children.title: Moment-Matching Methods
children.top_down_role: Scenario construction targeting selected moments or cross-moments.

knowledge_statements.title: Moment-Matching Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-support scenario construction by weighted moment-residual minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Input target moments \(\mu_k\), moment functions \(\phi_k:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\) for \(k\in K\), scenario count \(N\), admissible support \(Z\), penalties \(w_k>0\), and solver tolerances. Seek nodes \(z_i\in Z\) and probabilities \(p_i\ge0\) satisfying \(\sum_{i=1}^{N}p_i=1\) that reduce the objective
\[
R(z,p)=\sum_{k\in K}w_k\left(\sum_{i=1}^{N}p_i\phi_k(z_i)-\mu_k\right)^2.
\]
Initialize with admissible nodes and simplex weights, apply a constrained nonlinear solver, and terminate according to its declared feasibility and stationarity criteria. Output the candidate distribution \(Q_N=\sum_{i=1}^{N}p_i\delta_{z_i}\), its moment-residual vector, and the attained value \(R(z,p)\). Global minimality may be asserted only when independently certified by the chosen solver or problem structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose scenario locations and probabilities by applying a constrained solver to a weighted moment-discrepancy objective, then report the candidate distribution and its attained residuals without claiming an uncertified global minimum.
assumptions_latex: Every target moment \(\mu_k\) is finite.
The admissible support set \(Z\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) is specified.
At least one feasible probability vector exists.
The solver's feasibility and stationarity tolerances are specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q_N=\sum_{i=1}^{N}p_i\delta_{z_i}\) is the returned finite scenario distribution, accompanied by its attained moment residuals; global optimality requires a separate certificate.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: constrained weighted-residual formulation for finite-support moment matching

children.title: Distribution-Fitting Methods
children.top_down_role: Scenario construction targeting broader distributional features.

knowledge_statements.title: Distribution-Fitting Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parametric fitting followed by finite-support discretization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Input observations \(\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_M\), a parametric family \(\{P_\theta:\theta\in\Theta\}\), a fitting loss \(L_M\), an admissible scenario support \(Z\), a scenario count \(N\), a discrepancy \(D\), and optimization tolerances. First compute a declared exact or approximate solution \(\widehat\theta\in\Theta\) of
\[
\inf_{\theta\in\Theta}L_M(\theta).
\]
Then compute a declared exact or approximate solution with \(z_i\in Z\), \(p_i\ge0\), and \(\sum_{i=1}^{N}p_i=1\) for
\[
\inf_{z,p}D\left(P_{\widehat\theta},\sum_{i=1}^{N}p_i\delta_{z_i}\right).
\]
Output the fitted law \(P_{\widehat\theta}\), the finite scenario law \(Q_N=\sum_{i=1}^{N}p_i\delta_{z_i}\), the attained loss and discrepancy values, and the declared termination tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fit a parametric distribution to the observations, then approximate that fitted law with weighted scenarios drawn from a specified admissible support, reporting whether each optimization was solved exactly or approximately.
assumptions_latex: The loss \(L_M\) is defined on \(\Theta\).
The discrepancy \(D\) is defined for the fitted and discrete laws.
The admissible support \(Z\) is specified.
Each optimization uses a declared exact-solution or approximate-solution rule.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q_N=\sum_{i=1}^{N}p_i\delta_{z_i}\) is the selected exact or tolerance-qualified finite approximation of \(P_{\widehat\theta}\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: fit-then-discretize construction with explicit approximate-solution rules

children.title: Moment Selection Regimes
children.top_down_role: Choices of marginal, joint, tail, or temporal moments used as fitting targets.

knowledge_statements.title: Moment Selection Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Admissibility and dimension conditions for exact regular moment matching.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For support nodes \(z_i\in\mathbb R^d\), positive simplex weights \(p_i\), and selected scalar moment functions \(\{\phi_k:k\in K\}\), define
\[
F_k(z,p)=\sum_{i=1}^{N}p_i\phi_k(z_i)-\mu_k.
\]
A regular exact moment-selection regime requires: every \(\mu_k\) is finite; each \(\phi_k\) is differentiable near the candidate support; \(F(z,p)=0\); and the Jacobian of \(F\) has row rank \(|K|\). Since \(N\) free nodes and simplex weights provide at most \(Nd+N-1\) scalar degrees of freedom, regular exact matching necessarily satisfies
\[
|K|\le Nd+N-1.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Selected moments must exist and be locally independent. Regular exact matching cannot impose more scalar moment equations than the scenario nodes and simplex weights have degrees of freedom.
assumptions_latex: All scenario weights at the candidate solution are positive.
The support nodes vary freely in an open subset of \(\mathbb R^d\).
Moment equations are scalar and differentiable near the candidate solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Regular exact matching implies \(\operatorname{rank}DF=|K|\le Nd+N-1\).

notation.meaning: index set of selected scalar moments

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: dimension counting and full-row-rank regularity for nonlinear moment equations
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The full-row-rank condition and parameter-count bound are mathematically consistent under the stated interior-support assumptions, but no source supports this particular definition of a regular moment-selection regime.

children.title: Fit-Complexity Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Relationships among distributional fidelity, scenario count, plus numerical tractability.

knowledge_statements.title: Fit-Complexity Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotone approximation improvement versus finite-scenario model growth.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal Q_N\) be the probability measures supported on at most \(N\) points, let \(P\) be the target law, and define
\[
e_N=\inf_{Q\in\mathcal Q_N}D(P,Q).
\]
Because \(\mathcal Q_N\subseteq\mathcal Q_{N+1}\), the best achievable fit satisfies \(e_{N+1}\le e_N\). If each scenario contributes \(d_y\) recourse variables, \(m_y\) recourse constraints, and at most \(z_y\) local nonzeros to a two-stage extensive form, increasing from \(N\) to \(N+1\) adds \(d_y\) variables, \(m_y\) constraints, and at most \(z_y\) local nonzeros, excluding fixed first-stage data. Thus richer finite supports weakly improve optimal fit while enlarging the deterministic equivalent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Allowing more scenarios cannot worsen the best distributional fit, but each added scenario enlarges the extensive form by another recourse block.
assumptions_latex: The discrepancy \(D(P,Q)\) is defined for every \(Q\in\mathcal Q_N\).
Scenario-local recourse blocks have fixed dimensions \(d_y,m_y,z_y\).
The deterministic equivalent represents every retained scenario explicitly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(e_{N+1}\le e_N\), while explicit recourse formulation size grows linearly with \(N\) under fixed block dimensions.

notation.meaning: laws with at most N support points

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: nested approximation classes and additive scenario-block accounting
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Nested support classes justify monotonic best-fit error, and fixed scenario blocks justify linear extensive-form growth, but both tradeoff claims lack an inspectable citation.

children.title: Distribution Quantization
children.top_down_role: Finite-support approximation through representative locations.

knowledge_statements.title: Distribution Quantization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-support quantization of a probability distribution on Euclidean space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\) be a Borel probability measure on \(\mathbb{R}^d\), let \(p\geq 1\), and let \(\Gamma=\{z_1,\ldots,z_m\}\subset\mathbb{R}^d\) with \(m\leq N\). Choose a measurable nearest-neighbor map \(q_\Gamma(x)\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{z\in\Gamma}\|x-z\|\), using a fixed tie-breaking rule. The \(N\)-point quantization of \(P\) induced by \(\Gamma\) is the discrete measure \[Q_\Gamma=(q_\Gamma)_\#P=\sum_{j=1}^m P\bigl(q_\Gamma^{-1}(\{z_j\})\bigr)\,\delta_{z_j}.\] Thus each scenario is a codepoint and its probability is the mass of its quantization cell.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Distribution quantization replaces a probability law by at most N representative scenarios, assigning each scenario the probability mass of its nearest-neighbor cell.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) is a Borel probability measure on \(\mathbb{R}^d\).
\(\Gamma\) is nonempty and satisfies \(|\Gamma|\leq N\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q_\Gamma\) is a probability measure supported on at most \(N\) points.

notation.meaning: pushforward of P through the quantizer

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard finite-codebook nearest-neighbor quantization definition

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the leaf and is mathematically standard, but it has no inspectable citation. The introduced parameter p is unused.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Asymptotic Quantization Error
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Asymptotic leading constant for optimal finite-support approximation measured by the order-r quantization distance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(P\) be a probability measure on \(\mathbb{R}^m\) satisfying \(P\in\mathcal{P}_{r+\delta}(\mathbb{R}^m)\) for some \(\delta>0\). If \(P_a\) is the absolutely continuous part of \(P\) and \(\lambda^m\) is Lebesgue measure, then
\[
\lim_{n\to\infty} n^{1/m}\,\mathrm{d}_{r;n}(P)
=\left\|\frac{dP_a}{d\lambda^m}\right\|_{m/(m+r)}^{1/r}
\inf_{k\ge 1} k^{1/m}\,\mathrm{d}_{r;k}\!\left(U([0,1]^m)\right),
\]
and
\[
\inf_{k\ge 1} k^{1/m}\,\mathrm{d}_{r;k}\!\left(U([0,1]^m)\right)>0.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a probability measure with a finite moment of order r+delta, the optimal n-point quantization error scaled by n^(1/m) converges to a density-dependent factor times a strictly positive constant determined by the uniform distribution on the unit cube.
assumptions_latex: P\text{ is a probability measure on }\mathbb{R}^m
P\in\mathcal{P}_{r+\delta}(\mathbb{R}^m)\text{ for some }\delta>0
P_a\text{ is the absolutely continuous part of }P\text{ with respect to }\lambda^m
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \lim_{n\to\infty}n^{1/m}\mathrm{d}_{r;n}(P)=\left\|\frac{dP_a}{d\lambda^m}\right\|_{m/(m+r)}^{1/r}\inf_{k\ge1}k^{1/m}\mathrm{d}_{r;k}(U([0,1]^m)),\qquad \inf_{k\ge1}k^{1/m}\mathrm{d}_{r;k}(U([0,1]^m))>0

children.title: Optimal Discretization
children.top_down_role: Finite approximations selected according to an explicit approximation criterion.

knowledge_statements.title: Optimal Discretization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimal fixed-cardinality discretization under an order-p quantization objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\) be a Borel probability measure on \(\mathbb{R}^d\) satisfying \(\int\|x\|^pP(dx)<\infty\), where \(p\geq1\). For a codebook \(\Gamma\subset\mathbb{R}^d\), define \(D_p(P,\Gamma)=\int\min_{z\in\Gamma}\|x-z\|^pP(dx)\). A codebook \(\Gamma_N^*\) is an optimal \(N\)-point discretization when \[|\Gamma_N^*|\leq N,\qquad D_p(P,\Gamma_N^*)=\inf_{1\leq|\Gamma|\leq N}D_p(P,\Gamma).\] Its associated discrete law is \(Q_N^*=(q_{\Gamma_N^*})_\#P\), with cell probabilities induced by the nearest-neighbor quantizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An optimal N-point discretization is a codebook of at most N scenarios minimizing expected pth-power distance from the random outcome to its nearest scenario.
assumptions_latex: \(p\geq1\) and \(\int\|x\|^pP(dx)<\infty\).
The displayed infimum is attained by \(\Gamma_N^*\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D_p(P,\Gamma_N^*)=\inf_{1\leq|\Gamma|\leq N}D_p(P,\Gamma)\).

notation.meaning: optimal codebook with at most N points
discrete law induced by the optimal codebook

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The fixed-cardinality distortion formulation fits Optimal Discretization, but no source supports the formulation or its attainment conditions.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Almost-Sure Stationarity of Stochastic Optimal Discretization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Method-specific convergence guarantee for the stochastic approximation discretization algorithm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let Z(k) be generated by the stochastic optimal-discretization algorithm. Suppose a_k\geq0, \sum_k a_k=\infty, and \sum_k a_k^2<\infty, and suppose all hypotheses of the associated noisy-gradient convergence proposition hold. Then D(Z(k)) converges almost surely and \nabla_ZD(Z(k))\to0 almost surely. In particular, if D has a unique local minimizer Z^*, then Z(k)\to Z^* almost surely.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the stated step-size conditions and all assumptions of the associated noisy-gradient proposition, the discretization objective converges almost surely and its gradient tends to zero. If the objective has a unique local minimizer, the support configurations converge almost surely to that minimizer.
assumptions_latex: Z(k)\text{ is generated by the stochastic optimal-discretization algorithm}.
a_k\geq0,\quad \sum_k a_k=\infty,\quad \sum_k a_k^2<\infty.
\text{All assumptions of Proposition 4.16 hold}.
D\text{ has a unique local minimizer }Z^*\text{ for the final iterate-convergence conclusion}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: D(Z(k))\text{ converges a.s.},\qquad \nabla_ZD(Z(k))\to0\text{ a.s.; if }D\text{ has a unique local minimizer }Z^*,\text{ then }Z(k)\to Z^*\text{ a.s.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Stochastic Approximation for Optimal Discretization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sample-driven construction of an s-point discrete approximation under a distance-power distortion criterion; the extract does not specify how nearest-point ties are resolved.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Draw n\gg s samples from P, cluster them into s groups, and initialize Z(0) with the cluster medians. Choose a_k>0 with \sum_{k=0}^{\infty}a_k=\infty and \sum_{k=0}^{\infty}a_k^2<\infty. At iteration k, draw an independent sample \xi(k), choose i\in\arg\min_{1\leq\ell\leq s}d(\xi(k),z^{(\ell)}(k)), and update z^{(i)}(k+1)=z^{(i)}(k)-a_k r\,d(\xi(k),z^{(i)}(k))^{r-1}\nabla_zd(\xi(k),z^{(i)}(k)), leaving the other support points unchanged. Stop after a prescribed number of iterations or when the relative change in Z is below \epsilon. From a fresh sample, estimate nearest-support probabilities p_i and return \widetilde P=\sum_{i=1}^s p_i\delta_{z^{(i)}}.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Initialize s representatives by clustering a large sample. For each new independent observation, update a nearest representative by the displayed stochastic gradient step and leave the others fixed. After stopping, estimate the support probabilities with a fresh sample and form the resulting discrete distribution.
assumptions_latex: n\gg s.
a_k>0,\quad \sum_{k=0}^{\infty}a_k=\infty,\quad \sum_{k=0}^{\infty}a_k^2<\infty.
\xi(k)\text{ is a new independent sample from }P\text{ at iteration }k.
\nabla_zd(\xi,z)\text{ exists at each selected update point}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \widetilde P=\sum_{i=1}^{s}p_i\delta_{z^{(i)}},\qquad p_i=\frac1n\#\left\{\ell:d(\xi(\ell),z^{(i)})=\min_jd(\xi(\ell),z^{(j)})\right\}.

children.title: Quantization Distortion Criteria
children.top_down_role: Distance-based criteria used to compare finite-support approximations.

knowledge_statements.title: Quantization Distortion Criteria
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Expected nearest-codepoint loss for a general pointwise distortion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\) be a probability measure on a measurable space \(\mathcal X\), let \(\Gamma\subset\mathcal Z\) be a nonempty finite codebook, and let \(c:\mathcal X\times\mathcal Z\to[0,\infty]\) be measurable. The distortion criterion of \(\Gamma\) is \[D_c(P,\Gamma)=\int_{\mathcal X}\min_{z\in\Gamma}c(x,z)\,P(dx).\] For \(\mathcal X=\mathcal Z=\mathbb R^d\) and \(c(x,z)=\|x-z\|^p\), this becomes the order-\(p\) criterion \(D_p(P,\Gamma)=\mathbb E[\min_{z\in\Gamma}\|X-z\|^p]\). A normalized error may be reported as \(D_p(P,\Gamma)^{1/p}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A quantization distortion criterion averages the smallest loss incurred by representing each outcome with one codepoint; pth-power metric loss is the standard case.
assumptions_latex: \(c\) is nonnegative and jointly measurable.
\(\Gamma\) is finite and nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D_c(P,\Gamma)\) is the expected pointwise loss of the best representative in \(\Gamma\).

notation.meaning: loss from representing outcome x by codepoint z

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard expected-distortion criterion for vector quantization

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The criterion fits the leaf, but no citation is supplied, and X in the order-p expectation is not explicitly introduced as having law P.

children.title: Discretization Cardinality Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Approximation-quality changes associated with the number of support points.

knowledge_statements.title: Discretization Cardinality Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotonic approximation benefit and exactness threshold as scenario cardinality increases.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(p\geq1\) and a probability measure \(P\) on \(\mathbb R^d\) with finite \(p\)-th moment, define \[e_{N,p}(P)=\inf_{1\leq|\Gamma|\leq N}\left(\int\min_{z\in\Gamma}\|x-z\|^pP(dx)\right)^{1/p}.\] Then \(e_{N+1,p}(P)\leq e_{N,p}(P)\) for every \(N\), and \(e_{N,p}(P)\to0\) as \(N\to\infty\). If \(P\) has finite support of cardinality \(M\), then \(e_{N,p}(P)=0\) for every \(N\geq M\). Thus additional scenarios cannot worsen optimal distortion, although they enlarge the resulting discrete model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Optimal distortion decreases with the number of scenarios, converges to zero under a finite moment, and vanishes once all atoms of a finite law fit.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) is a Borel probability measure on \(\mathbb R^d\).
\(p\geq1\) and \(\int\|x\|^pP(dx)<\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(e_{N+1,p}(P)\leq e_{N,p}(P)\) and \(\lim_{N\to\infty}e_{N,p}(P)=0\).

notation.meaning: minimum order-p distortion norm using at most N points
support cardinality when P is finitely supported

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard density and monotonicity properties of finite quantizers

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The monotonicity, convergence, and finite-support claims are plausible and fit the tradeoff leaf, but the nontrivial convergence assertion lacks an inspectable authoritative source.

knowledge_statements.title: Stagewise Tree Construction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recursive conditional clustering of weighted sample paths into a finite scenario tree.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input weighted paths \((\xi_{1:T}^i,w_i)_{i=1}^S\), a horizon \(T\), and branching limits \((b_t)_{t=1}^T\). Initialize a root containing all indices and probability one. At every stage-\(t\) node \(n\) with index set \(I_n\), partition \(I_n\) into at most \(b_{t+1}\) clusters using the conditional observations \(\xi_{t+1}^i\). Create one child per nonempty cluster \(C\), assign representative \(\bar\xi_C\), and set \(p(C\mid n)=\sum_{i\in C}w_i/\sum_{i\in I_n}w_i\). Recurse until stage \(T\); output the nodes, representatives, arcs, and conditional probabilities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stagewise construction repeatedly clusters next-stage observations within each current node and assigns child probabilities from the conditional sample weights.
assumptions_latex: \(w_i\geq0\) and \(\sum_{i=1}^S w_i=1\).
Every processed node has positive total sample weight.
\(b_t\) are positive integers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is a rooted depth-\(T\) tree whose outgoing probabilities sum to one at every nonterminal positive-probability node.

notation.meaning: sample-path indices assigned to node n
conditional probability of child cluster C

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The content kind and local topic fit, but the cited general scenario-tree section does not yet establish the specific recursive conditional-clustering algorithm or its indexing convention.

knowledge_statements.title: Path-Based Tree Construction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Whole-path selection followed by prefix sharing and probability accumulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input weighted trajectories \((\xi_{1:T}^i,w_i)_{i=1}^S\), a path metric \(d_{\mathrm{path}}\), and a budget \(K\). Select representative trajectories \((z_{1:T}^k)_{k=1}^K\), and assign each input trajectory to \(a(i)\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{1\leq k\leq K}d_{\mathrm{path}}(\xi_{1:T}^i,z_{1:T}^k)\). Form a prefix trie from the selected trajectories, merging exactly equal prefixes. Give leaf \(k\) mass \(\pi_k=\sum_{i:a(i)=k}w_i\); give every internal node the sum of descendant leaf masses and every arc its child-to-parent mass ratio. Output the resulting tree, node labels, and probabilities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Path-based construction selects representative complete trajectories, joins their shared prefixes, and obtains node and transition probabilities by accumulating assigned path weights.
assumptions_latex: \(w_i\geq0\) and \(\sum_iw_i=1\).
\(1\leq K\leq S\).
A deterministic rule resolves assignment ties.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output preserves the selected complete paths and defines consistent probabilities on their shared-prefix tree.

notation.meaning: representative path assigned to sample i

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits Path-Based Tree Construction, but the cited general section does not confirm representative-path selection. The assumptions also do not exclude zero-mass representative leaves, for which a child-to-parent mass ratio may be undefined.

children.title: Tree Recombination
children.top_down_role: Merging compatible tree histories into shared successor structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Tree Recombination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lossless merging of stage nodes having identical continuation-relevant state and transition kernels.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a finite scenario tree have node masses \(p_n\), stage labels, continuation states \(s_n\), and outgoing labeled transition kernels \(K_n\). At each stage, define \(n\sim m\) only when \(s_n=s_m\), their feasible continuation decisions coincide, and \(K_n=K_m\) after identifying equivalent successors. Replace each equivalence class \(C\) by one node with mass \(p_C=\sum_{n\in C}p_n\); redirect incoming arcs to \(C\), retain the common outgoing kernel, and recursively merge equivalent successors. Stop when no class contains distinct nodes. The resulting directed acyclic graph is a recombining scenario structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Tree recombination merges same-stage nodes only when their continuation state, feasible decisions, and future transition law agree, while adding their incoming probabilities.
assumptions_latex: The original scenario tree is finite.
Equivalence is restricted to nodes at the same stage.
Equivalent nodes have identical continuation kernels after successor identification.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Recombination preserves total probability and the conditional continuation model associated with every merged class.

notation.meaning: outgoing labeled transition kernel at node n

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits Tree Recombination, but the exact equivalence conditions and lossless preservation conclusion are not confirmed by the cited general scenario-tree locator.

children.title: State Aggregation
children.top_down_role: Combining similar state descriptions into coarser representatives.

knowledge_statements.title: State Aggregation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Probability-preserving replacement of same-stage states by representative aggregate states.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a fixed stage, let nodes \(n\) have states \(s_n\in\mathbb R^d\) and masses \(p_n\). Choose a partition \(\mathcal C\) of the nodes. For each class \(C\in\mathcal C\) with \(p_C=\sum_{n\in C}p_n>0\), create an aggregate node with representative \[\bar s_C=\frac{1}{p_C}\sum_{n\in C}p_ns_n.\] Redirect all incoming mass to the aggregate node. Its outgoing transition probabilities and stage costs are the corresponding \(p_n/p_C\)-weighted mixtures, unless a separately specified projection is used. Repeat only within stages and output the aggregated scenario structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: State aggregation groups same-stage nodes, sums their probabilities, and replaces their states, costs, and transitions by probability-weighted representatives or mixtures.
assumptions_latex: All aggregated nodes belong to the same stage.
\(p_n\geq0\) and each retained class has \(p_C>0\).
States lie in a vector space where weighted averages are defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each aggregate class preserves its total incoming probability, with representative state \(\bar s_C\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits State Aggregation, but mixing outgoing kernels and stage costs requires compatible successor and action spaces that are not specified, and the cited source has not been inspected for this convention.

children.title: History-Compatibility Criteria
children.top_down_role: Information-based criteria governing permissible history merging.

knowledge_statements.title: History-Compatibility Criteria
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Criterion for merging histories without changing admissible continuation policies or conditional dynamics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(h_t\) and \(h_t'\) be histories at stage \(t\), and let \(\phi_t\) be a proposed aggregation map. The pair is history-compatible when \(\phi_t(h_t)=\phi_t(h_t')\) implies all three conditions: \(A_t(h_t)=A_t(h_t')\); the current cost satisfies \(c_t(h_t,a)=c_t(h_t',a)\) for every common feasible action \(a\); and the conditional law of the next aggregate state agrees, \[\mathcal L\bigl(\phi_{t+1}(H_{t+1})\mid h_t,a\bigr)=\mathcal L\bigl(\phi_{t+1}(H_{t+1})\mid h_t',a\bigr).\] Compatibility is required at every nonterminal stage.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two histories may share an aggregate node only if they permit identical actions, incur identical current costs, and induce identical laws for the next aggregate state.
assumptions_latex: Conditional laws are defined for every feasible history-action pair.
The aggregation maps \(\phi_t\) are measurable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The aggregate state retains all information needed to specify feasible continuation decisions, costs, and aggregate transition laws.

notation.meaning: feasible action set after history h_t

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition role fits the leaf, but the exact history-sufficiency criterion is not confirmed by the cited aggregation section. As written, the implication should be quantified over every pair of histories mapped to the same aggregate state.

children.title: Aggregation-Loss Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Decision-relevant distinctions lost through recombination or state compression.

knowledge_statements.title: Aggregation-Loss Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unbounded value loss when aggregation erases decision-relevant observed history.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For any \(M>0\), let an observed state \(B\) be uniform on \(\{0,1\}\), let the action satisfy \(a\in\{0,1\}\), and define cost \(c(B,a)=M\mathbf 1_{\{a\neq B\}}\). With separate post-observation nodes, the policy \(a=B\) has expected cost zero. If aggregation merges the histories \(B=0\) and \(B=1\) and requires one common action, every deterministic common action has expected cost \(M/2\); randomized common actions have the same minimum. Hence probability-preserving aggregation alone gives no uniform value-loss bound when history compatibility is removed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Merging histories that reveal different decision-relevant states can cause arbitrarily large loss, even if their total probability is preserved exactly.
assumptions_latex: \(B\) is observed before the action is selected.
Aggregation forces the same action at both observed histories.
\(M>0\) is arbitrary.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The aggregation gap equals \(M/2\) and is therefore unbounded over \(M\).

children.title: Probability Improvement
children.top_down_role: Refinement of branch or leaf probability assignments.

knowledge_statements.title: Probability Improvement
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Probability refinement for fixed scenario paths under a differentiable discrepancy objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix scenario paths \(z^1,\ldots,z^K\) and a differentiable discrepancy \(F(\pi;z)\) between their discrete law and a target law. Initialize \(\pi^0\in\Delta_K\). At iteration \(r\), choose a step \(\alpha_r>0\) and compute \[\pi^{r+1}=\operatorname{Proj}_{\Delta_K}\bigl(\pi^r-\alpha_r\nabla_\pi F(\pi^r;z)\bigr),\qquad \Delta_K=\{\pi\in\mathbb R_+^K:\mathbf1^\top\pi=1\}.\] Accept the update only if it decreases \(F\), reducing \(\alpha_r\) otherwise. Stop when the accepted decrease or projected-gradient residual is at most a prescribed tolerance; output the fixed paths with probabilities \(\pi^{r+1}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With paths fixed, probability improvement minimizes a distributional discrepancy by projected updates on the probability simplex and stops at small decrease or residual.
assumptions_latex: \(F(\cdot;z)\) is differentiable on a neighborhood of \(\Delta_K\).
The projection uses the Euclidean norm.
Line search returns a decreasing feasible update or declares stationarity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every accepted iterate lies in \(\Delta_K\) and does not increase \(F\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: projected-gradient refinement on a probability simplex

children.title: Path Improvement
children.top_down_role: Refinement of scenario trajectories or their representative values.

knowledge_statements.title: Path Improvement
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasible descent refinement of scenario-path locations with probabilities held fixed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix probabilities \(\pi\in\Delta_K\), initialize paths \(z^0=(z^{1,0},\ldots,z^{K,0})\) in a closed feasible set \(\mathcal Z\) encoding the horizon and required shared prefixes, and choose a differentiable discrepancy \(F(\pi;z)\). At iteration \(r\), compute \[z^{r+1}=\operatorname{Proj}_{\mathcal Z}\bigl(z^r-\eta_r\nabla_zF(\pi;z^r)\bigr).\] Use backtracking to choose \(\eta_r>0\) so that the accepted update decreases \(F\). Rebuild node labels from the updated paths without changing \(\pi\). Stop when the accepted decrease or projected-gradient residual is below tolerance; output \(z^{r+1}\) and \(\pi\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With probabilities fixed, path improvement moves scenario trajectories by projected descent while preserving horizon, prefix, and other structural constraints.
assumptions_latex: \(F(\pi;\cdot)\) is differentiable near \(\mathcal Z\).
Projection onto \(\mathcal Z\) is defined for each trial update.
Backtracking accepts only discrepancy-decreasing updates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every accepted path collection is feasible and satisfies \(F(\pi;z^{r+1})\leq F(\pi;z^r)\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: projected descent for fixed-weight representative paths

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The projected-descent algorithm fits Path Improvement and is internally coherent, but no source supports this particular scenario-tree refinement method or its structural projection assumptions.

children.title: Probability-Path Coordination
children.top_down_role: Joint adjustment of path locations plus associated probability mass.

knowledge_statements.title: Probability-Path Coordination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Alternating coordination of probabilities and representative paths in a finite scenario tree.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a finite rooted tree with child probabilities \(p_{vc}\), representative states \(z_{vc}\), and a discrepancy functional \(D(p,z)\), initialize a feasible pair \((p^0,z^0)\). At iteration \(k\), compute \(p^{k+1}\) by approximately minimizing \(D(p,z^k)\) subject to \(p_{vc}\ge 0\) and \(\sum_{c\in C(v)}p_{vc}=1\). Then compute \(z^{k+1}\) by approximately minimizing \(D(p^{k+1},z)\) subject to the tree's stagewise information and nonanticipativity constraints. Accept both updates only if \(D(p^{k+1},z^{k+1})\le D(p^k,z^k)\); otherwise damp or reject the offending update. Output the last accepted finite-distribution approximation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Alternately improve branch probabilities and representative paths while preserving probability normalization, information structure, and nonincreasing approximation discrepancy.
assumptions_latex: \(D(p,z)\) is finite on at least one feasible probability-path pair.
Each probability and path subproblem admits an accepted update or a null update.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D(p^{k+1},z^{k+1})\le D(p^k,z^k)\) for every accepted coordinated iteration.

notation.meaning: conditional probability of child c given node v
representative state attached to the child branch

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the terminal container, but no evidence supports the alternating subproblems, joint acceptance rule, or damping/rejection convention. These choices are algorithm-specific rather than consequences of the stated assumptions.

children.title: Improvement Stopping Criteria
children.top_down_role: Quality thresholds used to terminate scenario-tree refinement.

knowledge_statements.title: Improvement Stopping Criteria
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Termination test for coupled probability and path refinement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For accepted iterates \((p^k,z^k)\), define the probability change \(r_p^k=\max_{v,c}|p_{vc}^{k+1}-p_{vc}^k|\), the path change \(r_z^k=\max_{v,c}\|z_{vc}^{k+1}-z_{vc}^k\|\), and, when certified expectation bounds are available, the bound gap \(g^k=U^k-L^k\). Stop when \(r_p^k\le\varepsilon_p\), \(r_z^k\le\varepsilon_z\), and either no certified gap is maintained or \(g^k\le\varepsilon_g\). Also stop with a resource-limit status if a prescribed iteration, node, or time budget is exhausted; only the gap test certifies expectation accuracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stop when probability changes, path changes, and any certified bound gap meet their tolerances; resource exhaustion stops computation without an accuracy certificate.
assumptions_latex: \(\varepsilon_p,\varepsilon_z,\varepsilon_g\ge 0\).
Whenever \(g^k\) is used, \(L^k\le V\le U^k\) are valid bounds on the target value \(V\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r_p^k\le\varepsilon_p\), \(r_z^k\le\varepsilon_z\), and \(g^k\le\varepsilon_g\) imply certified termination with respect to the stated residuals and gap.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits the stopping-criteria container, but the particular residuals, conjunction of tests, optional-gap convention, and resource-limit behavior require an algorithm-specific source.

knowledge_statements.title: Jensen Lower-Bound Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional Jensen bounds generated by finite measurable partitions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\xi\) be an integrable random vector taking values in a convex set \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^d\), and let \(f:C\to\mathbb R\) be convex with \(f(\xi)\) integrable. For any finite measurable partition \(\{A_i\}_{i=1}^m\) with \(p_i=\mathbb P(A_i)>0\), set \(\mu_i=\mathbb E[\xi\mid A_i]\). Conditional Jensen inequalities give
\[
\sum_{i=1}^m p_i f(\mu_i)\le \mathbb E[f(\xi)].
\]
The one-cell partition yields \(f(\mathbb E[\xi])\le\mathbb E[f(\xi)]\). Thus the conditional means and cell probabilities define a finite-distribution lower approximation for every such partition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Evaluating a convex integrand at conditional cell means and weighting by cell probabilities gives a lower bound on its expectation.
assumptions_latex: \(\xi\in L^1(\Omega;\mathbb R^d)\) and \(\xi\in C\) almost surely.
\(f\) is convex on \(C\) and \(f(\xi)\in L^1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_{i=1}^m p_i f(\mu_i)\le \mathbb E[f(\xi)]\).

notation.meaning: cell of a finite measurable partition
conditional mean of the random vector on cell i

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Jensen's inequality for probability measures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Integral Jensen inequality for a convex real-valued function on Euclidean space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(F:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}\) is convex and \(\mu\) is a probability measure on \(\mathbb{R}^d\), with the barycenter and displayed expectation well defined, then \[F\!\left(\int_{\mathbb{R}^d}\theta\,d\mu(\theta)\right)\le \int_{\mathbb{R}^d}F(\theta)\,d\mu(\theta).\]

knowledge_statements.title: Edmundson–Madansky Upper-Bound Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex upper bounds obtained from vertex-valued distributions preserving the random vector's mean representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(P=\operatorname{conv}\{v_1,\ldots,v_s\}\subseteq\mathbb R^d\), let \(\xi\in P\) almost surely, and let \(f:P\to\mathbb R\) be convex and integrable at the required arguments. Suppose measurable functions \(\lambda_j:P\to[0,1]\) satisfy \(\sum_{j=1}^s\lambda_j(x)=1\) and \(x=\sum_{j=1}^s\lambda_j(x)v_j\). Convexity implies
\[
\mathbb E[f(\xi)]\le\sum_{j=1}^s\mathbb E[\lambda_j(\xi)]f(v_j).
\]
Hence replacing \(\xi\) by the vertex-valued distribution assigning probability \(\mathbb E[\lambda_j(\xi)]\) to \(v_j\) gives an Edmundson–Madansky upper bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex integrand's expectation is bounded above by a vertex distribution whose barycentric weights reproduce each realization of the random vector.
assumptions_latex: \(\xi\) is supported on the compact polytope \(P\).
\(f\) is convex on \(P\), and all displayed expectations are finite.
The functions \(\lambda_j\) form a measurable convex decomposition of every point in \(P\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[f(\xi)]\le\sum_{j=1}^s\mathbb E[\lambda_j(\xi)]f(v_j)\).

barycentric coordinate function for vertex j

knowledge_statements.title: Piecewise-Linear Expectation Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Partitionwise Jensen lower bounds and piecewise-linear upper-majorant bounds for convex expectations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\xi\) be an integrable random vector, and let \(\{A_i\}_{i=1}^m\) be a finite measurable partition of its probability space with \(p_i=\mathbb P(A_i)>0\) and \(\mu_i=\mathbb E[\xi\mid A_i]\). Let \(f\) be convex on a convex set containing the support of \(\xi\). For each \(i\), let \(u_i\) be an integrable convex piecewise-linear function satisfying \(f(x)\le u_i(x)\) for every \(x\) in the conditional support of \(\xi\) on \(A_i\). Then
\[
L_{\mathcal P}=\sum_{i=1}^m p_i f(\mu_i)\le \mathbb E[f(\xi)]\le \sum_{i=1}^m p_i\mathbb E[u_i(\xi)\mid A_i]=U_{\mathcal P}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A measurable partition gives a conditional-Jensen lower sum, while integrable piecewise-linear majorants on its cells give an upper sum for the same convex expectation.
assumptions_latex: \(\xi\) and \(f(\xi)\) are integrable.
\(f\) is convex on a convex set containing the support of \(\xi\).
Each \(u_i(\xi)\mathbf 1_{A_i}\) is integrable and \(u_i\) majorizes \(f\) on the conditional support associated with \(A_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_{\mathcal P}\le\mathbb E[f(\xi)]\le U_{\mathcal P}\).

notation.meaning: finite measurable partition of the probability space

children.title: Partition-Bound Families
children.top_down_role: Expectation bounds organized through partitions of uncertainty or recourse structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Partition-Bound Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotone expectation bounds induced by nested measurable partitions and compatible local upper majorants.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f\) and \(\xi\) satisfy the convexity and integrability hypotheses, and let the finite measurable partition \(\mathcal P'\) refine \(\mathcal P\). Conditional-Jensen lower bounds satisfy
\[
L_{\mathcal P}\le L_{\mathcal P'}\le\mathbb E[f(\xi)].
\]
Suppose additionally that each cell \(A\in\mathcal P\) has an integrable majorant \(u_A\) of \(f\), and each child \(B\in\mathcal P'\) contained in \(A\) has an integrable majorant \(u_B\) satisfying \(f(x)\le u_B(x)\le u_A(x)\) on the conditional support associated with \(B\). Defining
\[
U_{\mathcal P}=\sum_{A\in\mathcal P}\mathbb E[u_A(\xi)\mathbf 1_A],\qquad U_{\mathcal P'}=\sum_{B\in\mathcal P'}\mathbb E[u_B(\xi)\mathbf 1_B],
\]
gives
\[
\mathbb E[f(\xi)]\le U_{\mathcal P'}\le U_{\mathcal P}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partition refinement raises conditional-Jensen lower bounds; it lowers upper bounds when every refined-cell majorant is dominated by the corresponding parent-cell majorant.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is convex, and all displayed random variables are integrable.
\(\mathcal P'\) is a finite measurable refinement of \(\mathcal P\).
For every child cell \(B\subseteq A\), the local majorants satisfy \(f\le u_B\le u_A\) on the conditional support associated with \(B\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_{\mathcal P}\le L_{\mathcal P'}\le\mathbb E[f(\xi)]\le U_{\mathcal P'}\le U_{\mathcal P}\).

notation.meaning: the first measurable partition refines the second
lower and upper bounds induced by a partition
integrable local upper majorant associated with cell A

children.title: Separable-Bound Families
children.top_down_role: Expectation bounds exploiting separability across components.

knowledge_statements.title: Separable-Bound Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Componentwise construction of expectation bounds for additively separable integrands.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\xi=(\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_d)\) and suppose \(f(x)=\sum_{j=1}^d f_j(x_j)\), where every \(f_j(\xi_j)\) is integrable. If valid scalar bounds satisfy \(L_j\le\mathbb E[f_j(\xi_j)]\le U_j\), then linearity of expectation gives
\[
\sum_{j=1}^d L_j\le\mathbb E[f(\xi)]\le\sum_{j=1}^d U_j.
\]
No independence among the components is required. When each \(f_j\) is convex, the component bounds may be formed separately by Jensen lower constructions and scalar chord or secant upper constructions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bounds for an additively separable expectation are obtained by summing valid component bounds; dependence among components does not affect validity.
assumptions_latex: Each \(f_j(\xi_j)\) is integrable.
\(L_j\) and \(U_j\) are valid bounds for the corresponding scalar expectation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_{j=1}^dL_j\le\mathbb E[f(\xi)]\le\sum_{j=1}^dU_j\).

children.title: Moment-Bound Families
children.top_down_role: Expectation bounds based on available moment information.

knowledge_statements.title: Moment-Bound Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp expectation bounds over probability laws satisfying prescribed moment information.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(S\subseteq\mathbb R^d\), let \(h_0\equiv1,h_1,\ldots,h_r:S\to\mathbb R\), and prescribe moments \(m_0=1,m_1,\ldots,m_r\). Define
\[
\mathcal M(m)=\left\{P:\ P\text{ is a probability measure on }S,\ \int_S h_k(x)\,dP(x)=m_k\text{ for }k=0,\ldots,r\right\}.
\]
For measurable \(f\) with finite integrals, the moment bounds are
\[
L(m)=\inf_{P\in\mathcal M(m)}\int_S f\,dP,\qquad U(m)=\sup_{P\in\mathcal M(m)}\int_S f\,dP.
\]
Every distribution having the prescribed moments satisfies \(L(m)\le\mathbb E[f(\xi)]\le U(m)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Optimize the expected integrand over all probability laws matching specified moments; the resulting infimum and supremum bound every compatible distribution.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal M(m)\ne\varnothing\).
The integrals defining the moment constraints and objective are well-defined and finite for the laws considered.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L(m)\le\mathbb E_P[f(\xi)]\le U(m)\) for every \(P\in\mathcal M(m)\).

notation.meaning: set of probability laws satisfying prescribed moments
sharp lower and upper moment bounds

children.title: Hybrid Bound Families
children.top_down_role: Certificates combining partition, separability, or moment information.

knowledge_statements.title: Hybrid Bound Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Intersection of independently valid expectation-bound constructions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(V=\mathbb E[f(\xi)]\), and suppose \(K\) bounding constructions, possibly using partitions, separability, moments, or support geometry, produce valid intervals \([L_k,U_k]\) satisfying \(L_k\le V\le U_k\) for \(k=1,\ldots,K\). Their hybrid bound is the interval intersection
\[
L_{\mathrm{hyb}}=\max_{1\le k\le K}L_k,\qquad U_{\mathrm{hyb}}=\min_{1\le k\le K}U_k.
\]
Provided the component bounds concern the same expectation and assumptions, \(L_{\mathrm{hyb}}\le V\le U_{\mathrm{hyb}}\), and the hybrid interval is no wider than any component interval containing it.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Intersect valid bounds derived from partitions, separability, moments, or support geometry by taking the largest lower and smallest upper bound.
assumptions_latex: Every interval \([L_k,U_k]\) validly bounds the same finite value \(V\) under compatible assumptions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\max_kL_k\le V\le\min_kU_k\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Intersecting valid intervals is mathematically correct, and property fits the container, but no citation identifies this construction as the intended Hybrid Bound Families knowledge rather than a generic interval operation.

children.title: Bound Refinement
children.top_down_role: Progressive tightening of deterministic expectation bounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Bound Refinement
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Iterative tightening of certified convex-expectation bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Initialize a finite partition \(\mathcal P_0\) and compute certified bounds \(L_0\le V\le U_0\) for \(V=\mathbb E[f(\xi)]\). At iteration \(k\), assign each cell a nonnegative local gap contribution whose sum is \(U_k-L_k\), select one or more cells with positive contribution, split them measurably, and recompute conditional means and local upper constructions on the refined partition \(\mathcal P_{k+1}\). Retain an update only when
\[
L_k\le L_{k+1}\le V\le U_{k+1}\le U_k.
\]
Stop when \(U_k-L_k\le\varepsilon\) or a resource limit is reached; output \([L_k,U_k]\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly split cells contributing most to the certified gap, recompute bounds, and retain only refinements that tighten the enclosing interval.
assumptions_latex: Initial bounds \(L_0\le V\le U_0\) are valid.
Every refinement preserves the hypotheses of its lower and upper constructions.
\(\varepsilon\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \([L_{k+1},U_{k+1}]\subseteq[L_k,U_k]\) for every retained refinement.

children.title: Expectation Approximation Schemes

knowledge_statements.title: Expectation Approximation Schemes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-sided finite-distribution approximation embedded in stochastic optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider \(V=\inf_{x\in X}\{c(x)+\mathbb E[Q(x,\xi)]\}\). For refinement level \(k\), construct functions \(\underline Q_k\) and \(\overline Q_k\) satisfying \(\mathbb E[\underline Q_k(x,\xi)]\le\mathbb E[Q(x,\xi)]\le\mathbb E[\overline Q_k(x,\xi)]\) for every \(x\in X\). Solve
\[
L_k=\inf_{x\in X}\{c(x)+\mathbb E[\underline Q_k(x,\xi)]\},\qquad
U_k=\inf_{x\in X}\{c(x)+\mathbb E[\overline Q_k(x,\xi)]\}.
\]
Then \(L_k\le V\le U_k\). Refine the finite-distribution approximations until \(U_k-L_k\le\varepsilon\), and output the bounds and an upper-model optimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve lower and upper finite-distribution models of the same stochastic program, refine their expectation approximations, and stop when their optimal-value gap is acceptable.
assumptions_latex: \(X\ne\varnothing\), and all three optimization values are finite.
The expectation surrogates bound the true expected recourse uniformly for every \(x\in X\).
The lower and upper approximate problems are solved to the accuracy included in their reported bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_k\le V\le U_k\), with certified gap \(U_k-L_k\).

notation.meaning: optimal values of the bounding models

children.title: Adaptive Partition Refinement
children.top_down_role: Partition enrichment guided by local approximation quality.

knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive Partition Refinement
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gap-driven subdivision of support cells for convex-expectation bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a partition \(\mathcal P_k\), compute for every cell \(A\in\mathcal P_k\) a certified lower contribution \(\ell_A\), upper contribution \(u_A\), and indicator \(\eta_A=u_A-\ell_A\ge0\). Choose a marked set \(M_k\subseteq\mathcal P_k\) satisfying \(\sum_{A\in M_k}\eta_A\ge\theta\sum_{A\in\mathcal P_k}\eta_A\) for a fixed \(\theta\in(0,1]\). Split every marked cell into measurable positive-probability children, set \(\mathcal P_{k+1}\) to the resulting refinement, and recompute all affected conditional data. Continue until \(\sum_A\eta_A\le\varepsilon\); output the refined partition and its certified bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Mark cells accounting for a fixed fraction of the current bound gap, subdivide them, and repeat until the total certified gap meets tolerance.
assumptions_latex: Each cell contribution satisfies \(\ell_A\le\mathbb E[f(\xi)\mathbf1_A]\le u_A\).
Every marked positive-gap cell admits a measurable positive-probability split.
\(\theta\in(0,1]\) and \(\varepsilon\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_{A\in\mathcal P_k}\ell_A\le\mathbb E[f(\xi)]\le\sum_{A\in\mathcal P_k}u_A\), and termination gives total gap at most \(\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: certified local bound gap on cell A
set of cells marked for refinement
required marked fraction of the total gap

children.title: Refinement Quality Control
children.top_down_role: Assessment of approximation gaps, refinement value, plus termination thresholds.

knowledge_statements.title: Refinement Quality Control
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A computable stopping certificate for adaptive lower–upper expectation approximations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\Xi\to\mathbb R\) be integrable under \(P\), and let partition \(\mathcal P_k\) produce certified numbers \(L_k\) and \(U_k\) satisfying \[L_k\leq \mathbb E_P[f(\xi)]\leq U_k.\] The refinement passes quality control at absolute tolerance \(\varepsilon>0\) when \(U_k-L_k\leq\varepsilon\). Then every \(v_k\in[L_k,U_k]\), including \(v_k=(L_k+U_k)/2\), has error at most \(U_k-L_k\); the midpoint has error at most \((U_k-L_k)/2\). For nested refinements, the additional checks \(L_{k+1}\geq L_k\) and \(U_{k+1}\leq U_k\) certify monotone tightening.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Valid expectation bounds certify refinement quality; their gap supplies a stopping rule and an explicit error bound, while nested bounds should tighten monotonically.
assumptions_latex: \(L_k\) and \(U_k\) are independently certified expectation bounds.
\(\varepsilon>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(U_k-L_k\leq\varepsilon\) certifies absolute enclosure width at most \(\varepsilon\), and the midpoint error is at most \(\varepsilon/2\).

notation.meaning: partition used at refinement iteration k
certified lower and upper expectation bounds

knowledge_statements.title: Forward Scenario Reduction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Greedy forward selection for a finite distribution under a prescribed transport cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input scenarios \(\xi_i\) with masses \(p_i>0\), a nonnegative cost \(c\), and target size \(m\). Initialize \(J_0=\varnothing\). For \(k=0,\ldots,m-1\), choose \[j_{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{j\notin J_k}\sum_{i\notin J_k\cup\{j\}}p_i\min_{\ell\in J_k\cup\{j\}}c(\xi_i,\xi_\ell),\qquad J_{k+1}=J_k\cup\{j_{k+1}\}.\] After \(m\) selections, assign every discarded index to a nearest member of \(J_m\) and add its mass to that representative. Output the retained scenarios and their reallocated masses; ties may be resolved deterministically.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Greedily add the scenario giving the smallest residual assignment cost, then transfer each discarded scenario’s mass to its nearest retained representative.
assumptions_latex: \(c(\xi_i,\xi_j)\geq0\) is finite on the scenario set.
\(1\leq m\leq n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is a probability distribution supported on exactly \(m\) retained scenarios.

notation.meaning: indices retained after k forward selections

knowledge_statements.title: Backward Scenario Reduction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Greedy deletion from a finite distribution under nearest-neighbor transport cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input scenarios \(\xi_i\), masses \(p_i>0\), a nonnegative cost \(c\), and target size \(m\). Initialize \(J_n=\{1,\ldots,n\}\). While \(|J_k|>m\), delete \[i_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{i\in J_k}p_i\min_{j\in J_k\setminus\{i\}}c(\xi_i,\xi_j),\qquad J_{k-1}=J_k\setminus\{i_k\}.\] Assign the deleted scenario’s current mass to a nearest surviving scenario, updating that survivor’s mass before the next deletion. Stop when \(|J_m|=m\), and output the surviving scenarios with their accumulated masses. A deterministic tie rule makes the procedure single-valued.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly delete the scenario whose transfer to its nearest survivor has least cost, reallocating its current mass after every deletion.
assumptions_latex: \(c(\xi_i,\xi_j)\geq0\) is finite on the scenario set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output preserves total probability mass and has support cardinality \(m\).

notation.meaning: current set of surviving scenario indices
current mass attached to scenario i

children.title: Scenario-Tree Pruning
children.top_down_role: Removal of branches or leaves from finite scenario trees.

knowledge_statements.title: Scenario-Tree Pruning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Leaf pruning and probability reallocation that retain a valid finite rooted scenario tree.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T=(V,E)\) be a finite rooted scenario tree with leaf set \(L\) and leaf probabilities \(p_\ell\geq0\) satisfying \(\sum_{\ell\in L}p_\ell=1\). Choose a nonempty retained leaf set \(\widehat L\subseteq L\), let \(\widehat V\) be the union of the root-to-leaf paths ending in \(\widehat L\), and choose a reassignment map \(r:L\to\widehat L\) satisfying \(r(u)=u\) for every \(u\in\widehat L\). Define \[\widehat p_u=\sum_{\ell\in L:r(\ell)=u}p_\ell\qquad(u\in\widehat L).\] On the rooted subtree induced by \(\widehat V\), define each internal-node mass as the sum of its descendant retained-leaf masses and, for every positive-mass parent, define each conditional edge probability as the child mass divided by the parent mass. Remove zero-mass branches. The output is the resulting reduced rooted probability tree.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Retain selected leaves and all their ancestors, transfer every removed leaf's probability to a retained leaf, and recompute internal and conditional probabilities.
assumptions_latex: \(T\) is a finite rooted scenario tree.
\(p_\ell\geq0\) and \(\sum_{\ell\in L}p_\ell=1\).
\(\widehat L\neq\varnothing\) and \(r:L\to\widehat L\) is total.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The reduced leaf masses are nonnegative and satisfy \(\sum_{u\in\widehat L}\widehat p_u=1\), so the retained subtree defines a rooted probability tree.

notation.meaning: leaf set of the original scenario tree

children.title: Conditional Scenario Reduction
children.top_down_role: Reduction of successor scenarios within history-conditioned subtrees.

knowledge_statements.title: Conditional Scenario Reduction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local scenario reduction applied separately at each retained history.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every retained nonterminal node \(v\), let its children \(C(v)\) carry conditional masses \(q_{w\mid v}\) and stage outcomes \(\xi_w\). Choose a retained child set \(R(v)\subseteq C(v)\). Map each discarded child \(w\) to \[r_v(w)\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{u\in R(v)}c_v(\xi_w,\xi_u),\] and set \(\widehat q_{u\mid v}=\sum_{w:r_v(w)=u}q_{w\mid v}\). Repeat recursively below retained children, using only descendants sharing the history represented by \(v\). Output the reduced tree with conditional probabilities \(\widehat q_{u\mid v}\); stop according to prescribed local cardinalities or conditional-cost tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At every retained history, reduce only its conditional child distribution, transfer discarded conditional mass locally, and recurse through retained children.
assumptions_latex: Each nonterminal node has a finite conditional child distribution.
Every \(R(v)\) is nonempty.
Each reassignment remains within the same parent history.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every retained node \(v\), \(\sum_{u\in R(v)}\widehat q_{u\mid v}=1\), so the output defines a probability tree.

notation.meaning: conditional probability of child w given v
local reassignment map at history v

children.title: Conditional-Mass Reallocation
children.top_down_role: Redistribution of probability mass after history-specific scenario removal.

knowledge_statements.title: Conditional-Mass Reallocation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pushforward representation of local probability transfer on a scenario tree.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a retained parent node \(v\). Let \(C(v)\) be its original child set, let \(R(v)\subseteq C(v)\) be its nonempty retained child set, and let \(r_v:C(v)\to R(v)\) satisfy \(r_v(u)=u\) for every \(u\in R(v)\). Define the conditional probability measure on child indices by \(q_v=\sum_{w\in C(v)}q_{w\mid v}\delta_w\). Its pushforward under \(r_v\) is \[(r_v)_\#q_v=\sum_{u\in R(v)}\widehat q_{u\mid v}\delta_u,\qquad \widehat q_{u\mid v}=\sum_{w\in C(v):r_v(w)=u}q_{w\mid v}.\] If retained child \(u\) carries outcome \(\xi_u\), the corresponding reduced conditional outcome distribution is \(\sum_{u\in R(v)}\widehat q_{u\mid v}\delta_{\xi_u}\). If the probability mass reaching \(v\) is \(p_v\), the reduced joint mass on edge \((v,u)\) is \(p_v\widehat q_{u\mid v}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Push the conditional distribution on child indices through the local reassignment map, then attach each resulting mass to its retained child's outcome.
assumptions_latex: \(q_{w\mid v}\geq0\) and \(\sum_{w\in C(v)}q_{w\mid v}=1\).
\(R(v)\neq\varnothing\).
\(r_v:C(v)\to R(v)\) is total.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat q_{u\mid v}\geq0\) and \(\sum_{u\in R(v)}\widehat q_{u\mid v}=1\).

notation.meaning: conditional probability measure on the original child indices of v
pushforward conditional distribution on retained child indices
Dirac probability measure at child index u

children.title: Filtration-Preservation Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Information distinctions that conditional reduction must preserve.

knowledge_statements.title: Filtration-Preservation Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The information boundary beyond which tree reduction destroys admissible adapted policies.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H_t\) be original histories at stage \(t\), and let \(r_t:H_t\to\widehat H_t\) define reduced histories. A reduced policy can represent an original adapted policy \(x_t:H_t\to X_t\) only if \[r_t(h)=r_t(h')\Longrightarrow x_t(h)=x_t(h').\] Thus merging two histories on which an admissible policy takes different decisions loses that policy. Concretely, if \(H_1=\{a,b\}\), \(r_1(a)=r_1(b)\), and feasibility requires \(x_1(a)=0\) and \(x_1(b)=1\), no policy measurable with respect to the reduced filtration is feasible. Cross-history mass transfer therefore cannot generally preserve the original adapted feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Merging distinguishable histories forces equal decisions there; if feasibility or optimality requires different actions, the reduced filtration cannot represent the original policy.
assumptions_latex: Policies are adapted to their respective history filtrations.
Reduced decisions are functions of reduced histories.
The reduction merges at least two original histories.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If some admissible \(x_t\) is nonconstant on a fiber of \(r_t\), the reduction does not preserve the original adapted policy set.

children.title: Scenario Aggregation
children.top_down_role: Replacement of multiple scenarios by coarser aggregate representatives.

knowledge_statements.title: Scenario Aggregation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Partition-based compression of a finite scenario distribution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input scenarios \(\xi_i\in\Xi\), masses \(p_i\), a partition \(G_1,\ldots,G_m\) of \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\), and representatives \(z_g\in\Xi\). Define aggregate masses \[q_g=\sum_{i\in G_g}p_i\] and output the reduced distribution \(Q=\sum_{g=1}^m q_g\delta_{z_g}\). When \(\Xi\) is a convex subset of a Euclidean space and squared Euclidean distortion is used, a canonical representative is \(z_g=q_g^{-1}\sum_{i\in G_g}p_i\xi_i\). Otherwise representatives may be constrained medoids or minimizers of a prescribed within-group distortion. Empty groups are disallowed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partition scenarios into nonempty groups, sum each group's probabilities, and replace its members by a representative such as a weighted centroid or medoid.
assumptions_latex: \(G_1,\ldots,G_m\) is a partition into nonempty groups.
Each representative \(z_g\) belongs to the allowed scenario space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q\) is a probability measure supported on at most \(m\) aggregate representatives.

children.title: Scenario Bunching
children.top_down_role: Formation of scenario groups for joint treatment or compression.

knowledge_statements.title: Scenario Bunching
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A threshold condition defining coherent groups of nearby scenarios.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(d\) be a dissimilarity on the finite scenario set and let \(\tau\geq0\). A partition \(G_1,\ldots,G_m\) is a diameter-\(\tau\) scenario bunching when every group is nonempty and \[\max_{i,j\in G_g}d(\xi_i,\xi_j)\leq\tau\qquad\text{for every }g.\] If representatives \(z_g\) are prescribed, the alternative radius-\(\tau\) condition is \(\max_{i\in G_g}d(\xi_i,z_g)\leq\tau\). Diameter control implies that each member lies within \(\tau\) of any member selected as representative; radius control directly bounds every assignment cost to the prescribed representative.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A valid bunching partitions scenarios into nonempty groups whose diameter, or distance to a designated representative, does not exceed a chosen threshold.
assumptions_latex: \(d:\Xi\times\Xi\to[0,\infty)\) is a specified dissimilarity.
\(\tau\geq0\).
The scenario set is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each group satisfies the selected diameter or representative-radius fidelity threshold.

children.title: Aggregate Representative Selection
children.top_down_role: Choice of representative outcomes for compressed scenario groups.

knowledge_statements.title: Aggregate Representative Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distortion-minimizing representative choice within each scenario group.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a nonempty group \(G_g\), masses \(p_i>0\), an admissible representative set \(Z_g\), and a loss \(\ell:\Xi\times Z_g\to[0,\infty]\), select \[z_g\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{z\in Z_g}\sum_{i\in G_g}p_i\ell(\xi_i,z).\] For \(Z_g=\{\xi_i:i\in G_g\}\), this is a weighted medoid. In a Euclidean space with \(\ell(\xi,z)=\lVert\xi-z\rVert_2^2\), if the weighted centroid \(\bar\xi_g=(\sum_{i\in G_g}p_i)^{-1}\sum_{i\in G_g}p_i\xi_i\) belongs to \(Z_g\), then the unique selected representative is \(z_g=\bar\xi_g\). Output one selected representative for each group.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose each group's representative by minimizing weighted within-group distortion; this gives a medoid under scenario restriction and the weighted centroid under squared Euclidean loss when that centroid is admissible.
assumptions_latex: Every group \(G_g\) is finite and nonempty.
The displayed minimum is attained on \(Z_g\).
The group mass \(\sum_{i\in G_g}p_i\) is positive.
For the centroid specialization, \(\bar\xi_g\in Z_g\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each output \(z_g\) minimizes the prescribed weighted distortion over \(Z_g\).

children.title: Within-Group Fidelity
children.top_down_role: Preservation of decision-relevant variation inside scenario groups.

knowledge_statements.title: Within-Group Fidelity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A computable transport certificate for partition-based scenario aggregation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=\sum_{i=1}^n p_i\delta_{\xi_i}\), partition \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\) into nonempty groups \(G_1,\ldots,G_m\), choose representatives \(z_g\in\Xi\), and define \(q_g=\sum_{i\in G_g}p_i\) and \(Q=\sum_{g=1}^m q_g\delta_{z_g}\). For \(r\geq1\), define \[D_r^r=\sum_{g=1}^m\sum_{i\in G_g}p_i d(\xi_i,z_g)^r.\] The assignment coupling that sends each \(\xi_i\) to its group representative has marginals \(P\) and \(Q\), and therefore \(W_r(P,Q)\leq D_r\). Consequently, for any \(\varepsilon\geq0\), the condition \(D_r\leq\varepsilon\) certifies \(W_r(P,Q)\leq\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weighted within-group assignment distortion upper-bounds Wasserstein error, providing a computable fidelity certificate for an aggregated scenario distribution.
assumptions_latex: \((\Xi,d)\) is a metric space.
The groups form a partition, each \(z_g\in\Xi\), and \(D_r<\infty\).
\(\varepsilon\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(W_r(P,Q)\leq D_r\), so \(D_r\leq\varepsilon\) certifies \(W_r(P,Q)\leq\varepsilon\).

children.title: Wasserstein Metric Families
children.top_down_role: Transport-based probability metrics used for scenario approximation.

knowledge_statements.title: Wasserstein Metric Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Order-indexed optimal-transport metrics on probability measures with finite moments.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((\Xi,d)\) be a Polish metric space and \(r\in[1,\infty)\). For probability measures \(P,Q\) satisfying \(\int d(\xi,\xi_0)^r\,P(d\xi)<\infty\) and \(\int d(\xi,\xi_0)^r\,Q(d\xi)<\infty\) for some \(\xi_0\in\Xi\), define \[W_r(P,Q)=\left(\inf_{\pi\in\Pi(P,Q)}\int_{\Xi\times\Xi}d(\xi,\zeta)^r\,\pi(d\xi,d\zeta)\right)^{1/r}.\] Here \(\Pi(P,Q)\) is the set of couplings with marginals \(P\) and \(Q\). The family \(\{W_r:r\geq1\}\) consists of metrics on the corresponding finite-moment probability spaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The order-r Wasserstein distance is the minimum r-moment transportation cost over all couplings, defined for probability measures having finite r-th moments.
assumptions_latex: \((\Xi,d)\) is Polish.
\(r\in[1,\infty)\).
\(P,Q\) have finite \(r\)-th moments.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(W_r\) is a finite metric on \(\mathcal P_r(\Xi)\).

notation.meaning: probability measures on Xi with finite r-th moment

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition and finite-moment hypotheses are standard and mathematically precise, and definition is the correct kind, but the record supplies no citation or locator. An authoritative optimal-transport source is required.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Lipschitz seminorm and Wasserstein-1 distance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual Lipschitz representation of the Wasserstein-1 distance induced by a ground metric, including its finiteness boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let (\mathcal X,\rho) be a metric space. A function f:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R is L-Lipschitz when |f(x)-f(x')|\le L\rho(x,x') for all x,x'\in\mathcal X, and \|f\|_{\mathrm{Lip}} is the least such L. For probability measures \mathbb Q and \mathbb P, set W_\rho(\mathbb Q,\mathbb P)=\sup_{\|f\|_{\mathrm{Lip}}\le1}\left(\int f\,d\mathbb Q-\int f\,d\mathbb P\right). This is the Wasserstein metric on a class of measures for which it is finite, such as measures having finite first moment with respect to \rho.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Lipschitz seminorm is the smallest constant controlling changes of a function by the ground metric. The supremum of expectation differences over 1-Lipschitz functions gives the Wasserstein-1 distance; it is a metric on an appropriate finite-moment domain and may otherwise be infinite.
assumptions_latex: (\mathcal X,\rho)\text{ is a metric space}
\mathbb P,\mathbb Q\text{ are probability measures}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: W_\rho(\mathbb Q,\mathbb P)=\sup_{\|f\|_{\mathrm{Lip}}\le1}\left(\int f\,d\mathbb Q-\int f\,d\mathbb P\right),\text{ and this is a metric on its finite-moment domain.}

source_evidence.locator: Concentration of measure / 3.3. Wasserstein distances and information inequalities / Definition 3.3-extra-1

children.title: Fortet–Mourier Metric Families
children.top_down_role: Test-function probability metrics used for weak-distribution comparison.

assumptions_latex: \((S,d)\) is a separable metric space.
\(\mu,\nu\in\mathcal P(S)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d_{\mathrm{FM}}\) is a bounded probability metric whenever bounded Lipschitz functions separate probability measures.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bounded-Lipschitz normalization; alternative equivalent normalizations differ only by constants.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The Fortet–Mourier distance associated with \(d\) is
\[
d_{\mathrm{FM}}(\mu,\nu):=\sup_{f\in\mathrm{BL}_1(S)}\left|\int_S f\,d\mu-\int_S f\,d\nu\right|.
\]
More generally, positive bounds \(a,b\) define the family obtained from test functions satisfying \(\|f\|_\infty\le a\) and \(\operatorname{Lip}_d(f)\le b\). Each member is finite and is a probability metric provided its test-function class separates distinct measures; otherwise it is a pseudometric.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fortet–Mourier metrics compare probability laws through uniformly bounded Lipschitz test functions, with different norm and Lipschitz bounds giving equivalent family members.
knowledge_statements.title: Fortet–Mourier Metric Families

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition and content kind fit the leaf, but no cited source supports the normalization, separation condition, or equivalence of the parameterized family.

children.title: Metric Topology Comparisons
children.top_down_role: Comparative distributional distinctions captured by the two metric families.

assumptions_latex: \((S,d)\) is Polish.
\(p\ge 1\), and all measures considered lie in \(\mathcal P_p(S)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Fortet–Mourier convergence characterizes weak convergence, whereas \(W_p\)-convergence additionally controls the \(p\)-th moment.

notation.meaning: probability measures with finite p-th moment

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Comparison on Polish spaces with the bounded-Lipschitz Fortet–Mourier normalization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a sequence \((\mu_n)\subset\mathcal P_p(S)\) and \(\mu\in\mathcal P_p(S)\),
\[
d_{\mathrm{FM}}(\mu_n,\mu)\to0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \mu_n\Rightarrow\mu.
\]
Moreover,
\[
W_p(\mu_n,\mu)\to0
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\mu_n\Rightarrow\mu\ \text{ and }\int d(x,x_0)^p\,d\mu_n(x)\to\int d(x,x_0)^p\,d\mu(x)
\]
for one, hence every, \(x_0\in S\). Thus Wasserstein convergence implies Fortet–Mourier convergence, but the converse can fail when \(p\)-th moments are not uniformly controlled.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fortet–Mourier distance metrizes weak convergence; p-Wasserstein convergence is weak convergence plus convergence of p-th moments.
knowledge_statements.title: Metric Topology Comparisons

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The topology comparison is mathematically standard and the property kind fits, but the weak-convergence and Wasserstein moment characterizations require an authoritative, specifically located citation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Bounded-Lipschitz metrization of weak convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identifies the bounded-Lipschitz metric as a metric inducing the topology of weak convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For probability measures $\mu_1,\mu_2$ on a metric space $(R,r)$, define
\[
d_{BL}(\mu_1,\mu_2)=\sup\left\{\int_R H\,d\mu_1-\int_R H\,d\mu_2: H\in\operatorname{Lip}(1),\ \sup_{w\in R}|H(w)|\le 1\right\}.
\]
Then $d_{BL}$ metrizes the topology of weak convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The bounded-Lipschitz metric, formed from test functions bounded by one and having Lipschitz constant at most one, induces the topology of weak convergence of probability measures.
assumptions_latex: (R,r)\text{ is a metric space}
\mu_1,\mu_2\text{ are Borel probability measures on }R
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: d_{BL}\text{ metrizes the topology of weak convergence}

source_evidence.locator: Appendix J / J. The Wasserstein distance / Lemma J.4
