children.top_down_role: SAA estimators using density-ratio reweighting under changed sampling laws.

knowledge_statements.title: Likelihood-Ratio SAA
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Change-of-measure representation for weighted SAA, not likelihood-ratio gradient estimation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\) be a nonempty feasible set. Let \(P\) and \(Q\) admit densities \(p\) and \(q\) with respect to a common measure \(
u\), and assume \(P\ll Q\). Define \(L(z)=p(z)/q(z)\) on \(\{z:q(z)>0\}\). For every \(x\in X\) such that \(L(\xi)F(x,\xi)\in L^1(Q)\), \[\mathbb E_P[F(x,\xi)]=\int F(x,z)p(z)\,
u(dz)=\int F(x,z)L(z)q(z)\,
u(dz)=\mathbb E_Q[L(\xi)F(x,\xi)].\] Thus, for independent samples \(\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_N\sim Q\), the likelihood-ratio SAA objective is \(N^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^N L(\xi_i)F(x,\xi_i)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The target expectation equals a proposal-law expectation after multiplying losses by the target-to-proposal likelihood ratio, yielding a weighted SAA objective.
assumptions_latex: The feasible set \(X\) is nonempty.
The target and sampling laws have densities \(p\) and \(q\) with respect to a common measure \(\nu\), and \(P\ll Q\).
The likelihood-weighted loss \(L(\xi)F(x,\xi)\) is integrable under \(Q\) for every relevant \(x\in X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Multiplication by the likelihood ratio converts expectations under the sampling density into expectations under the target density.

notation.meaning: Target and sampling densities with respect to a common dominating measure

review_flags: Terminology should be checked because likelihood-ratio methods can also denote gradient estimation.

children.title: Sampling-Law Selection
children.top_down_role: Choice of alternative sampling distributions for variance reduction.

knowledge_statements.title: Sampling-Law Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise second-moment criterion for choosing an importance-sampling law.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\) be a nonempty feasible set, and let the target law have density \(p\) with respect to a measure \(
u\). For a fixed \(x\in X\), set \(g_x(z)=F(x,z)\) and \(f(x)=\int g_x(z)p(z)\,
u(dz)\). For \(N\) independent samples from a proposal density \(q\), the variance of the importance-sampling estimator is \(N^{-1} igl(\int g_x(z)^2p(z)^2/q(z)\,
u(dz)-f(x)^2 igr)\). Among all proposal densities positive wherever \(|g_x|p>0\), the second moment is minimized by \(q_x^*(z)=|g_x(z)|p(z)/\int|g_x(u)|p(u)\,
u(du)\), provided the denominator is finite and nonzero. Because the optimizing decision is not known in advance, a practical SAA sampling law should control an aggregate or worst-case weighted second moment over relevant \(x\in X\), while retaining the required support and feasible sampling.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose a proposal to reduce weighted second moments over relevant decisions; at a fixed decision, the ideal density is proportional to absolute loss times the target density.
assumptions_latex: The feasible set \(X\) is nonempty, and the target law has density \(p\) with respect to a measure \(\nu\).
Candidate proposal densities \(q\) are positive wherever \(|g_x|p>0\) for the relevant decisions.
For every relevant \(x\in X\), the weighted loss has a finite second moment under the selected proposal.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For a fixed decision \(x\), the variance-minimizing proposal density is proportional to \(|g_x|p\); practical selection must approximate this criterion across relevant decisions while preserving support.

notation.meaning: Target and proposal densities with respect to \(\nu\)
Loss integrand at a fixed decision

review_flags: The pointwise optimal proposal does not by itself solve uniform proposal selection over the feasible set.

children.title: Likelihood-Weight Stability
children.top_down_role: Variance or degeneracy risks arising from unstable likelihood weights.

knowledge_statements.title: Likelihood-Weight Stability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient moment condition controlling likelihood-weighted losses uniformly over decisions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a nonempty feasible set, let \(P\ll Q\), and let \(w=dP/dQ\). A sufficient likelihood-weight stability condition for weighted SAA is the existence of \(\delta>0\) such that \(\sup_{x\in X}\mathbb E_Q[|w(\xi)F(x,\xi)|^{2+\delta}]<\infty\), together with an envelope or regularity condition yielding a uniform law over \(X\). This moment bound implies uniformly finite variances and uniform integrability of the weighted losses. If \(\mathbb E_Q[w(\xi)^2F(x,\xi)^2]=\infty\) for some relevant \(x\in X\), the corresponding unbiased sample average has infinite variance; rare observations with very large \(w\) can then dominate the SAA objective and invalidate variance-based error assessments.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Control higher moments of likelihood-weighted losses uniformly over the feasible set; otherwise rare, enormous weights can cause infinite variance and unstable SAA objectives.
assumptions_latex: The feasible set \(X\) is nonempty.
The target law \(P\) is absolutely continuous with respect to the proposal law \(Q\).
The weighted loss class \(\{w(\cdot)F(x,\cdot):x\in X\}\) is measurable under \(Q\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A uniform \((2+\delta)\)-moment bound supplies finite variances and uniform integrability; without adequate weight-tail control, SAA estimates may have infinite variance or unstable extremes.
review_flags: The displayed moment condition is sufficient, not a necessary characterization.

assumptions_latex: The scenario admits a transform \(\xi=T(U)\) with \(U\) uniform on \([0,1]^d\).
For each feasible \(x\), the transformed integrand \(g_x(u)=F(x,T(u))\) is integrable.
The design points form a specified deterministic low-discrepancy sequence or a randomized version preserving uniform marginals.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The QMC SAA objective is an equal-weight cubature approximation of the population objective; bounded-variation integrands admit a discrepancy-based deterministic error bound.

notation.meaning: Transformed loss on the unit cube

review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports quasi-Monte Carlo SAA.
A source is needed for the discrepancy bound and optimization-level conditions.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transform-based QMC objective with the bounded-variation discrepancy bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=\int_{[0,1]^d}g_x(u)\,du\), where \(g_x(u)=F(x,T(u))\), and let \(u_1,\ldots,u_N\in[0,1]^d\) be low-discrepancy points. Quasi-Monte Carlo SAA solves \(\min_{x\in X}\widehat f_N^{\mathrm{QMC}}(x)\), where \(\widehat f_N^{\mathrm{QMC}}(x)=N^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^N g_x(u_i)\). If \(g_x\) has bounded Hardy-Krause variation \(V_{\mathrm{HK}}(g_x)\), then \(|\widehat f_N^{\mathrm{QMC}}(x)-f(x)|\leq V_{\mathrm{HK}}(g_x)D_N^*\). Uniform optimization guarantees require corresponding uniform variation or other function-class control; randomized QMC permits replication-based error assessment.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replace random scenarios by low-discrepancy unit-cube points; bounded-variation losses have integration error controlled by the design's discrepancy.
knowledge_statements.title: Quasi-Monte Carlo SAA

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation fits the QMC SAA leaf, and the pointwise Koksma-Hlawka form is standard. A specific source is still required for the Hardy-Krause variation convention, discrepancy bound, and any optimization-level uniformity claim.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Compact-Set SAA Value and Solution Consistency
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Almost-sure convergence of optimal values and one-sided solution-set deviation under compact containment and uniform objective convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose there exists a compact set \(C\subset\mathbb R^n\) such that \(S\neq\varnothing\) and \(S\subset C\), \(f\) is finite-valued and continuous on \(C\), \(\widehat f_N\to f\) uniformly on \(C\) with probability one, and, with probability one, \(\widehat S_N\neq\varnothing\) and \(\widehat S_N\subset C\) for all sufficiently large \(N\). Then \(\widehat\vartheta_N\to\vartheta^*\) and \(\mathbb D(\widehat S_N,S)\to0\) with probability one as \(N\to\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the true and eventual empirical solution sets lie in a common compact set, the true objective is continuous there, and the empirical objectives converge uniformly there almost surely, then the empirical optimal values and one-sided deviation of empirical solutions from the true solution set converge almost surely.
assumptions_latex: C\subset\mathbb R^n\text{ is compact}
\varnothing\ne S\subset C
f\text{ is finite-valued and continuous on }C
\widehat f_N\to f\text{ uniformly on }C\text{ w.p. }1
\mathbb P\!\left(\exists N_0\ \forall N\ge N_0:\ \varnothing\ne\widehat S_N\subset C\right)=1
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \widehat\vartheta_N\to\vartheta^*\quad\text{and}\quad\mathbb D(\widehat S_N,S)\to0\quad\text{w.p. }1

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Consistency of SAA optimal values and solution sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consistency under uniform objective convergence and compact containment of true and sampled optimizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose there exists a compact set \(C\subset\mathbb R^d\) such that \(\varnothing\neq\pi^*\subset C\), \(f_n\to f\) uniformly on \(C\) almost surely, and, almost surely for all sufficiently large \(n\), \(\varnothing\neq\Pi_n^*\subset C\). Then \(v_n^*\to v^*\). If, in addition, \(f\) is continuous on \(C\), then \(\mathbb D(\Pi_n^*,\pi^*)\to0\) almost surely.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform almost-sure convergence on a compact set containing the true and eventual sampled optimizers yields convergence of optimal values. Continuity of the true objective additionally gives almost-sure one-sided convergence of sampled solution sets to the true solution set.
assumptions_latex: C\subset\mathbb R^d\text{ is compact}
\varnothing\neq\pi^*\subset C
f_n\to f\text{ uniformly on }C\text{ a.s.}
\mathbb P(\exists N\;\forall n\ge N:\varnothing\neq\Pi_n^*\subset C)=1
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: v_n^*\to v^*;\qquad f\in C(C)\Longrightarrow\mathbb D(\Pi_n^*,\pi^*)\to0\text{ a.s.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Almost-sure consistency of SAA for compact stochastic minimax problems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strong consistency of the SAA optimal value and outer solution set under dominated Carathéodory, compactness, and iid assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(F(x,y,\xi)\) is a Carathéodory function, \(X\) and \(Y\) are nonempty compact sets, and there exist an open neighborhood \(N_0\supset X\times Y\) and an integrable function \(h(\xi)\) such that \(|F(x,y,\xi)|\le h(\xi)\) for all \((x,y)\in N_0\) and almost every \(\xi\). If the sample is iid, then, as the sample size \(N\to\infty\), \[\widehat\vartheta_N\to\vartheta^*,\qquad \mathbb D(\widehat S_{x,N},S_x)\to0\quad\text{with probability one}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an iid SAA of a compact stochastic minimax problem with a dominated Carathéodory integrand, the approximate optimal values converge almost surely to the true optimal value, and the deviation of the approximate outer solution set from the true outer solution set converges almost surely to zero.
assumptions_latex: F(x,y,\xi)\text{ is Carathéodory}
X\ne\varnothing,\ Y\ne\varnothing,\quad X,Y\text{ are compact}
\exists N_0\supset X\times Y\text{ open},\ \exists h\in L^1:\ |F(x,y,\xi)|\le h(\xi)\quad\forall(x,y)\in N_0\text{, a.e. }\xi
\{\xi_i\}_{i\ge1}\text{ is iid}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \widehat\vartheta_N\xrightarrow{\mathrm{a.s.}}\vartheta^*,\qquad \mathbb D(\widehat S_{x,N},S_x)\xrightarrow{\mathrm{a.s.}}0.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convex SAA Consistency under a Pointwise Law of Large Numbers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Almost-sure value and solution consistency for convex stochastic programs under pointwise LLN assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(F\) is random lower semicontinuous; \(F(\cdot,\xi)\) is convex for almost every \(\xi\in\Xi\); \(X\) is closed and convex; \(f\) is lower semicontinuous and there exists \(\bar x\in X\) such that \(f(x)<+\infty\) for every \(x\) in a neighborhood of \(\bar x\); the true solution set \(S\) is nonempty and bounded; and the law of large numbers holds pointwise. Then \(\widehat\vartheta_N\to\vartheta^*\) and \(\mathbb D(\widehat S_N,S)\to0\) with probability one as \(N\to\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the stated convex stochastic program, pointwise laws of large numbers yield almost-sure convergence of SAA optimal values and one-sided solution-set deviation when the expected objective has the required lower-semicontinuity and local-finiteness properties and the true solution set is nonempty and bounded.
assumptions_latex: F\text{ is random lower semicontinuous}
F(\cdot,\xi)\text{ is convex for almost every }\xi\in\Xi
X\text{ is closed and convex}
f\text{ is lower semicontinuous}
\exists\bar x\in X\ \exists\text{ a neighborhood }U\text{ of }\bar x:\ \forall x\in U,\ f(x)<+\infty
S\ne\varnothing\text{ and }S\text{ is bounded}
\forall x\in X,\ \widehat f_N(x)\to f(x)\text{ w.p. }1
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \widehat\vartheta_N\to\vartheta^*\quad\text{and}\quad\mathbb D(\widehat S_N,S)\to0\quad\text{w.p. }1

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Transfer of persistent SAA local minimality to the population objective
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local-minimum consistency under all assumptions of Theorem 8.5 and a pathwise, eventually uniform local-optimality radius for the selected SAA points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Assume all hypotheses of Theorem 8.5. Suppose further that, for every fixed sample path \(\bar\xi=(\xi_1,\xi_2,\ldots)\), there exist \(n_0>0\) and \(\delta>0\) such that, for all \(n\ge n_0\) and all \(x\in B(X_n^*,\delta)\cap\Theta\),
\[
f_n(X_n^*)\le f_n(x).
\]
Then \(x^*\) is a local minimum of \(f\) with probability one.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under all assumptions of the preceding SAA set-convergence theorem, if along every fixed sample path the selected sample solutions are eventually local minima with one positive radius, then the population point is a local minimum almost surely.
assumptions_latex: \text{All assumptions of Theorem 8.5 hold}.
\forall\bar\xi\ \exists n_0>0,\delta>0\ \forall n\ge n_0\ \forall x\in B(X_n^*,\delta)\cap\Theta:\ f_n(X_n^*)\le f_n(x).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathbb P\bigl(x^*\text{ is a local minimum of }f\bigr)=1.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Almost-Sure Consistency of SAA Generalized-Equation Solution Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Establishes one-sided set convergence of SAA generalized-equation solution sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subset\mathbb R^n\) be compact with \(S\subset C\). Suppose that \(\Gamma\) is closed, \(\phi\) is continuous on \(C\), and, with probability one, for all sufficiently large \(N\), \(\widehat S_N\neq\varnothing\) and \(\widehat S_N\subset C\). If \(\widehat\phi_N\to\phi\) uniformly on \(C\) with probability one, then \(\mathbb D(\widehat S_N,S)\to0\) with probability one as \(N\to\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under closedness, compact containment, continuity, eventual nonemptiness, and uniform almost-sure convergence of the sampled mappings, the one-sided deviation of the SAA solution set from the true solution set converges to zero almost surely.

\(\widehat\phi_N\to\phi\) uniformly on \(C\) with probability one

Each \(\widehat f_N\) attains its minimum on \(X\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compact-feasible-set version derived from almost-sure uniform objective convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a nonempty compact metric space, let \(f:X\to\mathbb R\) be lower semicontinuous, and let \(\widehat f_N:X\to\mathbb R\) be sample-average objectives attaining their minima. Define \(v=\min_{x\in X}f(x)\) and \(v_N=\min_{x\in X}\widehat f_N(x)\). If \(\sup_{x\in X}|\widehat f_N(x)-f(x)|\to0\) almost surely, then \(|v_N-v|\leq\sup_{x\in X}|\widehat f_N(x)-f(x)|\to0\) almost surely. Hence the optimal values of the SAA problems are strongly consistent for the population optimal value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a compact feasible set, almost-sure uniform convergence of SAA objectives implies almost-sure convergence of their minimum values.

Each SAA problem has at least one minimizer.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Outer consistency of global SAA minimizers under compactness and uniform convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a compact metric space, define \(S=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}f(x)\neq\varnothing\), and let \(S_N=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}\widehat f_N(x)\neq\varnothing\). Suppose \(f\) is lower semicontinuous and \(\sup_{x\in X}|\widehat f_N(x)-f(x)|\to0\) almost surely. Then every sequence \(x_N\in S_N\) has accumulation points, and every such accumulation point lies in \(S\) almost surely. Equivalently, with \(\operatorname{dist}(A,B)=\sup_{a\in A}\inf_{b\in B}d(a,b)\), one has \(\operatorname{dist}(S_N,S)\to0\) almost surely. If \(S=\{x^*\}\), every choice \(x_N\in S_N\) converges almost surely to \(x^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under compactness and uniform objective convergence, SAA minimizers can accumulate only at true minimizers; uniqueness gives convergence of every selected minimizer.
knowledge_statements.title: Solution-Set Consistency

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The outer solution-set consistency theorem is correctly scoped to compactness and uniform convergence, and the one-sided excess conclusion is appropriate. No source is cited for the theorem, so it cannot pass candidate review.

knowledge_statements.title: Generalized-Equation Consistency
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consistency of isolated solutions of sample-average generalized equations under graphical convergence and strong regularity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subset\mathbb R^d\) be closed and convex, and define \(G(x)=\mathbb E[F(x,\xi)]+N_C(x)\) and \(G_n(x)=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^nF(x,\xi_i)+N_C(x)\). Suppose \(0\in G(\bar x)\), the sample mappings converge locally uniformly to \(x\mapsto\mathbb E[F(x,\xi)]\) almost surely, and \(G\) is strongly metrically regular at \((\bar x,0)\). Then, almost surely, for all sufficiently large \(n\), the inclusion \(0\in G_n(x)\) has a unique solution \(x_n\) in a fixed neighborhood of \(\bar x\), and \(x_n\to\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Locally uniform sample-average convergence and strong metric regularity ensure that the nearby empirical generalized-equation solution exists uniquely and converges to the population solution.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subset\mathbb R^d\) is closed and convex, and \(\xi_i\) are iid.
\(n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^nF(\cdot,\xi_i)\to\mathbb E[F(\cdot,\xi)]\) locally uniformly almost surely.
\(G\) is strongly metrically regular at \((\bar x,0)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb P(\exists n_0\;\forall n\ge n_0:\ x_n\text{ exists uniquely near }\bar x\text{ and }x_n\to\bar x)=1\).

notation.meaning: normal cone to C at x

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No citation is supplied. Moreover, local uniform function-value perturbations alone do not generally preserve strong metric regularity or uniqueness; an authoritative result must specify the required perturbation topology or stronger Lipschitz/graphical assumptions.

children.title: Noncompactness Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Consistency difficulties caused by unbounded or noncompact decision regions.

knowledge_statements.title: Noncompactness Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of minimizer consistency when local convergence is not supplemented by level-boundedness or tightness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \(C=\mathbb R\), let \(f(x)=x^2\). For each \(n\), choose a continuous function \(f_n\) satisfying \(f_n(x)=x^2\) outside \((n-1/4,n+1/4)\), \(f_n(n)=-1\), and \(f_n(x)\ge-1\). Then \(f_n\to f\) uniformly on every compact set, while every global minimizer of \(f_n\) equals \(n\) if the well is chosen strictly above \(-1\) off its center. Hence \(x_n=n\to\infty\), although \(f\) has the unique minimizer \(0\). Local uniform convergence therefore does not imply solution consistency without eventual level-boundedness or an equivalent compactness condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A negative empirical well escaping to infinity defeats minimizer consistency despite uniform convergence on every compact set.
assumptions_latex: \(C=\mathbb R\) is noncompact.
\(f_n\to f\) uniformly on compact subsets only.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname*{argmin} f=\{0\}\), but \(x_n\in\operatorname*{argmin}f_n\) satisfies \(x_n=n\to\infty\).

notation.meaning: approximating objective with an escaping well

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The self-contained escaping-well construction is mathematically plausible and fits the failure-boundary container, but it has no cited source or registered evidence.

children.title: Nonuniqueness Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Consistency behavior when population or sample problems admit multiple solutions.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonuniqueness Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Set consistency need not select a convergent optimizer when the population optimum is nonunique.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C=[-1,1]\), \(f(x)=0\), and \(f_n(x)=(-1)^n x/n\). Then \(f_n\to f\) uniformly on \(C\), and the optimal values converge to \(0\). Nevertheless, each empirical problem has a unique minimizer: \(x_n=-1\) for even \(n\) and \(x_n=1\) for odd \(n\). Thus \((x_n)\) does not converge, although every cluster point belongs to \(\operatorname*{argmin}f=C\). Uniform objective convergence yields outer solution-set consistency here, but it cannot identify a single limiting optimizer without uniqueness or a selection rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With multiple population optimizers, empirical minimizers may oscillate forever even under uniform objective convergence and correct optimal values.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\limsup_n\operatorname*{argmin}f_n\subseteq\operatorname*{argmin}f\), but the unique selections \(x_n\) do not converge.

notation.meaning: unique optimizer of the nth approximation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The parity calculation and oscillating-minimizer conclusion are correct, and the content kind fits. No source or registered evidence supports the nontrivial counterexample claim.

knowledge_statements.title: Uniformity Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise objective convergence alone does not control empirical minimizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C=[0,1]\), \(f(x)=x^2\), and choose distinct \(a_n\in[1/2,1]\) with \(a_n\to1/2\). Define \(f_n(a_n)=-1\) and \(f_n(x)=x^2\) for \(x\ne a_n\). For each fixed \(x\), at most one term differs from \(f(x)\), so \(f_n(x)\to f(x)\) pointwise. Yet \(a_n\) is the unique minimizer of \(f_n\), while the unique minimizer of \(f\) is \(0\), and \(a_n\to1/2\). Thus pointwise convergence cannot replace uniform, epigraphical, or otherwise minimization-compatible convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Moving downward spikes can preserve pointwise convergence while forcing empirical minimizers toward a nonoptimal population point.
assumptions_latex: \(a_n\in[1/2,1]\) are distinct and \(a_n\to1/2\).
No lower-semicontinuity or uniform convergence is imposed on \(f_n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f_n(x)\to f(x)\) for every \(x\in C\), but \(\operatorname*{argmin}f_n=\{a_n\}\to\{1/2\}\ne\{0\}=\operatorname*{argmin}f\).

notation.meaning: location of the moving downward spike

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The moving-spike counterexample correctly separates pointwise convergence from minimizer consistency and fits the container, but no citation or registered evidence is supplied.

children.title: Interacting Consistency Pathologies
children.top_down_role: Combined effects of escaping solutions, multiplicity, plus nonuniform approximation.

knowledge_statements.title: Interacting Consistency Pathologies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Simultaneous loss of compactness, uniformity, and uniqueness can invalidate all common forms of optimizer consistency.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=0\) on \(C=\mathbb R\). For each \(n\), construct continuous \(f_n\) with a unique value \(-1\) at \(x=n\), with \(f_n(x)=(-1)^n x/n\) on \([-1,1]\), and with interpolation supported outside every fixed compact set for sufficiently large \(n\). Then \(f_n(x)\to0\) pointwise, but every global minimizer is \(x_n=n\). The limiting problem has no distinguished optimizer, convergence is nonuniform globally, and minimizers are not tight. Consequently neither convergence of selected solutions nor compact outer convergence of empirical solution sets follows.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Escaping wells, nonuniform convergence, and a flat population optimum can combine so that empirical optimizers have no finite cluster point.
assumptions_latex: \(C=\mathbb R\) and \(f\equiv0\).
Each \(f_n\) has a strict global well at \(n\) and converges pointwise to \(f\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_n=n\in\operatorname*{argmin}f_n\) has no finite cluster point, despite \(f_n\to f\) pointwise.

notation.meaning: approximation combining oscillation and an escaping well

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The intended interacting pathology is plausible, but the continuous interpolation and unique-global-minimum construction are not defined precisely enough for direct verification, and no source is cited.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Asymptotic expansion and singleton-saddle CLT for minimax SAA values
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Root-N asymptotic theory for the optimal value of an iid SAA of a stochastic minimax problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the stochastic minimax problem and its iid-sample SAA, suppose (A'1)--(A'2) and (A'4)--(A'5) hold. Then \widehat{\vartheta}_N=\inf_{x\in S_x}\sup_{y\in S_y}\widehat f_N(x,y)+o_p(N^{-1/2}). If S_x=\{\bar x\} and S_y=\{\bar y\}, then \sqrt N(\widehat\vartheta_N-\vartheta^*)\xrightarrow{\mathcal D}\mathcal N(0,\sigma^2), where \sigma^2=\operatorname{Var}[F(\bar x,\bar y,\xi)].
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the stated assumptions, the minimax SAA value equals the empirical objective optimized over the true primal and dual solution sets up to a root-N-negligible remainder. With a unique primal and dual solution, its centered root-N error is asymptotically normal with the integrand variance at the unique saddle point.
assumptions_latex: \xi_1,\ldots,\xi_N\text{ are iid}
(A'1)\text{--}(A'2)\text{ hold}
(A'4)\text{--}(A'5)\text{ hold}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \widehat{\vartheta}_N=\inf_{x\in S_x}\sup_{y\in S_y}\widehat f_N(x,y)+o_p(N^{-1/2});\quad S_x=\{\bar x\},\ S_y=\{\bar y\}\Rightarrow\sqrt N(\widehat\vartheta_N-\vartheta^*)\xrightarrow{\mathcal D}\mathcal N\!\left(0,\operatorname{Var}[F(\bar x,\bar y,\xi)]\right).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: First-order asymptotic distribution of the SAA optimal value
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Asymptotic expansion and limiting law for the SAA optimal value, including the normal limit under a unique true minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\widehat\vartheta_N\) be the optimal value of the SAA problem, let \(\vartheta^*=\inf_{x\in X}f(x)\), and let \(S=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}f(x)\). Suppose the sample is iid, \(X\) is compact, and assumptions (A1) and (A2) hold. Then \[\widehat\vartheta_N=\inf_{x\in S}\widehat f_N(x)+o_p(N^{-1/2}),\qquad \sqrt N(\widehat\vartheta_N-\vartheta^*)\xrightarrow{\mathcal D}\inf_{x\in S}Y(x).\] If additionally \(S=\{\bar x\}\), then \[\sqrt N(\widehat\vartheta_N-\vartheta^*)\xrightarrow{\mathcal D}\mathcal N\!\left(0,\sigma^2(\bar x)\right).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under iid sampling, compactness, and the square-integrable random Lipschitz assumptions, the SAA optimal value is asymptotically determined by minimizing the sample objective over the true solution set. Its scaled error converges to the infimum of the limiting Gaussian process over that set; with a unique true minimizer, the limit is normal.
assumptions_latex: \{\xi_i\}_{i=1}^N\text{ is iid}
X\text{ is compact}
\exists\widetilde x\in X:\ \mathbb E[F(\widetilde x,\xi)^2]<\infty
\exists C:\Xi\to\mathbb R_+\text{ measurable}:\ \mathbb E[C(\xi)^2]<\infty
|F(x,\xi)-F(x',\xi)|\le C(\xi)\|x-x'\|\quad\forall x,x'\in X\text{, a.e. }\xi
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \widehat\vartheta_N=\inf_{x\in S}\widehat f_N(x)+o_p(N^{-1/2}),\quad \sqrt N(\widehat\vartheta_N-\vartheta^*)\xrightarrow{\mathcal D}\inf_{x\in S}Y(x);\quad S=\{\bar x\}\Rightarrow \sqrt N(\widehat\vartheta_N-\vartheta^*)\xrightarrow{\mathcal D}\mathcal N(0,\sigma^2(\bar x)).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Second-order SAA optimal-value and solution asymptotics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Second-order expansion of the SAA optimal value and weak limits for its correction and, under directional uniqueness, the scaled SAA solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose (S1)--(S4) hold and \(\sqrt N(\widehat f_N-f)\xrightarrow{\mathcal D}Y\) as random elements of \(W^{1,\infty}(U)\). Then \[\widehat\vartheta_N=\widehat f_N(\bar x)+\frac12V_f''(\widehat f_N-f)+o_p(N^{-1}),\qquad N\bigl[\widehat\vartheta_N-\widehat f_N(\bar x)\bigr]\xrightarrow{\mathcal D}\frac12V_f''(Y).\] If, moreover, for every \(\delta\in\mathcal K\) the problem defining \(V_f''(\delta)\) has the unique solution \(\bar h(\delta)\), then \[\sqrt N(\widehat x_N-\bar x)\xrightarrow{\mathcal D}\bar h(Y).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the stated unique-minimizer, second-order regularity, quadratic-growth, integrand-regularity, and functional-CLT assumptions, the SAA optimal value has a second-order expansion. Its sample-size-scaled correction converges to half the second directional derivative evaluated at the limiting process. If the derivative problem has a unique solution in every direction, the scaled SAA optimizer converges to that solution evaluated at the limiting process.
assumptions_latex: f\text{ is Lipschitz on }U\text{, has the unique minimizer }\bar x\text{ over }X\text{, and is twice continuously differentiable at }\bar x
X\text{ is second-order regular at }\bar x
f\text{ satisfies the quadratic-growth condition at }\bar x
F(\cdot,\xi)\text{ is Lipschitz on }U\text{ and differentiable at }\bar x\text{ for a.e. }\xi
\sqrt N(\widehat f_N-f)\xrightarrow{\mathcal D}Y\text{ in }W^{1,\infty}(U)
\forall\delta\in\mathcal K,\ \operatorname*{argmin}\{\text{problem defining }V_f''(\delta)\}=\{\bar h(\delta)\}\text{ for the optimizer-limit conclusion}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \widehat\vartheta_N=\widehat f_N(\bar x)+\frac12V_f''(\widehat f_N-f)+o_p(N^{-1}),\quad N[\widehat\vartheta_N-\widehat f_N(\bar x)]\xrightarrow{\mathcal D}\frac12V_f''(Y),\quad \sqrt N(\widehat x_N-\bar x)\xrightarrow{\mathcal D}\bar h(Y)\text{ under directional uniqueness.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Computational-budget rate for sublinearly solved SAA problems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint sample-size and numerical-iteration scaling of the SAA objective error.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose $\mathbb E[Y(x,\xi)^2]<\infty$ for every $x\in\Theta$; $Y(\cdot,\xi)$ is Lipschitz almost surely with Lipschitz constant $K(\xi)$ satisfying $\mathbb E[K(\xi)]<\infty$; and $f_n$ attains its infimum on $\Theta$ for every $n$ almost surely. Let $c=nk$ and suppose
\[
\frac{n}{c^{1/(2p+1)}}\to a\in(0,\infty)
\quad\text{as }c\to\infty.
\]
If the numerical procedure exhibits $p$th-order sublinear convergence, then
\[
c^{p/(2p+1)}\left(f_n(A^k(x))-v^*\right)=O_p(1)
\quad\text{as }c\to\infty.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the stated moment, Lipschitz, attainment, budget-balancing, and sublinear-solver assumptions, the SAA objective error is of stochastic order c to the power minus p divided by 2p plus 1.
assumptions_latex: \mathbb E[Y(x,\xi)^2]<\infty\quad\forall x\in\Theta
Y(\cdot,\xi)\text{ is Lipschitz w.p.1 with constant }K(\xi),\quad\mathbb E[K(\xi)]<\infty
f_n\text{ attains its infimum on }\Theta\text{ for every }n\text{ w.p.1}
c=nk
n/c^{1/(2p+1)}\to a\in(0,\infty)
A\text{ exhibits }p\text{th-order sublinear convergence}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: c^{p/(2p+1)}\left(f_n(A^k(x))-v^*\right)=O_p(1)\quad(c\to\infty)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Limit distribution of constrained convex SAA optimal values
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Root-N asymptotics for the optimal value of an iid SAA of a constrained convex stochastic program.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \widehat\vartheta_N be the optimal value of the iid SAA. Suppose the problem is convex, its true solution set S is nonempty and bounded, f and g_i are finite-valued on a neighborhood of S, the true problem satisfies Slater's condition, and (A1)--(A2) hold for F and G_i, i=1,\ldots,p. Then \sqrt N(\widehat\vartheta_N-\vartheta^*)\xrightarrow{\mathcal D}\inf_{x\in S}\sup_{\lambda\in\Lambda}\left[Y(x)+\sum_{i=1}^p\lambda_iY_i(x)\right]. If S=\{\bar x\} and \Lambda=\{\bar\lambda\}, then the limit is \mathcal N(0,\sigma^2), where \sigma^2=\operatorname{Var}\left[F(\bar x,\xi)+\sum_{i=1}^p\bar\lambda_iG_i(\bar x,\xi)\right].
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a constrained convex stochastic program satisfying bounded-solution, local-finiteness, Slater, and integrand-regularity assumptions, the root-N SAA optimal-value error converges to an infimum–supremum functional of the limiting objective and constraint processes. Unique primal and multiplier solutions give a centered normal limit with the variance of the stochastic Lagrangian at that pair.
assumptions_latex: \xi_1,\ldots,\xi_N\text{ are iid}
\text{The stochastic program is convex}
S\ne\varnothing\text{ and }S\text{ is bounded}
f\text{ and }g_i\text{ are finite-valued on a neighborhood of }S
\text{Slater's condition holds for the true problem}
(A1)\text{ and }(A2)\text{ hold for }F\text{ and }G_i,\ i=1,\ldots,p
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sqrt N(\widehat\vartheta_N-\vartheta^*)\xrightarrow{\mathcal D}\inf_{x\in S}\sup_{\lambda\in\Lambda}\left[Y(x)+\sum_{i=1}^p\lambda_iY_i(x)\right];\quad S=\{\bar x\},\ \Lambda=\{\bar\lambda\}\Rightarrow\sqrt N(\widehat\vartheta_N-\vartheta^*)\xrightarrow{\mathcal D}\mathcal N\!\left(0,\operatorname{Var}\left[F(\bar x,\xi)+\sum_{i=1}^p\bar\lambda_iG_i(\bar x,\xi)\right]\right).

knowledge_statements.title: Optimal-Value Asymptotics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order central limit theorem for the optimal value of a smooth SAA problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=\mathbb E[h(x,\xi)]\) and \(f_n(x)=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^nh(x,\xi_i)\). Suppose \(f\) has a unique interior minimizer \(x_*\), is twice continuously differentiable near \(x_*\), and \(\nabla^2f(x_*)\) is positive definite. If the usual local stochastic equicontinuity conditions give \(x_n-x_*=O_p(n^{-1/2})\), then for \(v=f(x_*)\) and \(v_n=f_n(x_n)\), \[\sqrt n\,(v_n-v)=\frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{i=1}^n\bigl(h(x_*,\xi_i)-v\bigr)+o_p(1)\Rightarrow N(0,\sigma^2),\] where \(\sigma^2=\operatorname{Var}(h(x_*,\xi))<\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a regular smooth SAA problem, the optimal value has the same first-order Gaussian fluctuation as the sample objective evaluated at the true optimizer.
assumptions_latex: \(x_*\) is the unique interior minimizer and \(\nabla^2f(x_*)\succ0\).
\(\operatorname{Var}(h(x_*,\xi))<\infty\).
Local stochastic equicontinuity yields \(x_n-x_*=O_p(n^{-1/2})\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sqrt n\,(v_n-v)\Rightarrow N(0,\operatorname{Var}(h(x_*,\xi)))\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stated first-order optimal-value expansion is standard under suitable empirical-process conditions, but x_n is not explicitly introduced as a minimizer and the phrase 'usual local stochastic equicontinuity conditions' does not provide checkable sufficient hypotheses. Source alignment is required.

children.title: Solution Asymptotics
children.top_down_role: Large-sample behavior of SAA optimizers or solution sets.

knowledge_statements.title: Solution Asymptotics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Asymptotic normality of a smooth interior SAA minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x_n\) minimize \(f_n(x)=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^nh(x,\xi_i)\), and let \(x_*\) be the unique interior minimizer of \(f(x)=\mathbb E[h(x,\xi)]\). Suppose \(H=
abla^2f(x_*)\) is positive definite, differentiation and expectation interchange locally, and the empirical gradients admit a uniform linear expansion around \(x_*\). If \(\Sigma=\operatorname{Var}(
abla_xh(x_*,\xi))\) is finite, then \[\sqrt n\,(x_n-x_*)=-H^{-1} rac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{i=1}^n
abla_xh(x_*,\xi_i)+o_p(1)\Rightarrow N(0,H^{-1}\Sigma H^{-1}).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A regular empirical optimizer is asymptotically normal, with covariance obtained by sandwiching gradient noise between inverse population Hessians.
assumptions_latex: \(x_*\) is unique and interior, with \(H=\nabla^2f(x_*)\succ0\).
The empirical gradients have a uniform local linear expansion.
\(\Sigma=\operatorname{Var}(\nabla_xh(x_*,\xi))\) is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sqrt n\,(x_n-x_*)\Rightarrow N(0,H^{-1}\Sigma H^{-1})\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The sandwich-normal limit is standard, but iid sampling, consistency/localization, the gradient CLT, and the precise uniform expansion conditions are not fully stated or sourced.

children.title: Stationarity Asymptotics
children.top_down_role: Large-sample behavior of stationary points or stationarity residuals.

knowledge_statements.title: Stationarity Asymptotics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Asymptotic normality of a consistent root of the empirical stationarity equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(\psi(x)=\mathbb E[g(x,\xi)]\) and \(\psi_n(x)=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^ng(x,\xi_i)\). Let \(\psi(x_*)=0\), and let \(x_n\to_p x_*\) satisfy \(\psi_n(x_n)=o_p(n^{-1/2})\). If \(A=D\psi(x_*)\) is nonsingular, \(\psi_n\) is stochastically differentiable uniformly near \(x_*\), and \(B=\operatorname{Var}(g(x_*,\xi))\) is finite, then \[\sqrt n\,(x_n-x_*)=-A^{-1}\frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{i=1}^ng(x_*,\xi_i)+o_p(1)\Rightarrow N(0,A^{-1}A^{-T}).\] when \(B=I\); generally the covariance is \(A^{-1}BA^{-T}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A consistent approximate empirical stationary point is asymptotically normal when the population stationarity mapping has a nonsingular derivative.
assumptions_latex: \(A=D\psi(x_*)\) is nonsingular and the local expansion is uniform.
\(B=\operatorname{Var}(g(x_*,\xi))\) is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sqrt n\,(x_n-x_*)\Rightarrow N(0,A^{-1}BA^{-T})\).

notation.meaning: Jacobian of the population mapping at its root

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The estimating-equation limit and general covariance formula are standard, but iid sampling and sufficient conditions for the multivariate CLT and stochastic differentiability are not explicit. No source is supplied.

children.title: Solution-Stationarity Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Relationships between optimizer behavior plus stationary-point behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Solution-Stationarity Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local equivalence between solution error and stationarity residual under uniform strong convexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(U\subset\mathbb R^d\) be convex, and suppose each differentiable \(f_n\) is \(\mu\)-strongly convex on \(U\) with the same \(\mu>0\). If \(x_n\in U\) is the unique local minimizer satisfying \(
abla f_n(x_n)=0\), then every \(y_n\in U\) obeys \[\mu\lVert y_n-x_nVert\le \lVert
abla f_n(y_n)Vert.\] If, additionally, the gradients are uniformly \(L\)-Lipschitz on \(U\), then \[\mu\lVert y_n-x_nVert\le\lVert
abla f_n(y_n)Vert\le L\lVert y_n-x_nVert.\] Hence solution errors and stationarity residuals have the same stochastic order.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform strong convexity and gradient Lipschitzness make distance to the empirical optimizer equivalent to the stationarity residual.
assumptions_latex: \(U\) is convex and \(f_n\) is differentiable and uniformly \(\mu\)-strongly convex on \(U\).
\(\nabla f_n(x_n)=0\).
For two-sided equivalence, \(\nabla f_n\) is uniformly \(L\)-Lipschitz.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lVert\nabla f_n(y_n)\rVert=O_p(r_n)\) if and only if \(\lVert y_n-x_n\rVert=O_p(r_n)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The deterministic residual-distance inequalities are standard under the stated uniform curvature and Lipschitz bounds. However, r_n is undefined and the probabilistic equivalence lacks explicit quantification; the claim also has no citation.

children.title: Spurious-Stationarity Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Regimes where sample stationary points do not track population solutions.

knowledge_statements.title: Spurious-Stationarity Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stationarity alone does not imply local or global solution consistency in nonconvex SAA.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the deterministic objective \(f_n=f\) on \(\mathbb R\), where \(f(x)=(x^2-1)^2\). The sequence \(x_n=0\) satisfies \(f_n'(x_n)=0\) for every \(n\), so its stationarity residual is identically zero. However, \(f''(0)=-4<0\), and \(0\) is a strict local maximizer, while \(\operatorname*{argmin}f=\{-1,1\}\). Thus even exact empirical stationarity and perfect objective convergence do not imply convergence to solutions. Convexity, second-order sufficiency, stability, or an explicit branch-selection condition is required to exclude such stationary branches.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In a nonconvex problem, exact empirical stationary points can remain at a strict population maximum rather than approach any optimizer.
assumptions_latex: Only first-order stationarity is required.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f_n'(x_n)=0\) with \(x_n=0\), but \(\operatorname{dist}(x_n,\operatorname*{argmin}f)=1\) for all \(n\).

notation.meaning: empirical objective, here identical to the population objective

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The polynomial counterexample is correct and directly demonstrates spurious stationarity in the nonconvex setting, with an appropriate failure-boundary content kind. It nevertheless lacks cited or registered evidence.

knowledge_statements.title: Second-Order Asymptotics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratic second-order expansion of the optimized SAA objective around the population optimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the smooth interior assumptions for solution asymptotic normality, let \(H=\nabla^2f(x_*)\succ0\), \(Z_n=\sqrt n\,\nabla f_n(x_*)\), and let \(x_n\) minimize \(f_n\) locally near \(x_*\). If the empirical Hessians converge uniformly to \(H\) locally and third-order remainders are negligible, then \[n\bigl(f_n(x_n)-f_n(x_*)\bigr)=-\tfrac12 Z_n^{T}H^{-1}Z_n+o_p(1).\] Consequently, if \(Z_n\Rightarrow Z\sim N(0,\Sigma)\), then \[n\bigl(f_n(x_n)-f_n(x_*)\bigr)\Rightarrow-\tfrac12 Z^{T}H^{-1}Z.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Optimization contributes a second-order negative quadratic correction determined by the empirical gradient noise and inverse population Hessian.
assumptions_latex: \(x_*\) is interior and \(H=\nabla^2f(x_*)\succ0\).
Empirical Hessians converge uniformly to \(H\) near \(x_*\).
The local Taylor remainder is \(o_p(n^{-1})\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(n(f_n(x_n)-f_n(x_*))\Rightarrow-\tfrac12Z^TH^{-1}Z\).

notation.meaning: scaled empirical gradient at the population optimizer

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The negative quadratic correction is standard under a sufficiently uniform second-order stochastic expansion, but 'third-order remainders are negligible' is not a precise hypothesis and no source supports the exact formulation.

children.title: Nonsmooth Asymptotic Regimes
children.top_down_role: Large-sample behavior under kinks, set-valued derivatives, or active-set changes.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonsmooth Asymptotic Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sample-median asymptotics as a canonical nonsmooth SAA regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X_1,\ldots,X_n\) be iid with distribution function \(F\), and let \(m\) be the unique median. Define the nonsmooth SAA objective \(f_n(x)=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n|X_i-x|\), and choose any \(\hat m_n\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\mathbb R}f_n(x)\). If \(F\) is differentiable at \(m\), with density \(p(m)>0\), and \(F(m)=1/2\), then \[\sqrt n\,(\hat m_n-m)\Rightarrow N\!\left(0,\frac{1}{4p(m)^2}\right).\] Thus differentiability of individual losses is unnecessary; local distributional curvature replaces a classical Hessian.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The sample median is a nonsmooth SAA optimizer yet remains asymptotically normal when the population density is positive at the unique median.
assumptions_latex: \(X_i\) are iid and \(m\) is the unique median.
\(F(m)=1/2\) and \(F\) is differentiable at \(m\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sqrt n(\hat m_n-m)\Rightarrow N(0,[4p(m)^2]^{-1})\).

notation.meaning: sample median and empirical absolute-loss minimizer

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The sample-median limit is mathematically standard and is an appropriate theorem illustrating a nonsmooth asymptotic regime. No authoritative quantile-asymptotics citation or registered evidence is supplied.

children.title: Degenerate Asymptotic Regimes
children.top_down_role: Large-sample behavior under singular curvature or weak identification.

knowledge_statements.title: Degenerate Asymptotic Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of the usual root-sample-size Gaussian SAA approximation under second-order degeneracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(v(P)=\inf_{x\in X}P f_x\), let \(P_N\) be the empirical distribution of \(N\) independent observations from \(P\), and let \(v_N=v(P_N)\). If the first-order directional derivative satisfies \(v'_P(h)=0\) for every direction \(h\) in the support of the empirical-process limit, then the ordinary delta method yields only \(\sqrt N(v_N-v(P))\Rightarrow0\). Consequently, a nondegenerate limit requires a higher-order expansion and generally a faster normalization, such as \(N(v_N-v(P))\), whose limit need not be Gaussian. Root-sample-size normal confidence intervals are therefore unjustified without additional nondegeneracy assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When every relevant first-order perturbation vanishes, the usual root-sample-size Gaussian limit collapses; higher-order scaling and generally non-Gaussian limits are required.
assumptions_latex: \(P_N\) is based on independent observations and the empirical process has a weak limit.
\(v\) is directionally differentiable at \(P\).
\(v'_P\) vanishes on every direction supported by the limiting empirical process.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sqrt N(v_N-v(P))\Rightarrow0\), so first-order Gaussian inference is degenerate.

notation.meaning: directional derivative of the optimal-value functional at P

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role fits, but ordinary directional differentiability is insufficient for the asserted delta-method conclusion, and neither an N normalization nor a non-Gaussian higher-order limit follows without problem-specific second-order conditions. An authoritative asymptotic reference is required.

children.title: Active-Set Transition Regimes
children.top_down_role: Asymptotic effects of changing active constraints or local structural regimes.

knowledge_statements.title: Active-Set Transition Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local regime in which sample perturbations can change the active constraints or minimizing face.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a constrained population problem with solution \(x^*\), inequalities \(g_j(x)\leq0\), and multipliers \(\lambda_j^*\), define the active set by \(A(x^*)=\{j:g_j(x^*)=0\}\). An active-set transition regime occurs when there is an index \(j\in A(x^*)\) with \(\lambda_j^*=0\), or when the population objective has multiple minimizing faces meeting at \(x^*\). In that case arbitrarily small empirical perturbations can activate or deactivate \(j\), or select different faces. The local optimizer and optimal-value maps are then generally only directionally differentiable, and their limits are determined by a piecewise-linear or cone-constrained stochastic problem rather than one fixed KKT system.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A zero-multiplier active constraint or intersecting minimizing faces allow tiny sampling perturbations to switch active sets, producing piecewise or cone-constrained limits.
assumptions_latex: \(g_j\) and the population objective admit the local directional derivatives used in the KKT expansion.
\(x^*\) satisfies the population first-order optimality system.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The local solution map can switch KKT regimes and need not possess a single linear derivative.

notation.meaning: constraints active at the population solution
population KKT multiplier for constraint j

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition role fits, but a zero multiplier or intersecting minimizing faces alone does not guarantee that arbitrarily small empirical perturbations switch regimes. The claimed directional differentiability and cone-constrained limit also require explicit regularity and perturbation assumptions supported by a variational-asymptotics source.

children.title: Nonsmooth-Degenerate Interactions
children.top_down_role: Combined asymptotic effects of irregular geometry plus degeneracy.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonsmooth-Degenerate Interactions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Directional limit representation when nonsmoothness and first-order degeneracy occur simultaneously.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x^*\) minimize the population objective, let \(T\) be its feasible tangent cone, and suppose the local empirical criterion admits \(F_N(x^*+r_N^{-1}d)-F_N(x^*)=a_N^{-1}\{Z_N(d)+q(d)\}+o_p(a_N^{-1})\) uniformly on bounded subsets of \(T\), where \(Z_N\Rightarrow Z\), while \(q\) is nonzero, positively homogeneous, and possibly nondifferentiable. If the first-order smooth term vanishes, then every tight sequence \(r_N(\hat x_N-x^*)\) has limits among \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{d\in T}\{Z(d)+q(d)\}\). Thus degeneracy selects the scale, whereas nonsmoothness makes the limiting argmin potentially nonunique and non-Gaussian.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under a valid local expansion, degeneracy determines the normalization while the nonsmooth drift yields a cone-constrained, potentially nonunique and non-Gaussian argmin limit.
assumptions_latex: The displayed local expansion holds uniformly on bounded subsets of \(T\).
\(Z_N\Rightarrow Z\) in a topology supporting argmin convergence.
The scaled estimators are tight and the limiting objective is level-compact on \(T\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r_N(\hat x_N-x^*)\Rightarrow\operatorname*{argmin}_{d\in T}\{Z(d)+q(d)\}\) when the limiting argmin is almost surely unique.

notation.meaning: feasible tangent cone at the population solution

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation role matches the leaf, but weak convergence of the local process and level compactness alone do not establish the stated argmin limit; an appropriate epi-process topology, approximate-minimizer condition, and subsequence or uniqueness formulation are needed. The scaling interpretation also requires a source.

knowledge_statements.title: Lower-Bound Estimation Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Replication-based lower confidence bound for the expected SAA optimal value and hence the true optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For minimization, draw \(M\) independent batches of size \(N\). For batch \(m\), compute \(v_N^{(m)}=\inf_{x\in X}N^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^N F(x,\xi_{mi})\). Set \(\bar v_{N,M}=M^{-1}\sum_{m=1}^M v_N^{(m)}\) and \(s_{N,M}^2=(M-1)^{-1}\sum_{m=1}^M(v_N^{(m)}-\bar v_{N,M})^2\). Because \(\mathbb E[v_N^{(m)}]\leq v^*=\inf_{x\in X}\mathbb E[F(x,\xi)]\), output \(L=\bar v_{N,M}-t_{M-1,1-\alpha}s_{N,M}/\sqrt M\). Under the usual Studentized replication approximation, \(L\) is a one-sided lower confidence bound for \(v^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve independent SAA replications, average their optimal values, and subtract a Studentized margin; downward bias makes the result a lower bound for the true optimum.
assumptions_latex: The \(M\) batches are mutually independent and identically distributed.
Each replicated optimal value is measurable with finite, nonzero variance.
The Studentized replication approximation is adequate for the selected \(M\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb P\{L\leq v^*\}\approx1-\alpha\).

knowledge_statements.title: Candidate-Solution Upper-Bound Estimation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Independent evaluation bound for the objective value of a fixed candidate in a minimization problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\hat x\in X\) be selected without using an evaluation sample \(\xi'_1,\ldots,\xi'_n\). Compute \(\bar F_n(\hat x)=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^nF(\hat x,\xi'_i)\) and \(s_n^2=(n-1)^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n(F(\hat x,\xi'_i)-\bar F_n(\hat x))^2\). Output \(U=\bar F_n(\hat x)+t_{n-1,1-\alpha}s_n/\sqrt n\). Since \(v^*=\inf_{x\in X}\mathbb E[F(x,\xi)]\leq\mathbb E[F(\hat x,\xi)]\), a valid one-sided upper confidence bound for the candidate mean is also an upper bound for \(v^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Evaluate a previously selected candidate on fresh data and add a one-sided confidence margin; its mean objective upper-bounds the minimization optimum.
assumptions_latex: The evaluation observations are independent of the data used to select \(\hat x\).
Conditional on \(\hat x\), the evaluation losses are identically distributed with finite, nonzero variance.

knowledge_statements.title: Optimality-Gap Confidence Intervals
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-sided confidence certificate for the gap of an independently evaluated candidate solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(v^*\) be the minimum population value and \(G(\hat x)=\mathbb E[F(\hat x,\xi)]-v^*\geq0\). Suppose random bounds \(U\) and \(L\) are constructed so that \(\mathbb P\{\mathbb E[F(\hat x,\xi)]\leq U\}\geq1-\alpha_U\) and \(\mathbb P\{L\leq v^*\}\geq1-\alpha_L\). Then \(C=[0,\max\{0,U-L\}]\) is a verifiable one-sided confidence set for the gap satisfying \(\mathbb P\{G(\hat x)\in C\}\geq1-\alpha_U-\alpha_L\). The guarantee follows from simultaneous validity and does not require independence between \(U\) and \(L\).

knowledge_statements.title: Selection Bias
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimism caused by selecting and evaluating a candidate on the same sample.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\hat\mu_j=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^nY_{ij}\) estimate \(\mu_j=\mathbb E[Y_{1j}]\) for \(j=1,\ldots,K\), and select \(\hat j\in\operatorname*{argmin}_j
otag \hat\mu_j\). Even when every \(\hat\mu_j\) is unbiased, \(\mathbb E[\hat\mu_{\hat j}]\leq\min_j\mu_j\), with strict inequality whenever sampling noise can change the selected index and the estimators are nondegenerate. Thus the same-sample estimate \(\hat\mu_{\hat j}\) is optimistically biased for \(\mu_{\hat j}\); an ordinary fixed-candidate confidence interval need not cover after selection. Independent evaluation or selection-adjusted inference is required.

knowledge_statements.title: Multiple-Comparison Effects
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Simultaneous error inflation when many candidate-wise confidence statements are inspected.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For candidates \(j=1,\ldots,K\), let \(C_j\) satisfy the marginal guarantee \(\mathbb P
otag\{\theta_j\notin C_j\}\leq\alpha_j\). Regardless of dependence, the simultaneous coverage obeys \[\mathbb P
otag\{\theta_j\in C_j\text{ for every }j\}\geq1-\sum_{j=1}^K\alpha_j.\] Consequently, using unadjusted level \(1-\alpha\) intervals for all candidates permits familywise error as large as \(K\alpha\) under the union bound. Setting \(\alpha_j=\alpha/K\) yields Bonferroni simultaneous coverage at least \(1-\alpha\), and any interval chosen after inspecting all \(K\) comparisons inherits this multiplicity issue.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Inspecting many marginal intervals inflates the chance of at least one error; Bonferroni allocation restores simultaneous coverage without dependence assumptions.
assumptions_latex: There are \(K<\infty\) candidate-specific confidence sets.
Each marginal noncoverage probability is at most its assigned \(\alpha_j\).

knowledge_statements.title: Continuous Decision-Set Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform SAA deviation over a compact metric decision set using covering numbers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \((X,d)\) be compact and let \(F(x)=\mathbb E[f(x,\xi)]\) and \(F_N(x)=N^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^N f(x,\xi_i)\), where the samples are independent. Suppose \(f(\cdot,\xi)\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz almost surely and \(f(x,\xi)-F(x)\) is \(\sigma\)-sub-Gaussian for every \(x\in X\). \(f(\cdot,\xi)\) is almost surely \(L\)-Lipschitz.

children.title: Heavy-Tailed SAA Regimes

knowledge_statements.title: Heavy-Tailed SAA Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polynomial SAA concentration and failure of exponential deviation under moment-only tails.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(1<p\le2\), let \(Y=f(x,\xi)\), and suppose \(\mathbb E|Y-\mathbb EY|^p<\infty\). For independent copies, a constant \(C_p\) gives
\[\mathbb P\!\left\{\left|N^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^N Y_i-\mathbb EY\right|>\varepsilon\right\}\le \frac{C_p\mathbb E|Y-\mathbb EY|^p}{N^{p-1}\varepsilon^p}.\]
Moment finiteness alone cannot imply an exponential bound: if a nonnegative \(Y\) has \(\mathbb P(Y>t)\asymp t^{-\alpha}\) with \(\alpha>p\), then for fixed \(\varepsilon>0\) the sample-mean deviation probability is bounded below at polynomial order through the event \(\max_iY_i>N(\mathbb EY+\varepsilon)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite low-order moments give polynomial sample-mean concentration. Pareto-type observations show that exponential SAA deviation cannot follow from moment assumptions alone.
assumptions_latex: \(1<p\le2\) and the observations are independent.
\(\mathbb E|Y-\mathbb EY|^p<\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Moment-only SAA admits polynomial concentration but no general exponential-deviation guarantee.

notation.meaning: power-law tail exponent in the counterfamily

review_flags: A source for the moment inequality and the heavy-tail lower-bound mechanism is not present among the supplied locators.

children.title: Robustified SAA Regimes
children.top_down_role: SAA variants designed to reduce sensitivity to extreme observations.

knowledge_statements.title: Robustified SAA Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Median-of-means replacement for the ordinary sample-average objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given decisions \(X\), observations \(\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_N\), and an integer \(K\le N\), partition the indices into nonempty blocks \(B_1,\ldots,B_K\). For each \(x\in X\), compute
\[M_k(x)=|B_k|^{-1}\sum_{i\in B_k}f(x,\xi_i),\qquad \widehat F_{\mathrm{MOM}}(x)=\operatorname{median}_{1\le k\le K}M_k(x).\]
Return any \(\widehat x\in X\) satisfying \(\widehat F_{\mathrm{MOM}}(\widehat x)\le\inf_{x\in X}\widehat F_{\mathrm{MOM}}(x)+\eta\). The stopping tolerance is \(\eta\ge0\); the block count controls resistance to contaminated or heavy-tailed observations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partition observations, compute one sample objective per block, minimize their pointwise median, and stop at a prescribed optimization tolerance.
assumptions_latex: The loss values are measurable and each block mean is finite.
The robustified objective admits an \(\eta\)-approximate minimizer over \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat x\) is an \(\eta\)-approximate minimizer of the median-of-means objective.
review_flags: The supplied locators do not document median-of-means stochastic optimization.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The median-of-means construction fits the robustified-SAA algorithm leaf. A source is required, and the median convention should be specified when the block count is even.

children.title: Tail-Truncation Regimes
children.top_down_role: Approximation settings using clipped or truncated tail contributions.

knowledge_statements.title: Tail-Truncation Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bias–concentration decomposition for clipped heavy-tailed SAA over a finite decision set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\) be finite and suppose \(Y_x=f(x,\xi)\) satisfies \(\sup_{x\in X}\mathbb E|Y_x|^p\le M_p\) for some \(p>1\). Define \(T_\tau(y)=\max\{-\tau,\min\{y,\tau\}\}\) and \(F_{N,\tau}(x)=N^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^NT_\tau(f(x,\xi_i))\). Then
\[\sup_{x\in X}|\mathbb E T_\tau(Y_x)-\mathbb EY_x|\le M_p\tau^{1-p},\]
and, for every \(t>0\),
\[\mathbb P\!\left\{\sup_{x\in X}|F_{N,\tau}(x)-\mathbb ET_\tau(Y_x)|>t\right\}\le2|X|\exp\!\left(-\frac{Nt^2}{2\tau^2}\right).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Clipping produces deterministic tail bias but restores bounded-loss exponential concentration; the threshold balances these two errors.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is finite and the observations are independent.
For some \(p>1\), \(\sup_{x\in X}\mathbb E|f(x,\xi)|^p\le M_p\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The total uniform error is controlled by truncation bias \(M_p\tau^{1-p}\) plus a bounded-variable deviation term.

notation.meaning: two-sided clipping operator at threshold tau

review_flags: No supplied source locator supports this truncation bias and concentration decomposition.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The clipping bias and finite-family concentration bounds fit the tail-truncation leaf, but no inspectable citation supports their precise constants and hypotheses.

children.title: Robustness-Efficiency Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Accuracy, conservatism, plus sample-efficiency consequences of robustification.

knowledge_statements.title: Robustness-Efficiency Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tuning tradeoff between tail robustness, bias, and sampling efficiency.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For clipped SAA under the moment condition \(\sup_x\mathbb E|f(x,\xi)|^p\le M_p\), a confidence level \(1-\delta\) yields the generic uniform error proxy
\[R_N(\tau)=M_p\tau^{1-p}+\tau\sqrt{\frac{2\log(2|X|/\delta)}{N}}.\]
Increasing \(\tau\) decreases truncation bias but increases sampling deviation. Balancing the two terms gives
\[\tau\asymp\left(\frac{M_p\sqrt N}{\sqrt{\log(2|X|/\delta)}}\right)^{1/p},\qquad R_N(\tau)\asymp M_p^{1/p}\left(\frac{\log(2|X|/\delta)}{N}\right)^{(p-1)/(2p)},\]
up to constants depending only on \(p\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: More aggressive clipping improves concentration but increases bias. Balancing the two terms determines a moment- and confidence-dependent threshold.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is finite and \(\sup_x\mathbb E|f(x,\xi)|^p\le M_p\) for some \(p>1\).
The clipped empirical objective is formed from independent observations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed choice of \(\tau\) balances robustness bias and sampling efficiency up to \(p\)-dependent constants.
review_flags: The balancing calculation is standard but the supplied locators do not support this heavy-tail tradeoff.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The bias–deviation balancing principle fits the tradeoff leaf and its rate calculation is plausible, but it lacks a source and does not explicitly require a valid confidence parameter such as 0<δ<1.

knowledge_statements.title: Multistage SAA Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scenario-tree size growth for stagewise branching multistage SAA.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider a \(T\)-stage SAA tree in which every node at stage \(t-1\) has \(b_t\) sampled children for \(t=2,\ldots,T\). The number of leaf scenarios and total tree nodes are
\[L_T=\prod_{t=2}^T b_t,\qquad V_T=1+\sum_{s=2}^T\prod_{t=2}^s b_t.\]
Any explicit deterministic equivalent containing at least one distinct recourse block per tree node requires \(\Omega(V_T)\) stored blocks and node evaluations. If \(b_t=b\ge2\), then \(L_T=b^{T-1}\) and \(V_T=(b^T-1)/(b-1)\), so explicit-tree size is exponential in the number of stages.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stagewise branching multiplies leaf scenarios. An explicit multistage deterministic equivalent therefore has node and storage complexity exponential in the horizon.
assumptions_latex: The scenario tree branches independently with prescribed integers \(b_t\ge1\).
The deterministic equivalent represents a separate recourse block at every tree node.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Explicit representation requires \(\Omega(V_T)\) resources and becomes exponential in \(T\) under constant branching \(b\ge2\).
review_flags: The supplied decision-tree locators are relevant context but do not directly certify this complexity statement.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The scenario-tree counts and explicit-representation lower bound fit a multistage complexity record, but the cited inventory is not attached and does not directly establish the Ω(V_T) resource claim.

knowledge_statements.title: Independent Holdout Evaluation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional performance certificate using data independent of SAA model selection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\widehat x\) be any decision measurable with respect to training data, and let \(\zeta_1,\ldots,\zeta_m\) be an independent holdout sample. If \(a\le f(x,\zeta)\le b\) almost surely for every admissible \(x\), define \(\widehat F_H(\widehat x)=m^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^m f(\widehat x,\zeta_j)\). Conditional on the training data, with probability at least \(1-\delta\),
\[|\widehat F_H(\widehat x)-F(\widehat x)|\le(b-a)\sqrt{\frac{\log(2/\delta)}{2m}}.\]
Thus the displayed interval is a verifiable holdout certificate for the true expected performance of the selected decision.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An untouched bounded holdout sample gives a valid confidence interval for the true performance of a training-selected decision.
assumptions_latex: The holdout observations are independent of the training data and identically distributed with the target uncertainty.
The loss lies almost surely in \([a,b]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \([\widehat F_H(\widehat x)\pm(b-a)\sqrt{\log(2/\delta)/(2m)}]\) covers \(F(\widehat x)\) with conditional probability at least \(1-\delta\).
review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports independent holdout certification for a data-selected SAA decision.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The conditional Hoeffding interval fits the certificate role for independent holdout evaluation, but no source is cited and the domains m≥1 and 0<δ<1 are not explicit.

children.title: Bootstrap Validation
children.top_down_role: Bootstrap-based assessment of SAA solutions, objectives, or optimality gaps.

knowledge_statements.title: Bootstrap Validation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonparametric bootstrap approximation of an SAA validation statistic’s sampling distribution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given observations \(Z_1,ldots,Z_N\), their empirical law \(P_N\), a statistic \(T\), and replication count \(B\), repeat for \(b=1,\ldots,B\): draw \(N\) observations independently from \(P_N\), form \(P_N^{*(b)}\), and compute
\[W_b^*=\sqrt N\bigl(T(P_N^{*(b)})-T(P_N)\bigr).\]
Let \(q^*_{\gamma}\) be the empirical \(\gamma\)-quantile of \(\{W_b^*\}_{b=1}^B\). Output the basic interval
\[\left[T(P_N)-\frac{q^*_{1-\alpha/2}}{\sqrt N},\ T(P_N)-\frac{q^*_{\alpha/2}}{\sqrt N}\right].\]
Asymptotic validity requires bootstrap consistency for \(T\), rather than resampling alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly resample the empirical distribution, recompute the statistic, and use centered bootstrap quantiles to form a validation interval.
assumptions_latex: The observations are identically distributed and suitable for nonparametric resampling.
The statistic \(T\) is bootstrap-consistent under the data-generating law.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The algorithm outputs a basic bootstrap interval with nominal level \(1-\alpha\).
review_flags: No supplied source locator covers bootstrap validity or this interval construction.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The bootstrap procedure fits the algorithm leaf, but the opening data sequence contains the malformed text “ldots,” and nominal coverage is only asymptotic under the stated consistency premise. A source is required to verify the validity conditions and interval construction.

children.title: Subsampling Validation
