children.title: Nonconvex Scenario Problems
children.top_down_role: Scenario subproblems with discrete or other nonconvex structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonconvex Scenario Problems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-scenario extensive form with scenario-wise nonconvexity and linear nonanticipativity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(S\) be finite, let \(p_s>0\) with \(\sum_{s\in S}p_s=1\), and let \(C_s\subseteq X_s\). The scenario formulation is
\[v_P=\inf\left\{F(x):=\sum_{s\in S}p_s f_s(x_s)\;\middle|\;x\in C\cap N\right\},\qquad C:=\prod_{s\in S}C_s,\]
where \(N\) is the linear subspace imposing equality of decisions having the same observed history. It is a nonconvex scenario problem when at least one restricted function \(f_s+\delta_{C_s}\) is nonconvex; consequently, the extensive-form objective or feasible set need not be convex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A scenario problem is nonconvex when some scenario objective or feasible set is nonconvex, even though nonanticipativity remains a linear consensus constraint.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) is finite and every \(p_s\) is positive.
Each \(f_s:X_s\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) is proper.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists s\in S:\ f_s+\delta_{C_s}\text{ is nonconvex}\).

notation.meaning: Cartesian product of scenario feasible sets

children.title: Dual-Bound Interpretation
children.top_down_role: Scope of dual certificates when primal recovery or exactness is unavailable.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual-Bound Interpretation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weak Lagrangian duality for nonanticipativity relaxation, without convexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F(x)=\sum_{s\in S}p_s(f_s(x_s)+\delta_{C_s}(x_s))\), and let \(N^\perp\) be the orthogonal complement of the nonanticipativity subspace. For every multiplier \(w\in N^\perp\), define
\[q(w):=\inf_x\{F(x)+\langle w,x\rangle\}.\]
Because \(\langle w,x\rangle=0\) for every \(x\in N\), weak duality gives \(q(w)\le v_P\), irrespective of convexity. Hence \(v_D:=\sup_{w\in N^\perp}q(w)\) is a valid lower bound for the minimization problem, although \(v_D=v_P\) need not hold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every nonanticipativity multiplier yields a valid lower bound, but maximizing those bounds may still leave a positive nonconvex duality gap.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is proper and the primal feasible set intersects its effective domain.
The pairing defining \(N^\perp\) is the probability-weighted product-space pairing.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q(w)\le v_D\le v_P\) for every \(w\in N^\perp\).

children.title: Primal-Recovery Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Limits on converting dual solutions into feasible high-quality primal policies.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Recovery Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limits of recovering a globally optimal nonanticipative solution from dual scenario minimizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(w^\star\in N^\perp\) maximizes the dual function and \(x^\star\in\arg\min_x\{F(x)+\langle w^\star,x\rangle\}\). Dual optimality alone does not imply \(x^\star\in N\). If \(x^\star\notin N\), its scenario components do not constitute a primal solution; moreover, the consensus projection \(P_Nx^\star\) may leave the nonconvex product set \(C\) or increase the objective. Direct recovery is guaranteed only when a selected dual minimizer is nonanticipative and feasible. If \(v_D<v_P\), no dual minimizer can simultaneously be primal feasible and attain the dual value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dual optimizer recovers a primal optimizer only through a feasible nonanticipative minimizing selection; projection can fail under nonconvex scenario constraints.
assumptions_latex: The primal and dual optimal values are finite.
A dual maximizer and an associated Lagrangian minimizer exist.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^\star\in C\cap N\Rightarrow F(x^\star)=v_P=v_D\); thus \(v_D<v_P\Rightarrow x^\star\notin C\cap N\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary statement is mathematically plausible, but the cited general dual-decomposition section does not clearly support the specific nonconvex projection and primal-recovery claims. A direct locator on nonconvex dual recovery or progressive-hedging recovery limitations is required.

knowledge_statements.title: Scenario Consensus Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weighted Hilbert-space representation of nonanticipativity and scenario consensus.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Equip \(X=\prod_{s\in S}X_s\) with \(\langle x,y\rangle_p=\sum_{s\in S}p_s\langle x_s,y_s\rangle\). The nonanticipativity set \(N\) consists of scenario vectors whose decisions agree whenever the corresponding scenarios share the relevant information history. For an information bundle \(B\subseteq S\), the orthogonal projection is the conditional weighted average
\[(P_Nx)_s=\frac{\sum_{r\in B}p_r x_r}{\sum_{r\in B}p_r},\qquad s\in B.\]
Thus \(x=P_Nx+(I-P_N)x\), with consensus component in \(N\) and disagreement residual in \(N^\perp\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonanticipativity is a weighted consensus subspace; projection averages decisions within each common-history bundle and separates consensus from disagreement.
assumptions_latex: All scenario decision spaces in a bundle are identified with one Hilbert space.
Every information bundle has positive total probability.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_Nx\in N\), \((I-P_N)x\in N^\perp\), and \(x=P_Nx+(I-P_N)x\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The weighted projection representation is standard and fits the geometry container, but the cited individual-scenario-problems locator does not clearly support the Hilbert-space orthogonal decomposition and history-bundle projection formula.

children.title: Augmented-Lagrangian Interpretation
children.top_down_role: Progressive hedging viewed through penalized nonanticipativity dualization.

knowledge_statements.title: Augmented-Lagrangian Interpretation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Progressive-hedging scenario solves as separable augmented-Lagrangian minimizations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F(x)=\sum_{s\in S}p_s(f_s(x_s)+\delta_{C_s}(x_s))\), let \(z^k=P_Nx^k\), and let \(w^k\in N^\perp\). With \(\rho>0\), the progressive-hedging scenario step selects
\[x^{k+1}\in\arg\min_x\left\{F(x)+\langle w^k,x\rangle_p+\frac{\rho}{2}\lVert x-z^k\rVert_p^2\right\}.\]
The objective separates by scenario, while the multiplier update
\[w^{k+1}=w^k+\rho(x^{k+1}-P_Nx^{k+1})\]
accumulates nonanticipativity violations. These are block minimization and dual-ascent operations for the quadratically augmented nonanticipativity formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Progressive hedging minimizes a separable quadratic augmented Lagrangian and updates multipliers by the remaining scenario disagreement.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a probability-weighted Hilbert product space.
Each displayed scenario subproblem attains a minimizer.
\(w^0\in N^\perp\) and \(\rho>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^{k+1}\) is an augmented-Lagrangian minimizer at consensus \(z^k\), and \(w^{k+1}\in N^\perp\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The formulas describe the standard progressive-hedging update, but identifying them as augmented-Lagrangian block minimization and dual ascent requires a progressive-hedging or operator-splitting source. The cited generic dual-decomposition section is insufficiently direct.

children.title: Proximal Interpretation
children.top_down_role: Progressive hedging viewed through proximal splitting or regularized scenario updates.

knowledge_statements.title: Proximal Interpretation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Completed-square form of each progressive-hedging scenario update.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define \(g_s=f_s+\delta_{C_s}\). For fixed consensus point \(z_s^k\), multiplier \(w_s^k\), and \(\rho>0\), completing the square gives
\[\arg\min_u\left\{g_s(u)+\langle w_s^k,u\rangle+\frac{\rho}{2}\lVert u-z_s^k\rVert^2\right\}=\operatorname{prox}_{g_s/\rho}\left(z_s^k-\frac{w_s^k}{\rho}\right),\]
where the proximal mapping denotes the complete set of minimizers when it is not single-valued. Thus each exact scenario update is a proximal evaluation at a consensus point shifted by the scaled nonanticipativity multiplier.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each exact scenario solve is a proximal step centered at consensus minus the scaled scenario multiplier.
assumptions_latex: The scenario space is Hilbert and uses the same quadratic metric as the penalty.
The displayed minimizer set is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_s^{k+1}\in\operatorname{prox}_{g_s/\rho}(z_s^k-w_s^k/\rho)\).

notation.meaning: scenario objective including its feasibility indicator

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The completed-square proximal identity is correct with the stated set-valued convention and metric assumptions, and representation is the right kind. The cited dual-decomposition locator does not directly substantiate this proximal interpretation.

children.title: Interpretation Equivalence Regimes
children.top_down_role: Settings where the dual and proximal views describe the same decomposition structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Interpretation Equivalence Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditions under which augmented-Lagrangian and proximal descriptions produce identical scenario updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The augmented-Lagrangian and proximal interpretations are update-equivalent when: \(X\) is a Hilbert product space; the penalty is the squared norm generated by its inner product; the same \(\rho>0\), consensus point, and multiplier are used; and scenario subproblems are solved exactly. Under these conditions, for every scenario \(s\),
\[\arg\min_u\left\{g_s(u)+\langle w_s,u\rangle+\frac{\rho}{2}\lVert u-z_s\rVert^2\right\}=\operatorname{prox}_{g_s/\rho}(z_s-w_s/\rho).\]
If \(g_s\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex, this proximal mapping is single-valued whenever the ambient space is finite-dimensional or standard existence conditions hold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The two interpretations coincide with a shared Hilbert metric, quadratic penalty, parameters, and exact solves; convexity additionally makes the update well behaved.
assumptions_latex: Each scenario minimizer set is nonempty.
All terms use one common Hilbert-space metric.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Argmin}_{\mathrm{AL},s}=\operatorname{prox}_{g_s/\rho}(z_s-w_s/\rho)\) for every \(s\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: completing the square yields the stated minimizer-set identity

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition record gives a standard minimizer-set identity and appropriate equivalence regime, but it has no inspectable citation. An authoritative proximal-analysis or progressive-hedging source is required.

children.title: Interpretation Breakdown Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Nonconvex, inexact, or nonstandard settings where classical equivalences weaken.

knowledge_statements.title: Interpretation Breakdown Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failures of the standard proximal equivalence or its single-valued operator reading.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The shifted-proximal identity with center \(z-w/\rho\) ceases to describe the implemented update if the quadratic penalty is replaced by a nonquadratic divergence, if its metric differs from the multiplier pairing without the corresponding metric inverse, or if the scenario solve is inexact. Even with the standard quadratic penalty, a nonconvex \(g_s\) can make \(\operatorname{prox}_{g_s/\rho}\) empty or set-valued. For example, \(g(u)=\min\{(u-1)^2,(u+1)^2\}\) has two proximal minimizers at center zero for suitable positive \(\rho\); therefore a unique resolvent iteration and convex-operator convergence interpretation are unavailable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonquadratic metrics, inconsistent pairings, inexact solves, or nonconvex set-valued proximal maps break the standard equivalence or convergence interpretation.
assumptions_latex: The claimed standard interpretation uses the Euclidean or Hilbert squared norm.
No deterministic selection rule is imposed on multiple minimizers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g\text{ nonconvex}\Rightarrow\operatorname{prox}_{g/\rho}\text{ need not be single-valued}\), so operator-level equivalence can fail.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: nonconvex proximal maps may be set-valued and nonquadratic penalties do not admit the stated completed-square form

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The breakdown distinctions and nonconvex two-minimizer example are plausible and fit a failure-boundary leaf, but no source supports the generalized-metric, inexact-solve, emptiness, or operator-convergence claims.

knowledge_statements.title: Multistage Progressive Hedging
knowledge_statements.scope_note: History-wise progressive hedging on a finite multistage scenario tree.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given path probabilities \(p_s\), scenario-feasible sets \(C_s\), penalty \(\rho>0\), initial \(x^0\), and \(w^0\in N^\perp\), repeat
\[z^k=P_Nx^k,\qquad x_s^{k+1}\in\arg\min_{x_s\in C_s}\left\{f_s(x_s)+\langle w_s^k,x_s\rangle+\frac{\rho}{2}\lVert x_s-z_s^k\rVert^2\right\},\]
\[z^{k+1}=P_Nx^{k+1},\qquad w^{k+1}=w^k+\rho(x^{k+1}-z^{k+1}).\]
At every stage, \(P_N\) averages decisions over scenarios sharing that stage's history. Stop when the primal residual \(\lVert x^{k+1}-z^{k+1}\rVert_p\) and a prescribed successive-consensus residual meet their tolerances; output \(z^{k+1}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multistage progressive hedging alternates scenario-path optimization, history-wise conditional averaging, and multiplier updates until consensus residuals are small.
assumptions_latex: The scenario tree and its information bundles are finite.
Each scenario subproblem is solved to the stipulated accuracy.
Initial multipliers satisfy history-wise weighted zero-sum conditions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z^{k+1}\in N\) and \(w^{k+1}\in N^\perp\) at every iteration.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The content kind and finite-tree iteration fit the multistage progressive-hedging container, but the algorithm, history-wise projection, invariant, and stopping rule lack an authoritative citation.

children.title: Primal Warm Starts
children.top_down_role: Reuse of prior scenario primal solutions as initialization data.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal Warm Starts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Initialization of progressive hedging from precomputed scenario decisions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given reusable scenario decisions \(\widehat x_s\in C_s\), initialize \(x_s^0=\widehat x_s\) and compute the consistent consensus state \(z^0=P_Nx^0\). If only a candidate nonanticipative policy \(\widehat z\in N\) is available, initialize each scenario subproblem from \(\widehat z_s\), but retain a scenario-feasible iterate only after enforcing \(C_s\). The first progressive-hedging update uses \(z^0\) as its quadratic center. A primal warm start need not itself be nonanticipative, but its projected consensus and scenario components must use the current scenario probabilities, history bundles, variable scaling, and feasibility model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reuse scenario-feasible primal decisions, recompute their current consensus projection, and use it as the first quadratic center.
assumptions_latex: Stored and current scenario variables have a defined compatible mapping.
Projection uses the current probabilities and information structure.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^0\in\prod_s C_s\) and \(z^0=P_Nx^0\in N\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: initialization must preserve scenario feasibility and recompute consensus under the active projection

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The initialization procedure fits the primal-warm-start leaf, but its feasibility-restoration and state-compatibility requirements are implementation claims without an inspectable source.

children.title: Dual Warm Starts
children.top_down_role: Reuse of prior multipliers, dual estimates, or related certificate state.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Warm Starts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Admissibility condition for reused progressive-hedging multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A reused multiplier vector \(\widehat w\) is an admissible dual warm start precisely when it lies in the orthogonal complement of the current nonanticipativity space. Thus initialize
\[w^0=P_{N^\perp}\widehat w=(I-P_N)\widehat w.\]
Equivalently, for every information bundle \(B\), the probability-weighted multiplier sum must vanish:
\[\sum_{s\in B}p_s w_s^0=0.\]
This projection is required whenever scenario probabilities, bundle membership, variable scaling, or the scenario set has changed. With this initialization, subsequent updates by disagreement residuals preserve \(w^k\in N^\perp\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Project reused multipliers onto the current disagreement subspace; equivalently, their weighted sum must vanish within every history bundle.
assumptions_latex: Stored multipliers are mapped into the current product space.
The current weighted consensus projection is available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(w^0\in N^\perp\Longleftrightarrow P_Nw^0=0\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: admissible equality-constraint multipliers lie in the orthogonal complement of consensus

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Orthogonal projection gives an admissible multiplier state in the stated Hilbert representation, but the multistage bundle-wise equivalence and mandatory reprojection conditions require a direct algorithmic source.

children.title: Scenario-State Reuse
children.top_down_role: Retention of solver state, factorizations, bases, or search structures across iterations.

knowledge_statements.title: Scenario-State Reuse
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safe transfer of primal, consensus, and multiplier state between related scenario solves.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(T_s\) map stored scenario variables into the current model. For every compatible scenario, set \(\widetilde x_s=T_sx_s^{\mathrm{old}}\) and \(\widetilde w_s=T_sw_s^{\mathrm{old}}\); initialize new or incompatible scenarios by the prescribed cold-start rule. Restore feasibility scenario-wise to obtain \(x^0\in\prod_s C_s\), then recompute
\[z^0=P_Nx^0,\qquad w^0=P_{N^\perp}\widetilde w.\]
Do not reuse stored consensus averages or multipliers without these projections when probabilities or information bundles changed. The reusable state is therefore the mapped scenario state, while current consensus and dual admissibility are reconstructed from the current model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Map compatible scenario states, cold-start unmatched scenarios, restore feasibility, and recompute both consensus and admissible multipliers under the current model.
assumptions_latex: Each reused scenario has an explicit variable and history mapping.
The current feasibility sets, probabilities, and information bundles are known.
Feasibility restoration is available for mapped primal states.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^0\in\prod_s C_s\), \(z^0\in N\), and \(w^0\in N^\perp\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: changed probabilities or scenario mappings require reconstruction of projected state

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The safe-reuse workflow fits the leaf, but using the same map for primal variables and multipliers is not generally justified under rescaling or coordinate changes; dual states may require a distinct adjoint-compatible transformation. A source and precise mapping assumptions are required.

children.title: Stale-State Failure Modes
children.top_down_role: Performance or reliability losses caused by obsolete reused scenario information.

assumptions_latex: The scenario set is finite, with probabilities \(p_s>0\) satisfying \(\sum_s p_s=1\).
The current run uses penalty \(\rho>0\), scenario states \(x_s^k\), consensus state \(\bar x^k\), and multipliers \(w_s^k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A reused state is admissible only when it is synchronized with the current scenarios, probabilities, model, penalty convention, and iteration index; otherwise the resulting update is not an iteration of the intended progressive-hedging map.

notation.meaning: Scenario probability in the current run.
Scenario primal state and probability-weighted consensus state.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational failure boundary for reusing progressive-hedging state across runs or iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S_k\), \(p^k\), \(f_s^k\), and \(\rho_k\) denote the scenario set, probabilities, scenario objectives, and penalty convention at iteration \(k\). A state \((x_s^j,w_s^j,\bar x^j)\) is stale for iteration \(k\) if \(j\ne k\), or if any of \(S_j\), \(p^j\), \(f_s^j\), or \(\rho_j\) differs from its current counterpart without an explicit state transformation. In particular, retaining \(w_s^j\) after changing probabilities can violate \(\sum_{s\in S_k}p_s^k w_s^j=0\). Using a stale state in the scenario minimizations or multiplier update therefore applies a different iteration map and invalidates convergence or residual interpretations attached to the current progressive-hedging run.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A state becomes stale when its iteration, scenarios, probabilities, model, or penalty convention differs from the current run; untransformed reuse can break multiplier invariants and convergence diagnostics.
knowledge_statements.title: Stale-State Failure Modes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The leaf and failure_boundary kind fit, but declaring every state with j≠k stale is not generally valid: an iteration normally consumes state from an earlier indexed step, and restart compatibility depends on the precise update convention. The probability-weighted multiplier invariant and required transformations need a progressive-hedging state-reuse source.

assumptions_latex: The scenario space is finite and \(p_s>0\) for every scenario \(s\).
Each scenario objective is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex on a nonempty closed convex scenario set.
The nonanticipative deterministic-equivalent problem has at least one finite minimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: These hypotheses define the closed convex regime in which progressive hedging is covered by convex primal-dual splitting theory.

notation.meaning: Scenario feasible set in a finite-dimensional Hilbert space.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-scenario, finite-dimensional convex regime underlying standard progressive-hedging convergence results.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H=\prod_{s\in S}\mathbb R^{n_s}\) carry the probability-weighted inner product, let \(C=\prod_{s\in S}C_s\), and let \(N\subseteq H\) be the closed linear subspace expressing nonanticipativity. The closed convex scenario-problem regime holds when every \(C_s\) is nonempty, closed, and convex; every \(f_s:\mathbb R^{n_s}\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex; and the problem \[\min_{x\in C\cap N}\;F(x),\qquad F(x)=\sum_{s\in S}p_s f_s(x_s),\] has a nonempty solution set and finite optimal value. Integrality restrictions or other nonconvex scenario sets lie outside this regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The standard convex regime requires closed convex scenario sets, proper lower-semicontinuous convex objectives, a linear nonanticipativity subspace, and existence of a finite optimal solution.
knowledge_statements.title: Closed Convex Scenario-Problem Regime

assumptions_latex: The closed convex scenario-problem conditions hold.
A qualification condition ensures strong duality for the constraint \(x\in N\), and a primal minimizer exists.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The regime is characterized by a saddle point \((x^\star,w^\star)\), equivalently by primal feasibility, dual feasibility, and the displayed subdifferential inclusion.

notation.meaning: Probability-weighted sum of scenario objectives and set indicators.
Nonanticipativity subspace and its orthogonal complement.
Primal scenario vector and nonanticipativity multiplier.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Saddle-point characterization of finite-dimensional convex nonanticipativity decomposition.

source_refs.locator: 1.5 The Dual and Lexicographic Dual Methods p. 17

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(G(x)=\sum_{s\in S}p_s\bigl(f_s(x_s)+\delta_{C_s}(x_s)\bigr)\) and \(L(x,w)=G(x)+\langle w,x\rangle\) for \(w\in N^\perp\). The primal-dual saddle-point regime holds when there exists \((x^\star,w^\star)\in N\times N^\perp\) such that \[L(x^\star,w)\le L(x^\star,w^\star)\le L(x,w^\star)\quad\text{for all }x\in H,\ w\in N^\perp.\] Equivalently, \(x^\star\in N\), \(w^\star\in N^\perp\), and \(0\in\partial G(x^\star)+w^\star\). Under strong duality, these conditions characterize primal and dual solutions and supply the saddle structure used by progressive hedging.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In the saddle-point regime, a nonanticipative primal solution and an orthogonal multiplier satisfy the Lagrangian saddle inequalities, equivalently primal feasibility, dual feasibility, and subgradient stationarity.
knowledge_statements.title: Primal–Dual Saddle-Point Regime

source_witnesses.locator: 1.5 The Dual and Lexicographic Dual Methods p. 17

assumptions_latex: The exact progressive-hedging map is convergent in the closed convex saddle-point regime.
Each scenario subproblem returns an approximate first-order solution with residual \(e_s^k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Summable weighted scenario errors constitute a sufficient inexact-solve regime; merely bounded or nonvanishing errors are not covered by this condition.

notation.meaning: First-order residual of scenario solve at iteration k.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Summable-error version of inexact progressive hedging in the convex saddle-point regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iteration \(k\), let the computed scenario point \(x_s^{k+1}\) satisfy \[e_s^{k+1}\in \partial\bigl(f_s+\delta_{C_s}\bigr)(x_s^{k+1})+w_s^k+\rho\bigl(x_s^{k+1}-\bar x^k\bigr).\] Define \(\varepsilon_{k+1}=\bigl(\sum_{s\in S}p_s\lVert e_s^{k+1}\rVert^2\bigr)^{1/2}\). A summable-error inexact regime requires \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\varepsilon_{k+1}<\infty\), followed by the usual exact consensus projection and multiplier update. Under the same closed-convex and saddle-point hypotheses as the exact method, this condition is intended to preserve convergence. A fixed positive tolerance, or bounded errors whose sum diverges, does not satisfy this regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Approximate scenario solves remain in the summable-error regime when their weighted first-order residuals have finite total sum; fixed nonzero tolerances fall outside that condition.
knowledge_statements.title: Inexact Scenario-Solve Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Summable errors are a standard sufficient pattern for inexact splitting, but the displayed first-order residual must be connected quantitatively to the error notion used in an applicable progressive-hedging convergence theorem. No source establishes that this particular weighted residual criterion preserves convergence.

assumptions_latex: At least one scenario feasible set contains an integrality restriction, so the deterministic equivalent is nonconvex.
Progressive hedging is applied using quadratic scenario penalties and consensus multiplier updates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: In this regime progressive hedging is a heuristic unless supplemented by a separate globally valid bound, enumeration argument, or optimality certificate.

notation.meaning: Mixed-integer feasible set for scenario s.
Scenario decisions and their nonanticipative consensus.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between convex convergence theory and mixed-integer progressive-hedging heuristics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If some \(C_s\) imposes integrality, then the scenario objective \(f_s+\delta_{C_s}\) is generally nonconvex, and the convex monotone-operator interpretation of progressive hedging no longer applies. The scenario update \[x_s^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x_s\in C_s}\left\{f_s(x_s)+\langle w_s^k,x_s\rangle+\frac{\rho}{2}\lVert x_s-\bar x^k\rVert^2\right\}\] may switch discontinuously among integer solutions. Consequently, convergence of iterates and global optimality of a fixed point are not guaranteed by standard convex theory. If an iterate has \(x_s=\bar x\) for every \(s\), it certifies nonanticipative feasibility, but not global optimality without an independent bound or certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Integrality makes scenario subproblems nonconvex, so progressive hedging can switch between discrete solutions; consensus certifies feasibility but does not by itself certify global optimality.
knowledge_statements.title: Mixed-Integer Heuristic Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure boundary and its distinction between consensus feasibility and global optimality are plausible and appropriately scoped, but the record has no source for mixed-integer progressive hedging or its convergence limitations.

children.title: Penalty Scaling Sensitivity
children.top_down_role: Progressive-hedging behavior under poorly scaled or imbalanced penalty parameters.

knowledge_statements.title: Penalty Scaling Sensitivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scale-equivariance property of quadratic progressive-hedging subproblems under compatible objective, multiplier, and penalty scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the scenario update minimizing \(f_s(x)+\langle w_s^k,x\rangle+(\rho/2)\lVert x-\bar x^k\rVert^2\). Replace every \(f_s\) by \(f_s'=c f_s\), where \(c>0\), and set \(w_s^{\prime k}=c w_s^k\) and \(\rho'=c\rho\). The rescaled scenario objective is \[c\left(f_s(x)+\langle w_s^k,x\rangle+\frac{\rho}{2}\lVert x-\bar x^k\rVert^2\right),\] so the original and rescaled subproblems have the same minimizer sets. With identical initial primal states and coupled selection of the same minimizers, the consensus and primal sequences coincide, while the multipliers remain related by \(w_s^{\prime k}=c w_s^k\). Holding \(\rho\) fixed generally changes the penalty-to-objective ratio and need not preserve the minimizer sets or iterates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scaling objectives, penalties, and multipliers by the same positive factor preserves each scenario minimizer set. With matched initialization and minimizer choices, it preserves the primal sequence and scales the multipliers accordingly; keeping the penalty fixed generally does not.
assumptions_latex: A progressive-hedging instance has scenario objectives \(f_s\), multipliers \(w_s^k\), and penalty \(\rho>0\).
Every scenario objective is rescaled by a common constant \(c>0\).
The original and rescaled runs use identical initial primal states and coupled minimizer selections when a subproblem has multiple minimizers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The compatible choices \(f_s'=cf_s\), \(\rho'=c\rho\), and \(w_s^{\prime k}=cw_s^k\) preserve the scenario minimizer sets and, under coupled selections, the primal progressive-hedging sequence.

source_refs.locator: 1.4.8 Penalty and barrier function methods p. 38

source_witnesses.locator: 1.4.8 Penalty and barrier function methods p. 38

children.title: Consensus Stalling
children.top_down_role: Persistent failure to improve scenario consensus or residual measures.

assumptions_latex: Progressive-hedging iterates are generated for a finite scenario set with probabilities \(p_s>0\).
A diagnostic window length \(m\ge1\) and tolerance \(\eta\ge0\) are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed predicate defines consensus stalling over the selected window; it is a diagnostic condition, not an infeasibility or optimality certificate.
review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-window operational definition based on the nonanticipativity residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the consensus residual by \[r_k=\left(\sum_{s\in S}p_s\lVert x_s^k-\bar x^k\rVert^2\right)^{1/2}.\] For a chosen window \(m\ge1\) and decrease tolerance \(\eta\ge0\), consensus is stalled at iteration \(k\ge m\) when \(r_k>0\) and \[r_{k-m}-\min_{j=k-m+1,\ldots,k}r_j\le\eta.\] Thus no iterate in the window improves the residual by more than \(\eta\), despite nonanticipativity remaining violated. This finite-window predicate is an operational failure diagnostic. It does not imply that the underlying stochastic program is infeasible, nor does it alone establish eventual nonconvergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Consensus stalls over a chosen window when the nonanticipativity residual remains positive and fails to decrease by more than a prescribed tolerance.
knowledge_statements.title: Consensus Stalling

children.title: Iterate Cycling
children.top_down_role: Repeated return to prior scenario decisions or consensus patterns.

knowledge_statements.title: Iterate Cycling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational diagnostic for exact or approximate periodic recurrence in the full progressive-hedging state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(z^k=((x_s^k)_{s\in S},\bar x^k,(w_s^k)_{s\in S})\) be the complete iteration state. Approximate cycling of candidate period \(q\ge2\) is observed over indices \(k_0,\ldots,k_1\) when \[\lVert z^{k+q}-z^k\rVert\le\epsilon\quad\text{whenever }k_0\le k\le k_1-q,\] and at least two observed phases are separated according to \[\max_{0\le i<j<q}\lVert z^{k_0+i}-z^{k_0+j}\rVert\ge\delta,\qquad \delta>2\epsilon.\] When \(\epsilon=0\), these predicates identify exact nonconstant recurrence within the observed window. They define a finite-window cycling diagnostic only. If the exact recurrence continues for all subsequent indices, the resulting tail is a nonconstant periodic orbit and cannot converge to a single fixed point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cycling is diagnosed when the full primal-dual state approximately repeats after a period of at least two while at least two observed phases remain separated. A finite window is only diagnostic; an exact nonconstant recurrence that continues indefinitely is a periodic orbit and cannot converge to one fixed point.
assumptions_latex: The complete progressive-hedging state is denoted by \(z^k\).
Distances are measured in a fixed norm, with recurrence tolerance \(\epsilon\ge0\) and separation threshold \(\delta>2\epsilon\).
The observation window contains at least one comparison separated by the candidate period \(q\ge2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed predicates define finite-window approximate cycling; only exact nonconstant recurrence continuing indefinitely establishes a periodic orbit that cannot converge to one fixed point.

notation.meaning: Complete primal, consensus, and multiplier state.

children.title: Penalty-Induced Instability
children.top_down_role: Oscillation or erratic progress attributable to penalty choices.

assumptions_latex: Near a fixed point \(z^\star\), one progressive-hedging step is represented by a differentiable map \(T_\rho\).
The penalty parameter satisfies \(\rho>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(\operatorname{spr}(DT_\rho(z^\star))>1\), the fixed point is locally unstable for that penalty value; changing \(\rho\) can cross this stability boundary.

notation.meaning: One-step progressive-hedging state map at penalty rho.
Fixed point of the state map.
Spectral radius of a linear operator.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local spectral stability boundary for a differentiable fixed-point representation.

source_refs.locator: 1.4.8 Penalty and barrier function methods p. 38

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose the complete iteration can locally be written as \(z^{k+1}=T_\rho(z^k)\), where \(T_\rho\) is continuously differentiable near a fixed point \(z^\star=T_\rho(z^\star)\). If the Jacobian has an eigenvalue outside the unit disk, equivalently \[\operatorname{spr}\bigl(DT_\rho(z^\star)\bigr)>1,\] then perturbations with a component in the corresponding unstable direction grow to first order, and \(z^\star\) is not locally asymptotically stable. Because \(DT_\rho(z^\star)\) depends on the relative scaling induced by \(\rho\), varying the penalty can move eigenvalues across the unit circle and induce local instability.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A penalty value is locally destabilizing when the linearized progressive-hedging map has an eigenvalue outside the unit disk, causing some small perturbations to grow.
knowledge_statements.title: Penalty-Induced Instability

source_witnesses.locator: 1.4.8 Penalty and barrier function methods p. 38

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The spectral-radius instability criterion is standard for differentiable discrete maps, and the failure_boundary kind fits. The cited penalty-method sections do not specifically support differentiability of the progressive-hedging map, its Jacobian, or penalty-driven eigenvalue crossings; an appropriate dynamical-systems or local progressive-hedging analysis is required.

children.title: Sampling-Based Two-Stage Decomposition
children.top_down_role: Two-stage decomposition methods that build recourse approximations from sampled observations rather than exhaustive scenario enumeration.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: Stochastic Decomposition: A Statistical Method for Large Scale Stochastic Linear Programming
top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_title: Stochastic Decomposition: A Statistical Method for Large Scale Stochastic Linear Programming

assumptions_latex: A fixed sample \(\{\xi_i\}_{i=1}^N\) is given with positive weights \(a_i\) summing to one.
The first-stage set is polyhedral, recourse is linear, and relatively complete recourse holds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: When the master lower bound and incumbent sampled objective differ by at most \(\epsilon\), the output is \(\epsilon\)-optimal for the fixed sample-average problem.

notation.meaning: Fixed sample and normalized sample weights.
Scenario recourse value and its master approximation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multicut L-shaped algorithm for one fixed finite sample with relatively complete linear recourse.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the fixed sample problem \(\min_{x\in X}\{c^\top x+\sum_{i=1}^N a_iQ_i(x)\}\), initialize a master problem with variables \(x\in X\) and lower estimators \(\theta_i\). At master solution \(x^k\), solve every linear recourse problem and obtain an optimal dual solution \(\pi_i^k\). Add the valid cut \[\theta_i\ge (\pi_i^k)^\top(h_i-T_i x)\] for each scenario whose current estimator is violated. Re-solve the master, update an incumbent using evaluated recourse values, and stop when the incumbent sampled objective minus the master lower bound is at most \(\epsilon\). Return the incumbent first-stage decision.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fix the sample, iteratively solve a master problem and sampled recourse duals, add violated Benders cuts, and stop when the sampled upper-lower bound gap meets tolerance.
knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Sample L-Shaped Methods

assumptions_latex: Independent training samples have increasing sizes \(N_1<N_2<\cdots\).
Each sample-average problem has linear recourse and is solved by an L-shaped method to tolerance \(\epsilon_\ell\).
An independent validation sample is available at every outer iteration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The method returns the first candidate whose independently estimated validation uncertainty and inner optimization error satisfy the prescribed stopping tolerances.

notation.meaning: Training-sample size and inner solve tolerance at stage l.
Candidate first-stage decision at stage l.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Increasing-sample outer loop with L-shaped inner solves and independent validation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose increasing training sizes \(N_\ell\), inner tolerances \(\epsilon_\ell\), a validation confidence level \(1-\alpha\), and target half-width \(\tau\). At outer iteration \(\ell\), draw or enlarge an independent training sample, solve its sample-average problem by a fixed-sample L-shaped method to gap \(\epsilon_\ell\), and obtain \(x^\ell\). Evaluate \(c^\top x^\ell+Q(x^\ell,\xi)\) on an independent validation sample and form a confidence interval with half-width \(H_\ell\). Stop and return \(x^\ell\) when \(H_\ell\le\tau\) and \(\epsilon_\ell\le\tau\); otherwise increase the training and validation sizes and repeat.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sequential sampling repeatedly enlarges the training sample, solves each sampled problem by L-shaped decomposition, validates independently, and stops when statistical and optimization tolerances are met.
knowledge_statements.title: Sequential-Sampling L-Shaped Methods

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cited L-shaped section supports the inner solver but not the increasing-sample protocol or its stopping rule. A confidence interval for the value of one candidate does not by itself quantify that candidate's optimality gap, so the statistical meaning of the proposed validation test requires a dedicated source and fuller specification.

assumptions_latex: The target scenario law has density or mass function \(p\), while samples are drawn independently from \(q\).
Absolute continuity holds: \(p(\xi)>0\) implies \(q(\xi)>0\).
The weighted recourse estimator has finite first moment.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Likelihood weighting makes both sampled recourse values and aggregated L-shaped cuts unbiased for expectations under the target law \(p\).

notation.meaning: Likelihood ratio for converting proposal samples to the target law.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Likelihood-weighted fixed-sample L-shaped method under an absolutely continuous proposal law.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Draw \(\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_N\) independently from proposal law \(q\) and compute \(L_i=p(\xi_i)/q(\xi_i)\). Replace the target recourse expectation by \[\widehat Q_N(x)=\frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N L_iQ(x,\xi_i),\qquad \mathbb E_q[\widehat Q_N(x)]=\mathbb E_p[Q(x,\xi)].\] At each master iterate, solve the sampled recourse duals and multiply each resulting scenario cut by \(L_i/N\) before aggregation, or equivalently use weights proportional to \(L_i\) in a self-normalized variant. Apply the ordinary L-shaped cut-generation and gap test to this weighted sampled problem, and return its incumbent decision.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sample scenarios from a proposal law, weight recourse values and Benders cuts by target-to-proposal likelihood ratios, then run the usual fixed-sample L-shaped method.
knowledge_statements.title: Importance-Sampled L-Shaped Methods

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Ordinary likelihood-ratio weighting gives an unbiased expectation estimator under suitable integrability, but self-normalized likelihood weights are generally biased and are not equivalent for the fixed sampled problem. Unbiased cut coefficients also require integrability and measurable dual/subgradient selections beyond the stated finite first moment. The combined importance-sampled L-shaped construction therefore needs correction and direct source support.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Almost-Sure Subsequence Optimality for Stochastic Decomposition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded convergence theorem for stochastic decomposition. The extract invokes assumptions (i)–(iii) and problem (12.1.3) without reproducing their definitions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under assumptions (i), (ii), and (iii), there exists an infinite subsequence of indices $K^*\subseteq\{1,2,\ldots\}$ such that, with probability one, every accumulation point of $\{\mathbf{x}^k:k\in K^*\}$ is an optimal solution of problem $(12.1.3)$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the source's assumptions (i), (ii), and (iii), there is an infinite subsequence of the stochastic-decomposition iterates whose every accumulation point is, with probability one, an optimal solution of problem (12.1.3).
assumptions_latex: \text{Assumptions (i), (ii), and (iii) of the source theorem hold.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\,K^*\subseteq\mathbb{N}\text{ defining an infinite subsequence such that }\mathbb{P}\!\left(\text{every accumulation point of }\{\mathbf{x}^k:k\in K^*\}\text{ is optimal for }(12.1.3)\right)=1.

knowledge_statements.title: Sampled Recourse Approximations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-sample representation of expected recourse in a two-stage stochastic program.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), let \(c\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and let \(Q(x,\xi)\) be measurable with finite expectation for every \(x\in X\). For independent samples \(\xi^1,\ldots,\xi^N\) having the distribution of \(\xi\), the sampled recourse function and sample-average objective are \[\widehat q_N(x)=\frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N Q(x,\xi^i),\qquad \widehat F_N(x)=c^{\mathsf T}x+\widehat q_N(x).\] A sampled-recourse solution is any \(\widehat x_N\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}\widehat F_N(x)\). For each fixed \(x\), integrability implies \(\widehat q_N(x)\to\mathbb E[Q(x,\xi)]\) almost surely.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sampled recourse replaces the expected second-stage value by its empirical average over independent scenarios and minimizes the resulting sample-average objective.
assumptions_latex: \(\xi^1,\ldots,\xi^N\) are independent and identically distributed as \(\xi\).
\(Q(x,\xi)\) is measurable and integrable for each \(x\in X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat q_N(x)\to\mathbb E[Q(x,\xi)]\) almost surely for every fixed \(x\in X\).

notation.meaning: optimal second-stage recourse value at first-stage decision x and realization ξ

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: sample-average approximation and the pointwise strong law are standard

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The sampled-recourse representation and fixed-decision strong-law claim are standard, but no inspectable citation supports the precise integrability and convergence formulation. The plain statement also omits the convergence claim.

knowledge_statements.title: Stochastic-Decomposition Cut Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scenario-wise and aggregated affine minorants generated from sampled convex recourse functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), let \(x_k\in X\), and suppose \(Q(\cdot,\xi^i)\) is proper and convex for every \(i\in S_k\). Choose \(g_{k,i}\in\partial_x Q(x_k,\xi^i)\). For each \(i\in S_k\), the scenario cut is \[q_i\ge Q(x_k,\xi^i)+g_{k,i}^{\mathsf T}(x-x_k).\] A multicut model retains these inequalities separately. For the empirical recourse function \(\widehat q_{S_k}(x)=|S_k|^{-1}\sum_{i\in S_k}Q(x,\xi^i)\), the aggregated cut is \[q\ge\frac1{|S_k|}\sum_{i\in S_k}\left(Q(x_k,\xi^i)+g_{k,i}^{\mathsf T}(x-x_k)\right).\] It is an affine minorant of \(\widehat q_{S_k}\). Convex combinations of affine minorants remain valid for a common target function when the combination weights are nonnegative and sum to one.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scenario subgradients produce separate affine recourse cuts, while averaging cuts from the same scenario batch produces a valid lower estimator of that batch's empirical recourse function. Convex combinations are valid only when their component cuts minorize the same target function.

knowledge_statements.title: Stabilized Stochastic Decomposition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proximal stabilization of a sampled cutting-plane master problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a closed convex set \(X\), an initial center \(z_0\in X\), parameters \(\rho_k>0\), and sampled affine recourse model \(m_k(x)=\max_{j\le k}\{a_j+b_j^{\mathsf T}x\}\), compute \[x_{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}\left\{c^{\mathsf T}x+m_k(x)+\frac{\rho_k}{2}\lVert x-z_k\rVert^2\right\}.\] Evaluate new sampled recourse information at \(x_{k+1}\), append a valid affine cut to form \(m_{k+1}\), and either set \(z_{k+1}=x_{k+1}\) after a prescribed serious-step test or retain \(z_{k+1}=z_k\). Stop when a valid estimated optimality gap meets the chosen tolerance; otherwise repeat.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A proximal term anchors each sampled cutting-plane master problem, while a serious-step test controls when the stabilization center moves.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
Every affine piece in \(m_k\) is a valid sampled recourse minorant.

knowledge_statements.title: Stochastic-Decomposition Convergence Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Almost-sure convergence under diminishing-step stochastic approximation assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:X\to\mathbb R\) be convex on a nonempty compact convex set \(X\), with nonempty minimizer set \(X^*\). Consider \(x_{k+1}=\Pi_X(x_k-\alpha_kG_k)\), where \(\mathcal F_k\) contains the history through \(x_k\), \(\mathbb E[G_k\mid\mathcal F_k]\in\partial F(x_k)\), and \(\mathbb E[\lVert G_k\rVert^2\mid\mathcal F_k]\le M<\infty\). If \(\alpha_k>0\), \(\sum_k\alpha_k=\infty\), and \(\sum_k\alpha_k^2<\infty\), then \(F(x_k)\to F^*\) almost surely and every accumulation point of \((x_k)\) belongs to \(X^*\) almost surely. Persistent nonvanishing steps generally yield only neighborhood or averaged convergence guarantees.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Unbiased bounded-variance stochastic cuts with square-summable but nonsummable steps give almost-sure optimal-value convergence; constant steps generally do not.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is convex and \(X\) is nonempty, compact, and convex.
The stochastic subgradient is conditionally unbiased with uniformly bounded conditional second moment.
\(\sum_k\alpha_k=\infty\) and \(\sum_k\alpha_k^2<\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F(x_k)\to F^*\) and every cluster point lies in \(X^*\) almost surely.

knowledge_statements.title: Statistical Lower Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A one-sided lower confidence bound derived from independent bounded SAA optimal values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(z^*=\inf_{x\in X}\mathbb E[f(x,\xi)]\). For each \(j=1,\ldots,M\), solve an independent size-\(N\) sample-average problem and denote its optimal value by \(Z_j\). Suppose \(a\le Z_j\le b\) almost surely. Since an infimum and expectation satisfy \(\mathbb E[Z_j]\le z^*\), define, for \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), \[L_{M,\alpha}=\frac1M\sum_{j=1}^M Z_j-(b-a)\sqrt{\frac{\log(1/\alpha)}{2M}}.\] Hoeffding's inequality gives \(\mathbb P\{L_{M,\alpha}\le\mathbb E[Z_1]\}\ge1-\alpha\), and consequently \(\mathbb P\{L_{M,\alpha}\le z^*\}\ge1-\alpha\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent bounded SAA optimal values yield a Hoeffding lower confidence bound because their common expectation does not exceed the true optimal value.
assumptions_latex: The \(M\) SAA problems use mutually independent, identically distributed scenario batches.
\(a\le Z_j\le b\) almost surely for every \(j=1,\ldots,M\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb P\{L_{M,\alpha}\le z^*\}\ge1-\alpha\).

notation.meaning: optimal value of SAA replication j

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: SAA downward bias and Hoeffding concentration give the certificate

knowledge_statements.title: Candidate-Solution Upper Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Independent bounded-sample validation bound for a fixed or independently selected candidate solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\widehat x\in X\) be selected independently of validation observations \(\xi^1,\ldots,\xi^M\), which are i.i.d. with the distribution of \(\xi\). Suppose \(a\le f(\widehat x,\xi^i)\le b\) almost surely, and define \(F(x)=\mathbb E[f(x,\xi)]\). For \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), set \[U_{M,\alpha}(\widehat x)=\frac1M\sum_{i=1}^M f(\widehat x,\xi^i)+(b-a)\sqrt{\frac{\log(1/\alpha)}{2M}}.\] Conditional on \(\widehat x\), Hoeffding's inequality yields \(\mathbb P\{F(\widehat x)\le U_{M,\alpha}(\widehat x)\mid\widehat x\}\ge1-\alpha\). Since \(z^*\le F(\widehat x)\) for a minimization problem, \(U_{M,\alpha}(\widehat x)\) is also an upper confidence bound for \(z^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An independent bounded validation sample gives a one-sided upper confidence bound for a candidate's expected cost and therefore also bounds the minimization problem's optimal value from above.
assumptions_latex: \(\widehat x\in X\) is independent of the validation sample \(\xi^1,\ldots,\xi^M\).
The validation observations are i.i.d. with the distribution of \(\xi\).
\(a\le f(\widehat x,\xi^i)\le b\) almost surely.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb P\{F(\widehat x)\le U_{M,\alpha}(\widehat x)\mid\widehat x\}\ge1-\alpha\).

notation.meaning: candidate solution selected independently of validation

children.title: Sequential Stopping Rules
children.top_down_role: Data-dependent termination criteria for sampling-decomposition runs.

knowledge_statements.title: Sequential Stopping Rules
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stopping based on time-uniform lower and upper confidence sequences.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For stages \(t=1,2,\ldots\), construct statistics \(L_t\) and \(U_t\) satisfying \[\mathbb P\{\forall t\ge1:\ L_t\le z^*\le U_t\}\ge1-\alpha,\] where \(\alpha\in(0,1)\). Given an absolute tolerance \(\varepsilon\ge0\), define \[\tau=\inf\{t\ge1:U_t-L_t\le\varepsilon\},\] with \(\inf\varnothing=\infty\). At each stage, update the permitted optimization and validation samples, recompute \(L_t,U_t\), and stop at the first stage satisfying the width condition. If \(\tau<\infty\), return the incumbent candidate, \([L_\tau,U_\tau]\), and the certificate \(U_\tau-L_\tau\le\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Recompute jointly time-uniform value bounds after each sampling stage and stop the first time their width is no greater than the prescribed tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \((L_t,U_t)_{t\ge1}\) has simultaneous coverage at error level \(\alpha\in(0,1)\).
\(\varepsilon\ge0\).
Every data-dependent update used to form the bounds satisfies the validity conditions of the confidence-sequence construction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: With probability at least \(1-\alpha\), if \(\tau<\infty\), then \(z^*\in[L_\tau,U_\tau]\) and \(U_\tau-L_\tau\le\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: time-uniform lower and upper confidence-sequence endpoints

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: simultaneous confidence sequences remain valid at their induced stopping time

children.title: Optimality-Gap Assessment
children.top_down_role: Statistical assessment of the gap associated with a candidate solution.

knowledge_statements.title: Optimality-Gap Assessment
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Combining simultaneous objective bounds into absolute and relative optimality-gap certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization problem, let \(z^*\) be the optimal value and let \(\widehat x\in X\) be feasible. Suppose \(L\le z^*\) and \(F(\widehat x)\le U\) hold on a common event. Then \[0\le F(\widehat x)-z^*\le U-L.\] Thus \(G=U-L\) is an absolute optimality-gap certificate. If additionally \(L>0\), then \[\frac{F(\widehat x)-z^*}{z^*}\le\frac{U-L}{L}.\] If the common event has probability at least \(1-\alpha\), both assessments have that confidence level. Bounds constructed separately must receive simultaneous-error control before they are combined.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A simultaneous lower bound on the optimum and upper bound on a feasible candidate's cost give an absolute gap certificate and, when the lower bound is positive, a relative gap certificate.
assumptions_latex: \(\widehat x\in X\) is feasible.
\(L\le z^*\le F(\widehat x)\le U\) holds on a common event.
For the relative certificate, \(L>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F(\widehat x)-z^*\le U-L\), and if \(L>0\), then \((F(\widehat x)-z^*)/z^*\le(U-L)/L\).

notation.meaning: lower bound on the optimal value

children.title: Stopping-Time Error Control

knowledge_statements.title: Stopping-Time Error Control
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coverage transfer from a simultaneous confidence sequence to arbitrary stopping times.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((\mathcal F_t)_{t\ge1}\) be a filtration, let \(\tau\) be an \((\mathcal F_t)\)-stopping time taking values in \(\mathbb N\cup\{\infty\}\), and let \(C_t=[L_t,U_t]\) satisfy \[\mathbb P\{\forall t\ge1:z^*\in C_t\}\ge1-\alpha.\] Then \[\mathbb P\{\tau<\infty\text{ and }z^*\notin C_\tau\}\le\alpha.\] Therefore, repeated inspection and stopping by any history-measurable rule do not inflate the stated error probability. Pointwise intervals satisfying only \(\mathbb P\{z^*\in C_t\}\ge1-\alpha\) separately for each fixed \(t\) do not generally imply this conclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A simultaneous confidence sequence retains its coverage at any data-dependent stopping time, whereas separate fixed-stage confidence intervals generally do not.

\(\tau\) is an \((\mathcal F_t)\)-stopping time.
\(\mathbb P\{\forall t\ge1:z^*\in C_t\}\ge1-\alpha\) for \(\alpha\in(0,1)\).

children.title: Premature-Stopping Risk
children.top_down_role: Underestimation of uncertainty caused by repeated inspection or early termination.

knowledge_statements.title: Premature-Stopping Risk
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Error inflation from repeatedly applying fixed-stage tests without multiplicity correction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a procedure examines \(T\) independent stages and, under a nonacceptable solution, falsely declares success at each stage with probability \(\alpha\in(0,1)\). If it stops at the first declaration, then \[\mathbb P\{\text{at least one false declaration by stage }T\}=1-(1-\alpha)^T.\] This probability exceeds \(\alpha\) whenever \(T>1\), and it converges to \(1\) as \(T\to\infty\). Thus repeatedly inspected fixed-stage level-\(\alpha\) certificates do not retain overall level \(\alpha\). Valid remedies include time-uniform inference or stagewise error allocations \((\alpha_t)_{t\ge1}\) satisfying \(\sum_{t\ge1}\alpha_t\le\alpha\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeated independent level-alpha checks can make premature stopping nearly certain unless inference is time-uniform or the total error is allocated across stages.
assumptions_latex: There are \(T\) independent stagewise false-declaration events.
Each event has probability \(\alpha\in(0,1)\).
The procedure stops after the first declaration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb P\{\text{premature stop by stage }T\}=1-(1-\alpha)^T\to1\) as \(T\to\infty\).

notation.meaning: nominal error probability at each stage

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the independent repeated-testing calculation is elementary

children.title: Dependent-Sampling Boundary
children.top_down_role: Limits of certification under correlated observations or coupled replications.

knowledge_statements.title: Dependent-Sampling Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Perfect dependence invalidates concentration rates based on nominal sample size.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Y\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\) and define \(X_i=Y\) for every \(i=1,\ldots,M\). Each \(X_i\) has mean \(1/2\) and lies in \([0,1]\), but the observations are perfectly dependent and \[\overline X_M=\frac1M\sum_{i=1}^M X_i=Y.\] Hence, for every \(M\ge1\), \[\mathbb P\{|\overline X_M-1/2|\ge1/4\}=1.\] The independent-sample Hoeffding expression for this deviation is \(2\exp(-M/8)\), which tends to zero and therefore cannot bound this probability once it falls below one. Marginal boundedness alone does not justify independent-sample certification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Perfectly dependent Bernoulli observations have a sample mean equal to one shared observation, so independent-sample concentration can become arbitrarily overconfident.
assumptions_latex: \(Y\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\).
\(X_i=Y\) for every \(i=1,\ldots,M\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb P\{|\overline X_M-1/2|\ge1/4\}=1\) for every \(M\ge1\), despite bounded identical marginals.

notation.meaning: single Bernoulli variable shared by all observations

children.title: Adaptive-Selection Bias
children.top_down_role: Bias from choosing candidates, sample sizes, or designs using observed outcomes.

knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive-Selection Bias
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reusing evaluation data after candidate selection creates optimistic bias.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let two candidates have the same true expected cost \(p\in(0,1)\). For \(j\in\{1,2\}\), observe independent validation losses \(Y_j\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(p)\). Select any \(J\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{j\in\{1,2\}}Y_j\) and report \(Y_J\) as the selected candidate's estimated cost. Then \[\mathbb E[Y_J]=\mathbb E[\min(Y_1,Y_2)]=\mathbb P\{Y_1=Y_2=1\}=p^2<p.\] The selected candidate's true expected cost remains \(p\), but its reused validation estimate is downward biased by \(p-p^2\). Independent post-selection validation or valid simultaneous inference is required for assessment.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Selecting the better-looking candidate on validation data and reporting the same data produces an optimistically biased cost estimate even when both candidates have equal true cost.
assumptions_latex: \(Y_1,Y_2\) are independent \(\operatorname{Bernoulli}(p)\) variables.
Both candidates have true expected cost \(p\in(0,1)\).
\(J\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{j\in\{1,2\}}Y_j\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[Y_J]=p^2<p\), while the selected candidate's true expected cost is \(p\).

notation.meaning: validation loss observed for candidate j

children.title: Optional-Stopping Bias
children.top_down_role: Distortion associated with data-dependent continuation or termination.

knowledge_statements.title: Optional-Stopping Bias
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A finite-horizon example showing that adaptive termination biases a sample-average assessment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X_1,X_2\) be independent Rademacher variables, so \(\mathbb P(X_i=1)=\mathbb P(X_i=-1)=1/2\), and define the stopping time \(\tau=1\) when \(X_1=1\) and \(\tau=2\) otherwise. Although every fixed-sample mean is unbiased for zero, the stopped mean \(\bar X_\tau=\tau^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^{\tau}X_i\) satisfies \[\mathbb E[\bar X_\tau]=\tfrac12(1)+\tfrac12\mathbb E[(-1+X_2)/2]=\tfrac14>0.\] Thus repeatedly inspecting an assessment and stopping according to its observed value can invalidate fixed-sample unbiasedness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Even with independent mean-zero observations, stopping early after a favorable observation makes the reported sample mean positively biased.
assumptions_latex: \(X_1,X_2\) are independent and uniformly distributed on \(\{-1,1\}\).
\(\tau\) is adapted to the observation filtration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[\bar X_\tau]=1/4\neq 0\).

notation.meaning: sample mean evaluated at the stopping time

children.title: Dependence-Robust Assessment
children.top_down_role: Certification regimes designed for structured sampling dependence.

knowledge_statements.title: Dependence-Robust Assessment
knowledge_statements.scope_note: An anytime-valid certificate allowing temporal dependence through a supermartingale condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((\mathcal F_t)_{t\geq0}\) be a filtration generated by adaptive sampling and assessment decisions. Suppose that under every distribution \(P\) in the null class \(\mathcal P_0\), an adapted process \((E_t)_{t\geq0}\) is nonnegative, satisfies \(E_0=1\), and obeys \(\mathbb E_P[E_t\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}]\leq E_{t-1}\). For any \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), the rule that rejects when \(E_t\geq1/\alpha\) satisfies \[\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_0}\mathbb P_P\!\left(\sup_{t\geq0}E_t\geq1/\alpha\right)\leq\alpha.\] The certificate therefore remains valid under arbitrary stopping and permitted dependence encoded by the conditional supermartingale property.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonnegative null supermartingale yields a level-alpha assessment valid under adaptive stopping and any dependence compatible with its conditional expectation condition.
assumptions_latex: \((E_t)\) is nonnegative and adapted to \((\mathcal F_t)\).
\(\mathbb E_P[E_t\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}]\leq E_{t-1}\) for every \(P\in\mathcal P_0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_0}\mathbb P_P(\sup_{t\geq0}E_t\geq1/\alpha)\leq\alpha\).

knowledge_statements.title: Stagewise Value-Function Decomposition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bellman representation on a finite scenario tree with node-conditional continuation values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a finite scenario tree with nonterminal nodes \(n\), children \(\mathcal C(n)\), and conditional probabilities \(p_{m\mid n}\). If \(x\) is the state inherited by node \(n\), define \[V_n(x)=\inf_{y\in Y_n(x)}\left\{c_n(x,y)+\sum_{m\in\mathcal C(n)}p_{m\mid n}V_m(T_{nm}(x,y))\right\},\] with terminal values \(V_n(x)=\inf_{y\in Y_n(x)}c_n(x,y)\). Under stagewise additive costs and tree-adapted feasibility, the root optimum equals \(V_r(x_0)\); hence each subtree is represented upstream solely by its node value function.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Additive multistage optimization decomposes recursively: each node minimizes its local cost plus the conditional expected values of its child subtrees.
assumptions_latex: The scenario tree is finite and has conditional probabilities \(p_{m\mid n}\).
Costs are stagewise additive and feasible decisions are tree-adapted.
Every displayed infimum is well-defined in the extended-real sense.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v^\star=V_r(x_0)\) with \(V_n\) given by the nodewise recursion.

knowledge_statements.title: Tree-Node Cut Systems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Node-indexed supporting cuts for convex cost-to-go functions in nested Benders decomposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each nonterminal tree node \(n\), initialize a lower approximation \(\underline V_n^0(x)=\max_{j\in J_n^0}\{\alpha_{nj}+\beta_{nj}^{\mathsf T}x\}\), allowing an initial global lower bound. At iteration \(k\), solve a forward policy using the current approximations. In a backward traversal, solve each node recourse problem at the visited predecessor state \(x_n^k\), obtain its value \(q_n^k\) and subgradient \(g_n^k\), and append \[V_n(x)\geq q_n^k+(g_n^k)^{\mathsf T}(x-x_n^k).\] Stop when a valid root upper-lower bound gap meets the prescribed tolerance; output the incumbent policy and node cut collections.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nested Benders maintains separate supporting-cut models at tree nodes, adding backward-pass subgradient cuts until the certified root gap is sufficiently small.
assumptions_latex: Every node continuation value \(V_n\) is proper and convex.
Node subproblems return valid values and subgradients.
Valid root lower and upper bounds are available for stopping.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\underline V_n^k(x)\leq V_n(x)\) for every node \(n\), iteration \(k\), and admissible state \(x\).

knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic Nested Decomposition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nested decomposition for convex quadratic node subproblems with polyhedral linking constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At every node \(n\), let the local problem have convex quadratic objective \(\tfrac12y^{\mathsf T}H_ny+h_n^{\mathsf T}y\), where \(H_n\succeq0\), together with affine constraints linking \(y\) to the predecessor state \(x\). Initialize each downstream value model by valid affine lower bounds. At iteration \(k\), solve the resulting convex quadratic node problems forward; then traverse backward and use optimal multipliers of the linking constraints to construct a subgradient \(g_n^k\) and the supporting cut \[V_n(x)\geq V_n(x_n^k)+(g_n^k)^{\mathsf T}(x-x_n^k).\] Append the cuts and stop at the requested root optimality gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convex quadratic node problems can be nested-decomposed by solving node QPs and deriving affine value-function cuts from linking-constraint multipliers.

Linking and local feasibility constraints are affine.
Strong duality holds for each solved node problem.

notation.meaning: value-function subgradient derived from optimal multipliers

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convex and piecewise-quadratic structure of multistage quadratic recourse
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometry of the effective domains, expected future-value functions, and stage programs in the recursively defined MQSP model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the recursively defined MQSP with polyhedral stage constraints and discrete uncertainty. If \(D^t(\omega)\succeq0\) for every \(\omega\in\Omega\) and \(t=1,\ldots,H\), then \(K^t\) and \(\mathcal Q^{t+1}\) are convex for \(t=1,\ldots,H-1\). If, additionally, \(\Xi^t\) is finite for \(t=2,\ldots,H\), then each \(K^t\) is polyhedral. Moreover, for each applicable stage, \(z^t\) is either identically \(-\infty\), or \(K^t\) has a polyhedral-complex decomposition with respect to which the stage-t deterministic-equivalent program is piecewise quadratic.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In the recursively defined multistage quadratic stochastic program, positive-semidefinite stage matrices make the effective domains and future-value functions convex. Finite scenario supports additionally make the effective domains polyhedral. Each stage objective is either identically minus infinity or induces a piecewise-quadratic program over a polyhedral complex.
assumptions_latex: \text{The objects }K^t,\mathcal Q^{t+1},z^t\text{ are those of the recursively defined MQSP with polyhedral stage constraints and discrete uncertainty.}
D^t(\omega)\succeq0\quad\forall\omega\in\Omega,\quad t=1,\ldots,H
|\Xi^t|<\infty\quad(t=2,\ldots,H)\quad\text{only for the polyhedrality conclusion}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nested piecewise-quadratic programming algorithm for MQSP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Forward-and-backward nested procedure that refines working regions and propagates active quadratic pieces through the scenario tree.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Initialize the first-stage region and decision, then initialize descendant stage-node subproblems along the scenario tree. At a current pair \((t,k)\), compute minimizers \(v\) and \(w\) of the accumulated objective \(z_k^t\) over the maintained regions \(S_k^t\) and \(C_k^t\), respectively. If \(w\) lies at the limiting point of a ray on which \(z_k^t\) decreases to \(-\infty\), declare the current deterministic-equivalent problem unbounded and terminate. If \(\nabla z_k^t(w)^T(v-w)\ne0\), refine
\[
S_k^t\leftarrow S_k^t\cap\{x:\nabla z_k^t(w)^T(x-w)\le0\},
\]
reset the local model as specified, and resume the forward calculation. If \(\nabla z_k^t(w)^T(v-w)=0\) at \(t=1\), stop with \(w\) as an optimal first-period decision. Otherwise, identify the cell containing \(w\) and its quadratic piece, add the probability-weighted piece to the parent objective, intersect the parent region with the corresponding induced region, and continue backward or with the next child node.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nested PQP moves forward through the scenario tree while maintaining local regions and quadratic objectives. At each stage node it compares two regional minimizers. An objective-decreasing unbounded ray triggers an unboundedness report; a failed stationarity test adds a separating halfspace and restarts the forward calculation. A successful test either returns an optimal first-stage decision or propagates the active quadratic piece and region to the parent.
assumptions_latex: \text{The input and the objects }K^t,z_k^t,C_k^t,S_k^t\text{ are those used by the nested PQP construction for MQSP.}
\text{The required regional minimizers, polyhedral cells, and associated quadratic pieces are determined at the indicated steps.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Each iteration either detects an unbounded ray, returns an optimal first-period decision at stage }1,\text{ refines a working region, or propagates a quadratic piece to the parent stage.}

children.title: Block-Separable Nested Decomposition
children.top_down_role: Nested decomposition exploiting separable blocks within stages or tree nodes.

knowledge_statements.title: Block-Separable Nested Decomposition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact decomposition when every node’s feasible set, transition, and cost separate across blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a node \(n\), suppose \(x=(x_1,\ldots,x_B)\), \(y=(y_1,\ldots,y_B)\), \(Y_n(x)=\prod_{b=1}^B Y_{nb}(x_b)\), and both local costs and child transitions separate by block. If every child value also has the form \(V_m(z)=\sum_{b=1}^B V_{mb}(z_b)\), then \[V_n(x)=\sum_{b=1}^B\inf_{y_b\in Y_{nb}(x_b)}\left\{c_{nb}(x_b,y_b)+\sum_{m\in\mathcal C(n)}p_{m\mid n}V_{mb}(T_{nmb}(x_b,y_b))\right\}.\] Consequently, node solves and supporting cuts may be generated independently by block and summed without loss.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When costs, feasibility, transitions, and child values separate across blocks, the node value equals the sum of independently computed block values.
assumptions_latex: Costs, child transitions, and child values are additively block-separable.
Conditional probabilities are common fixed weights for the block objectives.

children.title: Network-Structured Nested Decomposition
children.top_down_role: Nested variants tailored to network-constrained stage problems.

knowledge_statements.title: Network-Structured Nested Decomposition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Benders cuts obtained from dual node potentials in linear network recourse.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a node recourse value is the feasible bounded network-flow program \[Q_n(x)=\min_y\{c_n^{\mathsf T}y:A_ny=b_n-B_nx,\;\ell_n\leq y\leq u_n\},\] where \(A_n\) is a node-arc incidence matrix. Its dual can be written with node potentials \(\pi\) and bound multipliers \(s^+,s^-\), and strong duality gives \[Q_n(x)=\max\{\pi^{\mathsf T}(b_n-B_nx)-u_n^{\mathsf T}s^++\ell_n^{\mathsf T}s^-:A_n^{\mathsf T}\pi-s^++s^-=c_n,\;s^+,s^-\geq0\}.\] Every dual-feasible triple therefore defines an affine lower cut in \(x\), with slope \(-B_n^{\mathsf T}\pi\), for the nested master.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For network-flow recourse, dual node potentials produce valid affine Benders cuts while preserving specialized network solution structure.
assumptions_latex: The primal network-flow recourse problem is feasible and bounded.
\(A_n\) is a node-arc incidence matrix.
Linear-programming strong duality applies.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q_n(x)\geq\pi^{\mathsf T}(b_n-B_nx)-u_n^{\mathsf T}s^++\ell_n^{\mathsf T}s^-\) for every dual-feasible \((\pi,s^+,s^-)\).

children.title: Quadratic-Structure Exploitation

knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic-Structure Exploitation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reuse of fixed quadratic and constraint structure across repeated node solves.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a node family \(\min_y\{\tfrac12y^{\mathsf T}Hy+q_k^{\mathsf T}y:A y=b_k-Bx_k\}\) with fixed \(H\succ0\) and fixed full-row-rank \(A\), initialize by factorizing the saddle-point matrix \[K=\begin{bmatrix}H&A^{\mathsf T}\\A&0\end{bmatrix}.\] At each nested-decomposition iteration \(k\), solve \(K(y_k,\lambda_k)^{\mathsf T}=(-q_k,b_k-Bx_k)^{\mathsf T}\) using the stored factorization, form the value-function slope \(B^{\mathsf T}\lambda_k\), and add its supporting cut. Stop when the global decomposition gap reaches tolerance; output the incumbent decisions and cuts. Reuse changes factorization cost, not the exact node solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When node Hessians and constraint matrices stay fixed, one KKT factorization can serve repeated solves and their multiplier-based cuts.
assumptions_latex: \(H\succ0\) and \(A\) has full row rank.
Only linear objective terms, right-hand sides, or predecessor states vary between solves.
The displayed equality-constrained quadratic model is feasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each iteration requires triangular solves with the stored factorization of \(K\), and \(B^{\mathsf T}\lambda_k\) is the value slope under the displayed KKT convention.

notation.meaning: iteration-k multiplier for the equality \(Ay=b_k-Bx_k\) under the displayed KKT convention

children.title: Cross-Block Coupling Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Couplings that weaken or prevent block-level decomposition.

knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Block Coupling Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A coupling constraint that prevents independent block minimization despite a separable objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider two scalar blocks and the convex recourse problem \[V(x)=\min_{y_1,y_2}\left\{\tfrac12y_1^2+\tfrac12y_2^2:y_1+y_2=x\right\}.\] The unique optimizer is \(y_1=y_2=x/2\), so \(V(x)=x^2/4\). Solving the blocks independently omits the shared equality and cannot enforce feasibility or recover this value. More generally, exact blockwise nested decomposition requires coupling constraints to be absent, assigned to an explicit coordinating master, or represented through interface variables or dual prices; otherwise independently generated block cuts need not constitute the original node value function.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A shared constraint couples otherwise separable quadratic blocks, so independent block solves are invalid unless a master or dual coordination mechanism represents the coupling.
assumptions_latex: \(x\in\mathbb R\).
Both block variables are unrestricted real scalars.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(V(x)=x^2/4\), and the equality \(y_1+y_2=x\) prevents uncoordinated block decomposition.
