children.title: Single-Cut SDDP
children.top_down_role: Stagewise value approximation using aggregated cut information.

assumptions_latex: At stage \(t\), outcomes \(j=1,\ldots,J_t\) have probabilities \(p_{tj}>0\) with \(\sum_jp_{tj}=1\).
Each backward solve returns a valid child cut \(a_{tj}^k+(b_{tj}^k)^{\mathsf T}x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\underline V_t^K(x)=\max_{1\le k\le K}\sum_{j=1}^{J_t}p_{tj}\bigl(a_{tj}^k+(b_{tj}^k)^{\mathsf T}x\bigr)\) is the single-cut stage model.

notation.meaning: probability of child outcome j at stage t
single-cut lower approximation after K iterations

review_flags: Source locators support decomposition and aggregation only indirectly
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Risk-neutral finite-support SDDP with one aggregated value variable per stage.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each backward iteration \(k\), solve every child-outcome subproblem \(j=1,\ldots,J_t\) at the trial state and obtain a valid affine cut \(a_{tj}^k+(b_{tj}^k)^{\mathsf T}x\). Form one probability-weighted cut \(A_t^k+(B_t^k)^{\mathsf T}x\), where \(A_t^k=\sum_jp_{tj}a_{tj}^k\) and \(B_t^k=\sum_jp_{tj}b_{tj}^k\). Append the constraint \(\theta_t\ge A_t^k+(B_t^k)^{\mathsf T}x\). After \(K\) iterations, output the lower model \(\underline V_t^K(x)=\max_{1\le k\le K}\{A_t^k+(B_t^k)^{\mathsf T}x\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Single-cut SDDP averages all child-outcome cuts generated in an iteration and adds one probability-weighted affine cut to the stage value approximation.
knowledge_statements.title: Single-Cut SDDP

children.title: Multicut SDDP
children.top_down_role: Value approximation retaining disaggregated outcome or state cuts.

assumptions_latex: At stage \(t\), outcome \(j\) has probability \(p_{tj}>0\).
Every outcome-specific backward oracle returns globally valid affine lower cuts.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\underline V_t^K(x)=\sum_{j=1}^{J_t}p_{tj}\max_{1\le k\le K}\bigl\{a_{tj}^k+(b_{tj}^k)^{\mathsf T}x\bigr\}\) is the multicut stage model.

notation.meaning: multicut lower approximation after K iterations

review_flags: Source locators support decomposition and aggregation only indirectly
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Risk-neutral finite-support SDDP with a separate value model for each child outcome.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every child outcome \(j\), maintain a separate epigraph variable \(\theta_{tj}\). At backward iteration \(k\), solve the outcome-specific subproblem and append \(\theta_{tj}\ge a_{tj}^k+(b_{tj}^k)^{\mathsf T}x\). The parent problem uses \(\sum_jp_{tj}\theta_{tj}\) as its downstream-cost approximation. After \(K\) iterations, output \(\underline V_t^K(x)=\sum_{j=1}^{J_t}p_{tj}\max_{1\le k\le K}\{a_{tj}^k+(b_{tj}^k)^{\mathsf T}x\}\). Thus maximization over stored cuts occurs separately before probability aggregation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multicut SDDP maintains one cut model per child outcome and aggregates their epigraph values by probability in the parent-stage problem.
knowledge_statements.title: Multicut SDDP

children.title: Hybrid-Cut SDDP
children.top_down_role: Intermediate SDDP designs using partial or changing cut aggregation.

assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal P_t\) is a partition of the stage-\(t\) outcome set, and \(p_{tG}=\sum_{j\in G}p_{tj}>0\) for each \(G\in\mathcal P_t\).
Outcome-specific backward solves return valid affine lower cuts.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\underline V_t^K(x)=\sum_{G\in\mathcal P_t}\max_{1\le k\le K}\sum_{j\in G}p_{tj}\bigl(a_{tj}^k+(b_{tj}^k)^{\mathsf T}x\bigr)\) interpolates between single-cut and multicut models.

notation.meaning: partition of outcomes into cut-aggregation groups

review_flags: Hybrid grouping convention is not directly supported by the supplied locator
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Partition-based hybrid between stagewise single-cut and outcome-wise multicut SDDP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose a partition \(\mathcal P_t\) of the child outcomes. For each group \(G\in\mathcal P_t\) and backward iteration \(k\), aggregate the child cuts inside that group and append \(\theta_{tG}\ge\sum_{j\in G}p_{tj}\bigl(a_{tj}^k+(b_{tj}^k)^{\mathsf T}x\bigr)\). The parent uses \(\sum_{G\in\mathcal P_t}\theta_{tG}\). After \(K\) iterations, output \(\underline V_t^K(x)=\sum_{G\in\mathcal P_t}\max_{1\le k\le K}\sum_{j\in G}p_{tj}\bigl(a_{tj}^k+(b_{tj}^k)^{\mathsf T}x\bigr)\). One group gives single-cut SDDP; singleton groups give multicut SDDP.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Hybrid-cut SDDP partitions child outcomes, aggregates cuts within each group, and maintains separate epigraph models across groups.
knowledge_statements.title: Hybrid-Cut SDDP

children.title: Cut-Regime Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Comparison of approximation strength, storage, plus subproblem granularity.

assumptions_latex: The single-cut, hybrid, and multicut models use the same outcome-specific affine cuts \(c_{jk}(x)\).
Hybrid partitions are ordered by refinement.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_{\mathrm{single}}(x)\le L_{\mathcal P}(x)\le L_{\mathrm{multi}}(x)\) for every state \(x\), while finer partitions require weakly more epigraph constraints and variables.

notation.meaning: hybrid lower model induced by partition P
affine cut k for outcome j, including its probability weight

review_flags: Tightness ordering follows algebraically, but implementation tradeoffs need empirical sourcing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise model-strength and storage ordering for identical generated cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(c_{jk}(x)\) be the probability-weighted affine cut for outcome \(j\) generated at iteration \(k\). For the same cut collection, define \(L_{\mathrm{single}}(x)=\max_k\sum_jc_{jk}(x)\), \(L_{\mathcal P}(x)=\sum_{G\in\mathcal P}\max_k\sum_{j\in G}c_{jk}(x)\), and \(L_{\mathrm{multi}}(x)=\sum_j\max_kc_{jk}(x)\). Then \(L_{\mathrm{single}}(x)\le L_{\mathcal P}(x)\le L_{\mathrm{multi}}(x)\) for every \(x\). Refining \(\mathcal P\) weakly strengthens the lower approximation but weakly increases the number of epigraph blocks and stored constraints; runtime need not be monotone because stronger bounds can reduce iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For identical cuts, multicut models are pointwise strongest, single-cut models weakest, and partition hybrids intermediate; finer models consume more storage but may need fewer iterations.
knowledge_statements.title: Cut-Regime Tradeoffs

children.title: Cut Selection
children.top_down_role: Retention or activation of cuts judged relevant to current value approximations.

knowledge_statements.title: Cut Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reference-state activity selection for a finite pool of affine lower cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a finite cut pool \(I\), reference states \(R\), and tolerance \(\tau\ge0\). Evaluate \(v(x)=\max_{\ell\in I}\{a_\ell+b_\ell^{\mathsf T}x\}\) for every \(x\in R\). Select \(S=\bigcup_{x\in R}\{\ell\in I:a_\ell+b_\ell^{\mathsf T}x\ge v(x)-\tau\}\); optionally force inclusion of newly generated or otherwise protected cuts. Output the restricted model \(\underline V_S(x)=\max_{\ell\in S}\{a_\ell+b_\ell^{\mathsf T}x\}\). For \(\tau=0\), at least one maximizer at every reference state is retained, ensuring \(\underline V_S(x)=v(x)\) on \(R\), though equality away from \(R\) is not guaranteed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Select cuts that are active or nearly active at reference states, retaining at least one maximizer per state; the restricted model agrees there but may weaken elsewhere.
assumptions_latex: The current model is \(\underline V(x)=\max_{\ell\in I}\{a_\ell+b_\ell^{\mathsf T}x\}\).
A finite reference set \(R\) and tie tolerance \(\tau\ge0\) are supplied.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S=\bigcup_{x\in R}\{\ell\in I:a_\ell+b_\ell^{\mathsf T}x\ge\underline V(x)-\tau\}\) is the selected cut set.

notation.meaning: indices of all stored cuts and selected cuts

review_flags: Specific SDDP cut-selection policy requires an authoritative source

children.title: Cut Deletion
children.top_down_role: Removal of inactive, dominated, or low-value stored cuts.

knowledge_statements.title: Cut Deletion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Model-preserving deletion by certified global dominance on the state domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input the state domain \(X\), cut indices \(I\), and affine cuts \(q_\ell(x)=a_\ell+b_\ell^{\mathsf T}x\). For a candidate cut \(r\), certify \(d_r=\sup_{x\in X}\{q_r(x)-\max_{\ell\in I\setminus\{r\}}q_\ell(x)\}\le0\). If certified, delete \(r\); otherwise retain it. Repeat until no tested cut is globally dominated, and output the remaining pool. Each accepted deletion preserves \(\max_{\ell\in I}q_\ell(x)\) for every \(x\in X\), hence preserves both lower-bound validity and all decisions based solely on that model. Deletion based only on inactivity at sampled states lacks this global preservation guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Delete a cut only after certifying that the remaining pool dominates it everywhere on the state domain; such deletion leaves the lower approximation unchanged.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is the state domain and \(q_\ell(x)=a_\ell+b_\ell^{\mathsf T}x\) are stored affine cuts.
For a candidate \(r\), the dominance test \(\sup_{x\in X}\bigl(q_r(x)-\max_{\ell\ne r}q_\ell(x)\bigr)\le0\) is certified exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\max_{\ell\in I}q_\ell(x)=\max_{\ell\in I\setminus\{r\}}q_\ell(x)\) for every \(x\in X\), so deleting \(r\) preserves the lower model.

notation.meaning: state domain and current cut-index set

review_flags: Exact dominance testing may be computationally difficult on general domains

children.title: Cut Activity Metrics
children.top_down_role: Measures used to assess cut relevance across sampled states.

knowledge_statements.title: Cut Activity Metrics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Metrics for ranking affine lower cuts in an SDDP stagewise value-function approximation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\underline Q_t^k(x)=\max_{j\in J_t^k}\{\alpha_{tj}+\beta_{tj}^{\mathsf T}x\}\) and let \(x_t^1,\ldots,x_t^k\) be trial states. For tolerance \(\tau\geq0\), define cut \(j\)'s activity indicator by \(A_{tj}^{\ell}=\mathbf 1\{\alpha_{tj}+\beta_{tj}^{\mathsf T}x_t^{\ell}\geq \underline Q_t^k(x_t^{\ell})-\tau\}\). Its cumulative frequency is \(F_{tj}^k=k^{-1}\sum_{\ell=1}^k A_{tj}^{\ell}\), its last-active iteration is \(R_{tj}^k=\max(\{\ell:A_{tj}^{\ell}=1\}\cup\{0\})\), and its inactivity age is \(G_{tj}^k=k-R_{tj}^k\). These metrics depend on the sampled trial-state history and do not establish global redundancy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Activity frequency, last-active iteration, and inactivity age summarize a cut's behavior on sampled trial states but do not prove global redundancy.
assumptions_latex: \(J_t^k\) is a finite cut index set.
All cut values are finite at the recorded trial states.

notation.meaning: cuts retained for stage t after iteration k
frequency, last-active iteration, and inactivity age

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definitions are internally coherent and fit the Cut Activity Metrics leaf, but no source supports these particular SDDP activity metrics or their interpretation. Also clarify that k is positive and that j belongs to the current cut set.

children.title: Aggressive-Pruning Failure
children.top_down_role: Approximation or convergence risks caused by excessive cut removal.

knowledge_statements.title: Aggressive-Pruning Failure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A sampled-inactivity rule can delete a cut needed elsewhere in the state space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \(X=[-1,1]\), consider the valid lower-cut model \(Q(x)=\max\{x,-x\}=|x|\). If trial states repeatedly equal \(1\), the cut \(-x\) is inactive there and an aggressive inactivity rule may delete it. The retained approximation becomes \(\widetilde Q(x)=x\). It remains a lower bound, but at \(x=-1\) it gives \(\widetilde Q(-1)=-1\) whereas \(Q(-1)=1\). Moreover, minimizing the retained model over \(X\) selects \(-1\), while minimizing \(Q\) selects \(0\). Thus sampled inactivity alone neither certifies redundancy nor preserves decision quality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cut inactive at repeatedly sampled states can be essential elsewhere; deleting it may create a large local error and change the minimizing decision.
assumptions_latex: The pruning rule deletes a cut solely because it is inactive on observed trial states.
No global dominance test is performed before deletion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q(-1)-\widetilde Q(-1)=2\), and \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}\widetilde Q(x)=\{-1\}\neq\{0\}=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}Q(x)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The calculation is correct and counterexample is the appropriate kind for this failure leaf, but the record has no cited evidence or explicit standard-field rationale as required by the common contract.

children.title: Regularized SDDP
children.top_down_role: SDDP variants using penalties or proximal terms to stabilize trial decisions.

knowledge_statements.title: Regularized SDDP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Forward-pass quadratic stabilization with unregularized backward cut generation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iteration \(k\), stage \(t\), trial state \(x_{t-1}^k\), and reference decision \(\bar x_t^k\), compute the forward decision by minimizing \(c_t(x_t,\xi_t^k)+\underline Q_{t+1}^{k-1}(x_t)+(\lambda_t^k/2)\lVert x_t-\bar x_t^k\rVert^2\) over the feasible set \(X_t(x_{t-1}^k,\xi_t^k)\), where \(\lambda_t^k\geq0\). In the backward pass, solve the original unregularized stage problem at sampled predecessor states, obtain a supporting affine lower cut from its value and a state subgradient, and append that cut to \(\underline Q_t^{k-1}\). Stop under the chosen statistical or bound-gap test and return the unregularized policy induced by the accumulated cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Regularized SDDP stabilizes forward decisions with a proximal penalty while generating backward cuts from the original, unregularized recourse problems.
assumptions_latex: Each stage subproblem is convex and admits a state subgradient at sampled states.
The backward oracle produces valid lower supporting cuts.
\(\lambda_t^k\geq0\) is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The update preserves lower-cut validity for the original cost-to-go functions because regularization is excluded from backward cut targets.

notation.meaning: stage-t polyhedral lower approximation after iteration k

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits the leaf, but a general regularized-decomposition section does not reliably establish the stated SDDP forward/backward separation, stopping rule, or returned-policy claim. A specific regularized-SDDP source is required.

children.title: Trust-Region SDDP
children.top_down_role: SDDP variants restricting trial decisions to localized regions.

knowledge_statements.title: Trust-Region SDDP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Forward exploration restricted around a reference policy while backward cuts remain globally valid.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a center \(\bar x_t^k\) and radius \(\Delta_t^k>0\), the forward pass at stage \(t\) solves the sampled SDDP subproblem subject additionally to \(\lVert x_t-\bar x_t^k\rVert\leq\Delta_t^k\). The backward pass omits this artificial trust-region constraint and constructs supporting lower cuts for the original recourse function. After comparing an observed merit improvement with the improvement predicted by the current model, accept or reject the trial center and shrink, retain, or enlarge \(\Delta_t^k\). Terminate under a prescribed bound-gap or statistical rule; output the policy defined by the cuts for the original stage problems.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Trust-region SDDP restricts forward trial decisions near a center, adapts the radius, and generates backward cuts without the artificial restriction.
assumptions_latex: Original stage subproblems are convex and have valid backward cut oracles.
\(\Delta_t^k>0\) at every finite iteration.
The acceptance statistic uses a consistently defined merit estimate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Backward cuts remain lower bounds for the original recourse functions when the artificial trust region is absent from their defining subproblems.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The content kind and local topic fit, but the precise trust-region SDDP mechanism, merit ratio, center acceptance, radius updates, and omission of the region from backward problems require a specific source.

children.title: Adaptive Stabilization Schedules
children.top_down_role: Iteration-dependent adjustment of regularization strength or trust-region size.

knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive Stabilization Schedules
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feedback rule for varying proximal weights or trust-region radii across SDDP iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p_k>0\) and \(a_k\) denote predicted and observed merit decreases, and set \(\rho_k=a_k/p_k\). Fix \(0<\eta_1<\eta_2<1\), \(\gamma_+>1\), and \(0<\gamma_-<1\). For proximal stabilization, update \(\lambda_{k+1}=\gamma_+\lambda_k\) when \(\rho_k<\eta_1\), set \(\lambda_{k+1}=\lambda_k\) when \(\eta_1\leq\rho_k<\eta_2\), and set \(\lambda_{k+1}=\gamma_-\lambda_k\) otherwise. For a trust region, apply the inverse scaling to its radius. Safeguard parameters within prescribed finite intervals and stop only under the parent SDDP termination test.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An agreement ratio strengthens stabilization after poor model agreement and relaxes it after good agreement, subject to parameter safeguards.
assumptions_latex: The predicted decrease satisfies \(p_k>0\).
Observed and predicted decreases use the same merit convention.
Parameter updates are clipped to prescribed safeguard intervals.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Poor agreement increases the proximal weight or decreases the trust radius; good agreement performs the converse.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: This is an algorithmic schedule appropriate to the leaf, but the proposed ratio and update directions are variant-dependent, especially under stochastic merit estimates. No source fixes the estimator, acceptance convention, or safeguards.

children.title: Stabilization-Bias Boundary
children.top_down_role: Distortion or stalling caused by excessive or persistent stabilization.

knowledge_statements.title: Stabilization-Bias Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Persistent stabilization changes the target when incorporated into backward value cuts or the reported policy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Stabilization is bias-free for the original SDDP model only when artificial penalties or restrictions guide trial-point selection without entering the backward Bellman target or final decision problem, or when their limiting effect vanishes. For a concrete boundary, minimize \(f(x)=(x-1)^2\) over \(\mathbb R\). Adding the persistent penalty \((\lambda/2)x^2\) with \(\lambda>0\) changes the unique minimizer from \(x^\star=1\) to \(x_\lambda=2/(2+\lambda)\). Hence cuts or policies derived from the permanently stabilized objective generally represent a perturbed problem rather than the original one.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stabilization becomes biased when a nonvanishing penalty or restriction enters backward targets or final decisions instead of only guiding trial points.
assumptions_latex: The stabilization term is artificial and absent from the original objective.
Its weight remains \(\lambda>0\) in the target problem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_\lambda=2/(2+\lambda)\neq1=x^\star\) for every \(\lambda>0\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The scalar example is mathematically correct and the failure-boundary kind fits. However, the broader claim about backward Bellman targets, final policies, and vanishing limiting effects is not established by the example alone and has no cited source.

knowledge_statements.title: Risk-Averse SDDP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Time-consistent convex risk recursion approximated by stagewise affine lower cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For stages \(t=1,\ldots,T\), define \(V_{T+1}\equiv0\) and the risk-averse Bellman recursion \[V_t(s)=\inf_{x\in X_t(s)}\left\{c_t(s,x)+\rho_t\bigl(V_{t+1}(S_{t+1})\mid s,x\bigr)\right\}.\] Here each \(\rho_t\) is a conditional monotone, translation-equivariant convex risk mapping, and nesting these mappings specifies a time-consistent objective. Risk-averse SDDP replaces \(V_t\) by maxima of affine lower cuts; backward subproblems evaluate the conditional risk mapping, or its dual risk-envelope maximization, and use resulting state subgradients to construct valid cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Risk-averse SDDP applies affine lower-cut approximations to a time-consistent Bellman recursion built from nested conditional convex risk mappings.
assumptions_latex: The multistage model is convex and relatively complete recourse holds.
Each conditional risk mapping is monotone, translation equivariant, and convex.
The backward risk evaluation yields valid values and state subgradients.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed nested recursion defines the time-consistent risk-averse cost-to-go functions targeted by the SDDP cuts.

notation.meaning: risk-averse cost-to-go function at stage t

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation fits Risk-Averse SDDP, but the exact conditional-risk assumptions, nesting/time-consistency statement, dual-envelope evaluation, and cut-validity conditions are specialized claims requiring an authoritative source.

children.title: Periodic SDDP
children.top_down_role: SDDP for systems whose data or dynamics repeat over a fixed cycle.

knowledge_statements.title: Periodic SDDP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Phase-indexed Bellman and cut approximations for periodically repeating long-horizon data.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the model data repeat with period \(p\geq1\), let \(r\in\{0,\ldots,p-1\}\) denote phase, and let \(r^+=(r+1)\bmod p\). Under discount factor \(0<\beta<1\), the phase value functions satisfy \[V_r(s)=\inf_{x\in X_r(s)}\left\{c_r(s,x)+\beta\,\mathbb E\left[V_{r^+}(S')\mid s,x,r\right]\right\}.\] Periodic SDDP maintains a separate polyhedral lower approximation \(\underline V_r\) and cut pool for each phase, samples transitions cyclically by phase, and sends every backward cut only to the pool indexed by its generating phase.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Periodic SDDP represents repeating long-horizon dynamics with one Bellman function and one cut pool for each phase of the cycle.
assumptions_latex: Costs, feasible correspondences, and transition laws repeat every \(p\) stages.
Stage problems are convex and admit valid supporting cuts.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Only \(p\) phase-indexed value approximations are required, with the successor relation \(r^+=(r+1)\bmod p\).

notation.meaning: value function associated with phase r

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The phase-indexed discounted recursion is coherent and fits the leaf, but the asserted periodic-SDDP cut-pool and cyclic sampling algorithm has no supporting citation.

children.title: Infinite-Horizon SDDP
children.top_down_role: SDDP formulations without a fixed terminal stage.

knowledge_statements.title: Infinite-Horizon SDDP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stationary discounted SDDP using a shared lower approximation of the fixed-point value function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a stationary convex model with \(0<\beta<1\), initialize a convex lower bound \(\underline V^0\leq V\). At iteration \(k\), simulate a finite forward trajectory using decisions that minimize \(c(s,x)+\beta\,\mathbb E[\underline V^{k-1}(S')\mid s,x]\). In the backward sweep, evaluate the same stationary Bellman subproblem at visited states, obtain a supporting affine lower cut, and set \(\underline V^k\) to the maximum of \(\underline V^{k-1}\) and all new cuts. Reuse this single cut pool at every time position; terminate using a prescribed residual, bound-gap, or simulation criterion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Infinite-horizon SDDP repeatedly adds cuts to one stationary value approximation and reuses that approximation at every simulated time position.
assumptions_latex: The stationary Bellman operator is well defined on bounded value functions.
\(0<\beta<1\), and one-stage costs are bounded below.
Backward subproblems provide valid supporting lower cuts.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The algorithm targets the fixed point \(V=\mathcal T V\) of the stationary discounted Bellman operator \(\mathcal T\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cited sections concern infinite-horizon dynamic programming and value iteration generally; they do not reliably support the specific stationary SDDP forward simulation, backward affine-cut construction, shared cut pool, or termination criteria.

children.title: Stationary Value Approximations
children.top_down_role: Time-invariant or phase-indexed value approximations for recurring horizons.

knowledge_statements.title: Stationary Value Approximations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A time-shared polyhedral lower representation for a stationary convex cost-to-go function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: When costs, feasible correspondences, and transition kernels are time homogeneous, a stationary convex value approximation can be represented by \[\underline V^k(s)=\max_{j\in J^k}\left\{\alpha_j+\beta_j^{\mathsf T}s\right\}.\] The same function and cut pool are used at every time position. If every affine term is a global lower bound on the stationary Bellman fixed point \(V\), then their maximum also satisfies \(\underline V^k(s)\leq V(s)\) for every state \(s\). Adding a valid cut enlarges the approximation pointwise without destroying the lower-bound property.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stationarity permits one maximum-of-affine-cuts value approximation to be shared across time, with valid cut additions improving it monotonically.
assumptions_latex: The infinite-horizon model is time homogeneous.
The target value function is convex on its state domain.
Every retained affine cut globally underestimates \(V\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\underline V^k\leq V\), and valid cut addition gives \(\underline V^{k+1}\geq\underline V^k\) pointwise.

notation.meaning: intercept and state slope of cut j

source_refs.locator: 4.7 Low-Dimensional Representations of Value Functions p. 144

source_witnesses.locator: 4.7 Low-Dimensional Representations of Value Functions p. 144

children.title: Horizon-Truncation Boundary
children.top_down_role: Approximation limits introduced by finite surrogates for indefinite-horizon problems.

knowledge_statements.title: Horizon-Truncation Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Discounting controls the omitted tail; without tail decay, finite truncation need not approximate the infinite horizon.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(0<\beta<1\) and every one-stage cost satisfies \(|c_t|\leq C\). Truncating an infinite discounted objective after stages \(0,\ldots,H-1\) omits a tail whose absolute value is at most \[\sum_{t=H}^{\infty}\beta^t C=\frac{C\beta^H}{1-\beta}.\] Thus choosing \(H\) with \(C\beta^H/(1-\beta)\leq\varepsilon\) ensures truncation error at most \(\varepsilon\), uniformly over policies. This guarantee fails at the boundary \(\beta=1\): the bounded cost sequence \(c_t=1\) has an infinite undiscounted tail for every finite \(H\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bounded discounted tails yield a geometric truncation bound; at unit discount, bounded stage costs alone provide no finite uniform tail guarantee.
assumptions_latex: \(|c_t|\leq C<\infty\) for every stage and admissible policy.
\(0<\beta<1\) for the geometric bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The uniform tail error is at most \(C\beta^H/(1-\beta)\); no analogous finite bound follows from bounded costs alone when \(\beta=1\).

notation.meaning: uniform absolute bound on one-stage cost

knowledge_statements.title: Iteration-Complexity Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classification by the iteration count required to close a certified or statistically controlled SDDP gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L_k\) be an SDDP lower bound after iteration \(k\), let \(U_k\) be a valid upper confidence bound with prescribed coverage \(1-\delta\), and define \(G_k=U_k-L_k\). The \((\varepsilon,\delta)\)-iteration complexity is \(K(\varepsilon,\delta)=\inf\{k:G_k\leq\varepsilon\}\). A regime is finite-termination if \(K\) is uniformly bounded for fixed finite problem data, geometric if \(K=O(\log(1/\varepsilon))\), polynomial if \(K=O(\varepsilon^{-q})\) for some \(q>0\), and asymptotic-without-rate when convergence is known but no finite bound of these forms is established under the stated oracle and sampling model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Iteration complexity counts iterations until a confidence-controlled upper bound and deterministic lower bound differ by at most the requested tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(L_k\) is a valid lower bound.
\(U_k\) has coverage at least \(1-\delta\).
Each iteration uses the explicitly fixed sampling and subproblem-oracle model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K(\varepsilon,delta)\) classifies finite-termination, geometric, polynomial, or unquantified asymptotic iteration regimes.

notation.meaning: iterations required to reach tolerance epsilon at confidence level one minus delta

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity taxonomy and confidence-controlled stopping definition require a source. Pointwise coverage of U_k does not by itself guarantee coverage at the data-dependent stopping iteration, and the sampling/oracle probability model is insufficiently specified. The conclusion also writes delta as plain letters in \(K(\varepsilon,delta)\) rather than \(K(\varepsilon,\delta)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Sampling-Complexity Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-policy Monte Carlo evaluation under bounded, independent simulation outputs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Z_1,\ldots,Z_N\) be independent policy-cost observations with \(Z_i\in[a,b]\) almost surely and \(J=\mathbb E[Z_i]\). For \(\widehat J_N=N^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^N Z_i\), Hoeffding's inequality gives \[\mathbb P\!\left(\lvert\widehat J_N-J\rvert>\varepsilon\right)\le 2\exp\!\left(-\frac{2N\varepsilon^2}{(b-a)^2}\right).\] Consequently, confidence at least \(1-\delta\) is obtained whenever \[N\ge \frac{(b-a)^2}{2\varepsilon^2}\log\!\frac{2}{\delta}.\] Thus bounded-cost policy evaluation has sampling complexity \(O(\varepsilon^{-2}\log(1/\delta))\); any horizon dependence enters through the range \(b-a\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bounded independent policy simulations require order epsilon-inverse-squared times log confidence-inverse samples; horizon dependence is carried by the total-cost range.
assumptions_latex: \(Z_1,\ldots,Z_N\) are independent and identically distributed.
\(a\le Z_i\le b\) almost surely.
\(\varepsilon>0\) and \(0<\delta<1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N\ge (b-a)^2\log(2/\delta)/(2\varepsilon^2)\) implies \(\mathbb P(|\widehat J_N-J|\le\varepsilon)\ge1-\delta\).

notation.meaning: Expected cost of the fixed policy

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The bounded-i.i.d. Hoeffding bound and resulting sampling rate are mathematically correct, but no inspectable source supports either the concentration result or its placement in the SDDP taxonomy.

knowledge_statements.title: Stage-Horizon Dependence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive propagation of uniform Bellman-approximation errors over a finite horizon.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a finite-horizon dynamic program with stages \(t=1,\ldots,T\), terminal values \(V_{T+1}=\widehat V_{T+1}=0\), and Bellman operators \(\mathcal T_t\) that are nonexpansive in the supremum norm. Let \(V_t=\mathcal T_tV_{t+1}\), and suppose \(\lVert\widehat V_t-\mathcal T_t\widehat V_{t+1}\rVert_\infty\le\varepsilon_t\) for every \(t=1,\ldots,T\). Then \[\lVert\widehat V_t-V_t\rVert_\infty\le\sum_{s=t}^{T}\varepsilon_s.\] In particular, if \(\varepsilon_t\le\bar\varepsilon\) at every stage, then \(\lVert\widehat V_1-V_1\rVert_\infty\le T\bar\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the exact and approximate terminal values agree, uniform stagewise Bellman residuals accumulate additively; equal residual tolerances therefore give linear horizon dependence.
assumptions_latex: \(T<\infty\) and \(V_{T+1}=\widehat V_{T+1}=0\).
Each \(\mathcal T_t\) is nonexpansive in the supremum norm.
For every \(t=1,\ldots,T\), the residual is bounded by \(\varepsilon_t\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lVert\widehat V_t-V_t\rVert_\infty\le\sum_{s=t}^{T}\varepsilon_s\).

notation.meaning: Exact and approximate stage-t value functions

children.title: State-Dimension Scaling
children.top_down_role: Computational dependence on the dimension of stagewise state representations.

knowledge_statements.title: State-Dimension Scaling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Storage and evaluation cost of affine SDDP cuts in a finite-dimensional state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At stage \(t\), let the post-decision state lie in \(\mathbb R^{d_t}\), and represent a lower approximation by \[\underline V_t(x)=\max_{1\le j\le K_t}\{\alpha_{tj}+\beta_{tj}^{\mathsf T}x\}.\] Each affine cut requires one intercept and \(d_t\) slope coefficients. Hence storing \(K_t\) dense cuts requires exactly \(K_t(d_t+1)\) scalar coefficients, while direct evaluation of every cut at one state requires \(O(K_td_t)\) arithmetic operations. Across all nonterminal stages, dense coefficient storage is \(\sum_tK_t(d_t+1)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dense affine cut stores one intercept and one coefficient per state coordinate, so storage and direct evaluation scale linearly in state dimension.
assumptions_latex: Stage-t states belong to \(\mathbb R^{d_t}\).
Cut slopes are stored densely.
The approximation contains \(K_t\) affine cuts at stage \(t\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S=\sum_tK_t(d_t+1)\) stored scalars and stage-t evaluation cost \(O(K_td_t)\).

notation.meaning: Intercept and slope of cut j

source_refs.locator: 4.7 Low-Dimensional Representations of Value Functions p. 144

source_witnesses.locator: 4.7 Low-Dimensional Representations of Value Functions p. 144

children.title: Cut-Storage Scaling
children.top_down_role: Memory growth from value-function cuts across stages, states, or outcomes.

knowledge_statements.title: Cut-Storage Scaling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scaling with the number of retained affine cuts across SDDP stages.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose stage \(t\) retains \(K_t\) dense affine cuts over states in \(\mathbb R^{d_t}\). Without coefficient sharing, total storage is \[S=\sum_{t=2}^{T}K_t(d_t+1)\] scalar values. Adding one cut at stage \(t\) increases storage by \(d_t+1\), and an iteration adding at most \(m_t\) cuts there increases storage by at most \(m_t(d_t+1)\). After \(n\) iterations, if no cuts are deleted and at most \(m_t\) are added per iteration, then \(K_t\le K_t^{(0)}+nm_t\), so storage grows at most linearly in \(n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With dense affine cuts, memory is linear in retained cut count; bounded additions per iteration therefore produce at most linear iteration-wise storage growth.
assumptions_latex: Cuts are stored as dense intercept-slope vectors.
At most \(m_t\) cuts are added at stage \(t\) per iteration.
No cuts are deleted during the stated growth calculation.

notation.meaning: Maximum new stage-t cuts per iteration

children.title: High-Dimensional Cut Geometry
children.top_down_role: Geometric effects of increasing state dimension on cut relevance plus coverage.

knowledge_statements.title: High-Dimensional Cut Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polyhedral geometry of max-affine lower approximations on polyhedral state domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) be a convex polyhedron, and let \(\ell_j(x)=\alpha_j+\beta_j^{\mathsf T}x\) for \(j=1,\ldots,K\). The function \[\underline V(x)=\max_{1\le j\le K}\ell_j(x)\] is convex and polyhedral on \(X\). Cut \(j\) is active on the polyhedron \[R_j=\{x\in X:\ell_j(x)\ge\ell_i(x)\text{ for every }i=1,\ldots,K\}.\] A cut with empty \(R_j\) is redundant on \(X\). If every \(\ell_j\) underestimates a function \(V:X\to\mathbb R\), then \(\underline V(x)\le V(x)\) for every \(x\in X\), independently of \(d\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a polyhedral state domain, the maximum of finitely many affine cuts is a convex polyhedral model, each active region is polyhedral, and the maximum remains a valid lower bound when every cut is valid.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) is a convex polyhedron.
The family consists of \(K<\infty\) affine functions.
For the lower-bound claim, \(\ell_j(x)\le V(x)\) for every \(x\in X\) and every \(j\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\underline V=\max_j\ell_j\) is convex and polyhedral on \(X\), each \(R_j\) is polyhedral, and \(\underline V\le V\) when every cut is valid.

notation.meaning: Region on which cut j is active

source_refs.locator: 4.7 Low-Dimensional Representations of Value Functions p. 144

source_witnesses.locator: 4.7 Low-Dimensional Representations of Value Functions p. 144

children.title: Storage-Limited Regimes
children.top_down_role: Problem regimes where retained cuts become the dominant computational constraint.

knowledge_statements.title: Storage-Limited Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consequences of enforcing a finite coefficient budget on max-affine lower models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a storage budget permit at most \(B\) scalar coefficients and let stage \(t\) use dense cuts of size \(d_t+1\). Any retained cut counts \(K_t\) must satisfy \[\sum_tK_t(d_t+1)\le B.\] Replacing a valid max-affine lower model by the maximum over a retained subset preserves lower-bound validity but can only decrease the model pointwise. In particular, if all stages have dimension at least \(d_{\min}\), then the total retained cut count cannot exceed \(\lfloor B/(d_{\min}+1)\rfloor\). Thus fixed storage prevents unbounded cut accumulation and may destroy previously attained local tightness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed memory budget caps retained cuts. Pruning preserves validity of lower bounds but can weaken them and remove tightness at previously represented states.
assumptions_latex: The coefficient budget is \(B<\infty\).
Cuts are stored densely.
Pruning retains a subset of individually valid lower cuts.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_tK_t(d_t+1)\le B\), and pruning yields \(\underline V_t^{\mathrm{new}}\le\underline V_t^{\mathrm{old}}\le V_t\).

notation.meaning: Minimum state dimension among represented stages

source_refs.locator: 4.7 Low-Dimensional Representations of Value Functions p. 144

source_witnesses.locator: 4.7 Low-Dimensional Representations of Value Functions p. 144

knowledge_statements.title: Deterministic Value-Function Lower Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pathwise-valid SDDP lower approximations as deterministic optimal-value certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V_t\) be the exact cost-to-go functions of a minimization dynamic program, and let \(\underline V_{T+1}=V_{T+1}\). Suppose every stored stage-t cut is a global lower bound on the Bellman image formed using \(\underline V_{t+1}\), and define \(\underline V_t\) as their maximum. Monotonicity of the Bellman operators implies \(\underline V_t(x)\le V_t(x)\) for every admissible state and stage. Therefore \(L=\underline V_1(x_1)\) is a deterministic lower bound on the optimal value \(V_1(x_1)\), requiring no policy-evaluation sampling.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Globally valid cuts propagated backward through monotone Bellman operators yield a deterministic initial lower bound on the optimal multistage value.
assumptions_latex: The problem is a finite-horizon minimization dynamic program.
Bellman operators are monotone.
Every retained cut is globally valid for its approximate Bellman image.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L=\underline V_1(x_1)\le V_1(x_1)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Bellman-monotonicity certificate is mathematically coherent, but the cited dual-decomposition locator does not specifically establish the stated multistage propagation of globally valid SDDP cuts.

knowledge_statements.title: Statistical Policy Upper Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-sided Monte Carlo upper certificate for a fixed feasible policy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a feasible nonanticipative policy \(\pi\), and let independent simulated total costs satisfy \(Z_i^\pi\in[a,b]\) almost surely with \(J(\pi)=\mathbb E[Z_i^\pi]\). Define \(\widehat J_N(\pi)=N^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^N Z_i^\pi\). Then, for \(0<\delta<1\), \[U_N(\pi)=\widehat J_N(\pi)+(b-a)\sqrt{\frac{\log(1/\delta)}{2N}}\] satisfies \(\mathbb P(J(\pi)\le U_N(\pi))\ge1-\delta\). Since the optimal value obeys \(V^\star\le J(\pi)\), the same random quantity is a \((1-\delta)\)-confidence upper bound on \(V^\star\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent bounded simulations of a fixed feasible policy give a one-sided high-confidence upper bound on both its expected cost and the optimal value.
assumptions_latex: Policy \(\pi\) is feasible and fixed independently of the evaluation sample.
Evaluation trajectories are independent and identically distributed.
\(a\le Z_i^\pi\le b\) almost surely.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb P(V^\star\le J(\pi)\le U_N(\pi))\ge1-\delta\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The one-sided Hoeffding certificate is correct for a policy fixed independently of the evaluation sample, but no inspectable source is supplied. Adaptive policy selection would require separate validation.

children.title: Dual SDDP Certificates
children.top_down_role: Dual constructions used to certify multistage policy quality.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual SDDP Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Affine lower cuts obtained from feasible dual solutions of parametric linear recourse problems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x\in\mathbb R^d\), \(y\in\mathbb R^n\), \(W\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(T\in\mathbb R^{m\times d}\), \(h\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(c\in\mathbb R^n\). For the parametric linear program \[Q(x)=\min_{y\in\mathbb R_+^n}\{c^{\mathsf T}y:Wy=h-Tx\},\] let \(\bar\lambda\in\mathbb R^m\) be unrestricted in sign and satisfy \(W^{\mathsf T}\bar\lambda\le c\). For every state \(x\) at which the primal problem is feasible, weak duality gives \[Q(x)\ge\bar\lambda^{\mathsf T}(h-Tx)=\alpha+\beta^{\mathsf T}x,\] where \(\alpha=\bar\lambda^{\mathsf T}h\) and \(\beta=-T^{\mathsf T}\bar\lambda\). Thus dual feasibility certifies that the affine function is a globally valid lower cut on the primal-feasible state domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An unrestricted multiplier satisfying the dual inequalities for a parametric equality-constrained recourse problem certifies a globally valid affine lower cut on its feasible state domain.
assumptions_latex: \(W\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(T\in\mathbb R^{m\times d}\), \(h\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(c\in\mathbb R^n\).
The primal recourse problem is feasible at every state under consideration.
\(\bar\lambda\in\mathbb R^m\) is unrestricted in sign and satisfies \(W^{\mathsf T}\bar\lambda\le c\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q(x)\ge\bar\lambda^{\mathsf T}(h-Tx)=\alpha+\beta^{\mathsf T}x\) on the primal-feasible state domain.

notation.meaning: Unrestricted dual-feasible multiplier for the equality constraints

children.title: Exact-Bound Constructions
children.top_down_role: Constructions that produce exact deterministic bounds in eligible multistage regimes.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact-Bound Constructions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact optimality certification by coincidence of valid lower and feasible upper bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L\) be any deterministic lower bound on the optimal value \(V^\star\) of a minimization problem, and let \(\pi\) be a feasible policy whose expected cost \(J(\pi)\) is evaluated exactly as \(U\). If \(L=U\), then \[L\le V^\star\le J(\pi)=U=L,\] so \(V^\star=L=U\) and \(\pi\) is optimal. More generally, if \(U-L\le\varepsilon\), then \(J(\pi)-V^\star\le\varepsilon\). Exact evaluation may arise from complete enumeration of a finite scenario tree or another nonstatistical expectation calculation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Matching a valid deterministic lower bound with the exact cost of a feasible policy certifies both the optimal value and policy optimality.
assumptions_latex: The problem is a minimization problem.
\(L\le V^\star\) is valid.
Policy \(\pi\) is feasible and its expected cost \(U=J(\pi)\) is evaluated exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L=U\) implies \(V^\star=L=U\) and \(\pi\) is optimal.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The lower-bound/feasible-policy-cost sandwich is correct and the certificate kind fits, but neither the exact-certificate statement nor the finite-scenario-tree evaluation example has an inspectable source.

children.title: Dual-to-Exact Certificate Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Relationships between dual SDDP certificates and exact-bound constructions.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual-to-Exact Certificate Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: When a dual-generated linear-recourse cut becomes an exact supporting value-function bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x\in\mathbb R^d\), \(W\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(T\in\mathbb R^{m\times d}\), \(h\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), and define \[Q(x)=\min_{y\in\mathbb R_+^n}\{c^{\mathsf T}y:Wy=h-Tx\}.\] Its dual is \[\max_{\lambda\in\mathbb R^m}\{\lambda^{\mathsf T}(h-Tx):W^{\mathsf T}\lambda\le c\},\] where \(\lambda\) is unrestricted in sign. Let \(\bar x\) be a state at which the primal optimum is attained and strong duality holds. If \(\bar\lambda\) is dual optimal at \(\bar x\), then \(\ell(x)=\bar\lambda^{\mathsf T}(h-Tx)\) satisfies \(\ell(x)\le Q(x)\) at every primal-feasible state and \[\ell(\bar x)=Q(\bar x).\] Conversely, a cut generated by a dual-feasible multiplier is exact at \(\bar x\) if and only if its dual objective value there equals \(Q(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dual-feasible multiplier gives a valid affine lower cut, and that cut contacts the recourse value exactly at a state if and only if its dual value equals the attained primal value there.
assumptions_latex: \(W\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(T\in\mathbb R^{m\times d}\), \(h\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(c\in\mathbb R^n\).
The primal optimum at \(\bar x\) is attained.
Strong duality holds at \(\bar x\).
\(\bar\lambda\in\mathbb R^m\) satisfies \(W^{\mathsf T}\bar\lambda\le c\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\ell(x)\le Q(x)\) on the primal-feasible state domain, and \(\ell(\bar x)=Q(\bar x)\) exactly when \(\bar\lambda\) attains the primal value at \(\bar x\).

notation.meaning: State at which exact contact is tested

children.title: Stopping-Rule Reliability
children.top_down_role: Reliability characteristics of stopping rules under stochastic evaluation.

knowledge_statements.title: Stopping-Rule Reliability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Simultaneously valid bounds for reliable data-dependent SDDP termination.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iteration \(k\), let \(L_k\) be a deterministic lower bound and \(U_k\) a random upper bound. Suppose \[\mathbb P\!\left(\forall k\ge1:\ L_k\le V^\star\le U_k\right)\ge1-\alpha.\] For the stopping time \(\tau=\inf\{k:U_k-L_k\le\varepsilon\}\), simultaneous validity implies \[\mathbb P\!\left(\tau<\infty\ \Longrightarrow\ U_\tau-V^\star\le\varepsilon\right)\ge1-\alpha.\] Pointwise confidence intervals valid only for each fixed \(k\) do not by themselves establish this guarantee under repeated, data-dependent inspection; a confidence sequence or an error allocation with total failure probability at most \(\alpha\) is sufficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reliable adaptive stopping requires bounds valid simultaneously over inspected iterations; fixed-iteration confidence intervals alone do not control repeated-testing termination risk.
assumptions_latex: \(L_k\le V^\star\) deterministically for every inspected iteration.
Upper bounds are simultaneously valid with probability at least \(1-\alpha\).
Stopping occurs only when \(U_k-L_k\le\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb P(\tau<\infty\Rightarrow U_\tau-V^\star\le\varepsilon)\ge1-\alpha\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The simultaneous-validity implication and warning about repeatedly inspected pointwise intervals are mathematically sound, and the condition kind fits the reliability leaf. No source is supplied for the sequential-inference or SDDP stopping claims.

children.title: False-Termination Mechanisms
children.top_down_role: Mechanisms that cause termination before certificate requirements are satisfied.

assumptions_latex: At a candidate stopping iteration \(k\), \(L_k\) is a valid lower bound and \(U_k\) is a simulation-based estimate of the incumbent policy value \(V^{\pi_k}\).
The prescribed optimality tolerance is \(\varepsilon>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The stopping event need not certify \(V^{\pi_k}-V^\star\leq\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: optimal value of the multistage stochastic program
true expected value of the policy selected at iteration k
reported lower and upper estimates at iteration k

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Statistical false stopping in sampling-based SDDP certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A false termination occurs on the event \[F_k=\{U_k-L_k\leq\varepsilon\}\cap\{V^{\pi_k}-V^\star>\varepsilon\}.\] It can have positive probability when \(U_k\) underestimates \(V^{\pi_k}\), when \(L_k\) is not a valid lower bound, or when a fixed-sample confidence interval is repeatedly inspected without simultaneous-coverage correction. In particular, marginal coverage at each iteration does not by itself control \(\mathbb P(\bigcup_k F_k)\), because the stopping time and the reported policy depend on the same evolving information.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Termination can be false when an estimated gap is small although the selected policy remains suboptimal, especially under biased bounds, repeated testing, or adaptive policy selection.
knowledge_statements.title: False-Termination Mechanisms

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The false-stopping event is coherent, but the statement invokes an invalid lower bound despite assuming that L_k is valid. The claims about adaptive inspection and SDDP certificate behavior also require a specific source.

children.title: Termination-Risk Calibration
children.top_down_role: Calibration of the risk that a stopping decision is unsupported.

assumptions_latex: For each inspection \(k\), the bad-bound event \(B_k\) contains every outcome on which stopping at \(k\) could falsely certify the tolerance.
A risk budget \(\alpha\in(0,1)\) and nonnegative allocations \((\alpha_k)_{k\geq1}\) satisfy \(\sum_{k\geq1}\alpha_k\leq\alpha\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The calibrated rule satisfies \(\mathbb P(\text{false termination at some inspection})\leq\alpha\).

notation.meaning: bad certificate event at inspection k

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Anytime risk control by alpha spending over sequential inspections.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A stopping rule is termination-risk calibrated at level \(\alpha\) if each inspection is constructed so that \(\mathbb P(B_k)\leq\alpha_k\) and false termination at inspection \(k\) implies \(B_k\). Then, without requiring independence, \[\mathbb P\!\left(\text{false termination at some }k\right)\leq \mathbb P\!\left(\bigcup_{k\geq1}B_k\right)\leq\sum_{k\geq1}\alpha_k\leq\alpha.\] Equivalently, an anytime-valid confidence sequence may replace the allocated marginal bounds, provided its simultaneous failure probability is at most \(\alpha\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Allocate a total error budget across all stopping inspections, or use an anytime-valid confidence sequence, so the probability of ever stopping falsely is at most alpha.
knowledge_statements.title: Termination-Risk Calibration

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The union-bound calibration is mathematically sound and the condition kind fits the leaf, but no evidence is supplied for its use as an SDDP termination-risk calibration rule or for the confidence-sequence alternative.

children.title: Discrete-Nonconvex Decomposition Regimes
children.top_down_role: Extensions and failure boundaries arising when first-stage decisions, recourse functions, or scenario subproblems lose continuous convex structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Integer L-Shaped Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Binary finite-set form of the integer L-shaped method.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize a master problem with \(x\in X\) and \(\theta\geq L\). At an incumbent \(\bar x\), evaluate \(Q(\bar x)\) and add the integer optimality cut \[\theta\geq Q(\bar x)-\bigl(Q(\bar x)-L\bigr)\left(\sum_{i:\bar x_i=1}(1-x_i)+\sum_{i:\bar x_i=0}x_i\right).\] Reoptimize \(c^\top x+\theta\). Stop when the master lower bound equals the best evaluated value \(c^\top x+Q(x)\); otherwise evaluate a distinct new incumbent. The cut is exact at \(\bar x\). At any other binary point its right-hand side is at most \(L\), so it is redundant in the presence of \(\theta\geq L\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The integer L-shaped method alternates a binary master problem with recourse evaluations and incumbent-specific cuts. Each cut is exact at its evaluated incumbent and is redundant at other binary points under the global recourse lower bound.
assumptions_latex: The first-stage feasible set \(X\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\) is finite and has deterministic cost \(c^\top x\).
The recourse value \(Q(x)\) is finite on \(X\), and a valid global lower bound \(L\leq Q(x)\) is known.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Finite enumeration of distinct incumbents yields an optimizer of \(\min_{x\in X}\{c^\top x+Q(x)\}\).

source_refs.locator: 3.7 Integer First Stage p. 209; 3.7.3 Optimality Cuts p. 217

source_witnesses.locator: 3.7 Integer First Stage p. 209; 3.7.3 Optimality Cuts p. 217

assumptions_latex: A master relaxation contains \(x\in X\), a recourse variable \(\theta\), and a valid lower bound \(L\leq Q(x)\).
For an evaluated incumbent \(\bar x\), each candidate inequality is valid for every \((x,\theta)\) with \(x\in X\) and \(\theta\geq Q(x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Replacing a cut by a dominating valid cut cannot weaken the master lower bound.

notation.meaning: epigraph of the recourse function over the integer set

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dominance criterion for strengthened integer optimality cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A cut \(\theta\geq g_2(x)\) dominates \(\theta\geq g_1(x)\) on the master domain \(X\) when \(g_2(x)\geq g_1(x)\) for every \(x\in X\), with strict inequality for at least one \(x\in X\), while both inequalities are valid for \(E\). Adding the dominating cut produces a master feasible region contained in that produced by the dominated cut. Hence, in a minimization master problem, its optimal value is no smaller. Improved integer optimality-cut families seek such dominance while retaining exactness at selected evaluated incumbents.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An improved integer optimality cut is valid, remains exact where required, and dominates a weaker cut throughout the integer master domain, thereby raising the master lower bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Improved Integer Optimality-Cut Families

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The dominance property is correct, but it is a generic ordering criterion and does not identify or characterize any improved integer optimality-cut family. The cited section must be inspected or a more specific source supplied before the title-level claim is reliable.

children.title: Branch-Based Master Search
children.top_down_role: Master-level branching structures used within decomposed integer optimization.

knowledge_statements.title: Branch-Based Master Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Branch-and-cut search on a decomposed integer master problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain active master nodes \(v\) with regions \(X_v\). At a selected node, solve its current cut relaxation to obtain \(z_v^{\mathrm{LB}}\). Fathom the node if it is infeasible or if \(z_v^{\mathrm{LB}}\geq z^{\mathrm{UB}}\). Otherwise, evaluate recourse at an integer candidate; update \(z^{\mathrm{UB}}\) only when that candidate is feasible for the original problem, and add any violated valid recourse cuts. If no sufficient cut is found and the relaxation solution is fractional, branch into child regions whose integer-feasible union equals that of \(X_v\). If the procedure terminates with no active node and a feasible incumbent has been retained, that incumbent is globally optimal; if no feasible incumbent exists, exhaustion of all nodes certifies infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Search the integer master by branching, generating valid recourse cuts at nodes, updating the incumbent only with feasible solutions, and pruning nodes whose valid lower bounds cannot improve it. Exhausting the tree proves optimality when an incumbent exists and otherwise can prove infeasibility.
assumptions_latex: The master variables satisfy mixed-integer restrictions \(x\in X\), and every generated recourse cut is valid for the original epigraph.
Branching partitions each active node region into children whose union contains all integer-feasible points of that region.
Every fathoming decision uses a valid infeasibility certificate or a valid node lower bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If all nodes are exhausted or validly fathomed, a retained feasible incumbent is globally optimal; if none exists, the original problem is infeasible.

notation.meaning: master region associated with node v
valid lower bound at node v
objective value of the best known feasible solution

children.title: Cut-Based Relaxation Strengthening
children.top_down_role: Cut mechanisms that strengthen node relaxations during decomposed search.

assumptions_latex: At node \(v\), the current relaxation is \(R_v\supseteq E_v\), where \(E_v\) is the feasible recourse epigraph restricted to that node.
An inequality \(a^\top x+b\theta\geq d\) is valid for every point of \(E_v\) and violated by the current relaxation solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Adding the inequality preserves \(E_v\) and produces the tighter relaxation \(R_v'\subsetneq R_v\).

notation.meaning: true feasible epigraph at node v

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity and monotonic strengthening at one branch-and-cut node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \[R_v'=R_v\cap\{(x,	heta):a^\top x+b\theta\geq d\}.\] Validity gives \(E_v\subseteq R_v'\), while violation by the current relaxation solution gives \(R_v'\subsetneq R_v\). Consequently, minimizing the node objective over \(R_v'\) yields a lower bound at least as large as that obtained from \(R_v\). Global cuts may be inherited by every node; cuts valid only under the branching restrictions defining \(X_v\) must remain local to node \(v\) and its descendants for which those restrictions hold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A violated valid cut removes the current relaxation point without removing feasible node solutions, so the node lower bound can only improve; locally valid cuts require restricted inheritance.
knowledge_statements.title: Cut-Based Relaxation Strengthening

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The relaxation-strengthening argument is correct and the property kind fits, but the decomposition-specific distinction between global and locally inheritable cuts has no cited evidence.

children.title: Node-Level Decomposition Coordination
children.top_down_role: Coordination between search-tree nodes and decomposition subproblems.

assumptions_latex: Every node \(v\) has branching region \(X_v\), a valid cut pool, and a valid node lower bound.
Global cuts are valid on the root domain, whereas local cuts are valid only under explicitly recorded node restrictions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The coordinated procedure preserves valid bounds and may safely fathom any node satisfying \(z_v^{\mathrm{LB}}\geq z^{\mathrm{UB}}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordination rules for decomposition inside a branch-and-cut tree.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: When processing node \(v\), solve the master relaxation over \(X_v\), send each candidate first-stage vector to the scenario recourse subproblems, and return violated cuts with validity metadata. Insert root-valid cuts into the global pool; insert node-valid cuts only at \(v\) and compatible descendants. Reoptimize until no selected cut is violated, then update \(z_v^{\mathrm{LB}}\). Update \(z^{\mathrm{UB}}\) only from a fully recourse-feasible integer solution. Fathom \(v\) when it is infeasible or \(z_v^{\mathrm{LB}}\geq z^{\mathrm{UB}}\); otherwise branch and propagate all applicable cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each search node, solve scenario subproblems, manage global and local cuts by validity domain, update rigorous bounds, and then prune or branch.
knowledge_statements.title: Node-Level Decomposition Coordination

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed coordination protocol is plausible, but no source supports its cut-validity metadata, propagation rules, or claim that the resulting node bounds remain rigorous.

assumptions_latex: For each component \(j\), shortage and surplus penalties satisfy \(q_j^+,q_j^-\geq0\).
The tender vector is \(z=h-Tx\in\mathbb R^m\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The recourse value is the displayed separable step function of \(z\).

notation.meaning: tender or residual vector after the first-stage decision
nonnegative integer shortage and surplus variables

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separable simple integer recourse with unit technology columns.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Simple integer recourse assigns to each \(z\in\mathbb R^m\) the value \[Q(z)=\min_{y^+,y^-\in\mathbb Z_+^m}\left\{(q^+)^\top y^++(q^-)^\top y^-:y^+\geq z,\ y^-\geq-z\right\}.\] Because the constraints and objective separate by component, an optimal choice is \(y_j^+=\lceil(z_j)_+\rceil\) and \(y_j^-=\lceil(-z_j)_+\rceil\). Hence \[Q(z)=\sum_{j=1}^m\left[q_j^+\lceil(z_j)_+\rceil+q_j^-\lceil(-z_j)_+\rceil\right].\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Simple integer recourse covers each tender component with nonnegative integer shortage and surplus units, producing a separable ceiling-valued recourse function.
knowledge_statements.title: Simple Integer Recourse

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed inequality model does yield the stated separable ceiling function, but the cited locator is labeled simple recourse and has not been shown to support this particular integer, inequality-based formulation. A source specific to simple integer recourse is required.

assumptions_latex: The second-stage value depends on the first-stage decision only through the tender vector \(z=h-Tx\).
A finite set of scenario recourse functions \(Q_s(z)\) and probabilities \(p_s\) is given.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: First-stage comparisons and recourse cuts may be organized in the lower-dimensional image \(Z=\{h-Tx:x\in X\}\).

notation.meaning: expected recourse as a function of tender

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tender-vector representation for integer recourse decomposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If two first-stage decisions \(x,x'\in X\) satisfy \(h-Tx=h-Tx'=z\), then their second-stage feasible sets and recourse values coincide whenever all first-stage dependence enters through the right-hand side. Thus \[Q_s(x)=Q_s(h-Tx)=Q_s(z),\qquad \mathcal Q(x)=\mathcal Q(z)=\sum_s p_sQ_s(z).\] A tender-space method therefore maps master candidates into \(Z\), evaluates or partitions \(\mathcal Q\) there, and transfers valid information back through the affine relation \(z=h-Tx\). This can identify multiple first-stage decisions with one recourse state.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Tender-space methods represent recourse through the residual vector h minus Tx, allowing decisions with the same residual to share evaluations, partitions, and cuts.
knowledge_statements.title: Tender-Space Methods

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation is correct under the stated dependence assumption, but no source supports its identification as a tender-space decomposition method or the claims about transferring partitions and cuts.

assumptions_latex: For a fixed scenario, the integer recourse epigraph over a bounded master region is representable as a finite union \(E=\bigcup_{r=1}^R P_r\) of polyhedra.
A linear inequality is valid for the convex hull \(\operatorname{conv}(E)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The inequality is a valid recourse cut and can separate relaxation points outside \(\operatorname{conv}(E)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex-hull certificate for a finite disjunction of recourse regimes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The inequality \(a^\top x+b\theta\geq d\) is a disjunctive recourse cut when it is valid on every term \(P_r\), equivalently when \[\inf_{(x,\theta)\in P_r}(a^\top x+b\theta)\geq d\qquad(r=1,\ldots,R).\] These finitely checkable inequalities certify validity on \(E\), and linearity then certifies validity on \(\operatorname{conv}(E)\). If a relaxation point \((\hat x,\hat\theta)\) satisfies \(a^\top\hat x+b\hat\theta<d\), the cut separates that point while retaining every feasible recourse epigraph point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A disjunctive recourse cut is certified by validity on every polyhedral recourse regime; it then remains valid for their convex hull and can remove an invalid relaxation point.
knowledge_statements.title: Disjunctive Recourse Cuts

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Validity on every disjunct correctly certifies validity on their union and convex hull, and certificate is an appropriate kind. A source is still required for the finite-polyhedral representation of the integer recourse epigraph and its use as a recourse cut.

assumptions_latex: At a master candidate \(\bar x\), a scenario subproblem is a mixed-integer program with a fractional relaxation solution.
Every second-stage branching disjunction used is exhaustive for the integer-feasible recourse set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The resulting disjunctive inequality is valid for all integer recourse solutions and may strengthen the first-stage master relaxation.

notation.meaning: a fractional second-stage variable selected for branching
floor of the fractional relaxation value

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cuts derived from exhaustive branching in an integer recourse subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Solve the scenario subproblem relaxation at \(\bar x\). If an integer-constrained component has value \(\hat y_j\notin\mathbb Z\), set \(k=\lfloor\hat y_j\rfloor\) and branch on \[y_j\leq k\quad\text{or}\quad y_j\geq k+1.\] Compute valid lower descriptions for both child recourse epigraphs, form a valid inequality for the convex hull of their union, and project that inequality into the master variables \((x,\theta)\). Add the projected cut when violated. Repeat until the subproblem is certified integer-feasible or its branching tree proves infeasibility or the required recourse bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Branch on a fractional second-stage integer variable, combine the child epigraphs through a disjunctive hull, project a violated valid inequality, and add it to the master.
knowledge_statements.title: Second-Stage Branching Cuts

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The branching disjunction is exhaustive, but the construction and projection of a master-space inequality are left unspecified. Without a source or explicit projection conditions, validity of the resulting master cut cannot be assessed.

assumptions_latex: Consider scalar simple integer recourse with unit shortage cost and no surplus demand: \(Q(z)=\min\{y:y\in\mathbb Z_+,\ y\geq z\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The recourse function is discontinuous at every nonnegative integer and has no supporting affine minorant that is exact immediately on both sides of a jump.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar example exposing jump geometry in integer recourse.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The value function is \[Q(z)=\lceil(z)_+\rceil.\] For every integer \(k\geq0\), \(Q(k)=k\), whereas \(Q(k+\delta)=k+1\) for all \(0<\delta<1\). Hence \(Q\) has a right jump of size one at \(k\) and is not convex: for example, \(Q(1/2)=1>\tfrac12Q(0)+\tfrac12Q(1)=1/2\). Therefore the continuous-recourse geometry underlying globally exact supporting-hyperplane cuts fails; decomposition must instead use disjunctive, integer, or tender-cell information.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Even one-dimensional integer recourse is a step function with jumps and nonconvexity, so continuous-recourse supporting-hyperplane logic cannot exactly describe it.
knowledge_statements.title: Discontinuous Recourse Geometry

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The scalar ceiling example correctly demonstrates jumps and nonconvexity, but the cited simple-recourse section has not been shown to cover integer recourse. The conclusion's additional assertion about affine minorants is also not stated precisely or established in the record.

knowledge_statements.title: Integer Value-Function Approximations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lower approximations of finite-state integer recourse value functions used in SDDiP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a stage state set \(X_t\subseteq\mathbb Z^{n_t}\) and cost-to-go function \(V_t:X_t\to\mathbb R\), an integer value-function approximation after iteration \(k\) is \[\underline V_t^k(x)=\max_{j\in J_t^k}\{\alpha_{tj}+\beta_{tj}^{\mathsf T}x\},\qquad x\in X_t,\] where every retained cut satisfies \(\alpha_{tj}+\beta_{tj}^{\mathsf T}x\le V_t(x)\) for all \(x\in X_t\). Consequently, \(\underline V_t^k\le V_t\) on \(X_t\); adding a valid cut makes the sequence pointwise nondecreasing.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The approximation is the maximum of finitely many affine lower bounds valid on the integer state set, and it increases whenever another valid cut is added.
assumptions_latex: \(X_t\) is a nonempty integer state set.
\(V_t(x)\) is finite for every \(x\in X_t\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\underline V_t^k(x)\le V_t(x)\) for all \(x\in X_t\), with monotonicity under cut addition.

notation.meaning: feasible integer states at stage t

children.title: Lagrangian SDDiP Cuts
children.top_down_role: SDDiP certificates derived from Lagrangian relaxation structures.

knowledge_statements.title: Lagrangian SDDiP Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lagrangian lower cuts obtained by dualizing a stage state-linking equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X_t\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), \(Y_t\subseteq\mathbb R^m\), \(A_t\in\mathbb R^{r\times m}\), \(B_t\in\mathbb R^{r\times n}\), and \(f_t:Y_t\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\). For every feasible state \(x\in X_t\), define \(V_t(x)=\inf\{f_t(y):y\in Y_t,\ A_ty=B_tx\}\). For any \(\pi\in\mathbb R^r\) with finite \(L_t(\pi)=\inf_{y\in Y_t}\{f_t(y)+\pi^{\mathsf T}A_ty\}\), the affine function \[\ell_{t,\pi}(x)=L_t(\pi)-\pi^{\mathsf T}B_tx\] satisfies \(\ell_{t,\pi}(x)\le V_t(x)\) for every feasible \(x\in X_t\). At a trial state \(\bar x\in X_t\), any attained maximizer of \(L_t(\pi)-\pi^{\mathsf T}B_t\bar x\) gives the largest cut value at \(\bar x\) within this multiplier family; if the supremum is not attained, maximizing sequences only approach that value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dualizing the state-linking equation produces an affine global lower bound. If the multiplier problem attains its maximum, a maximizing multiplier gives the best cut value at the trial state within this family; otherwise that value can only be approached.
assumptions_latex: \(X_t\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) and \(Y_t\subseteq\mathbb R^m\), with compatible linear maps \(A_t\) and \(B_t\).
\(V_t(x)\) is finite on the feasible state domain.
The selected multiplier \(\pi\in\mathbb R^r\) has finite \(L_t(\pi)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_t(\pi)-\pi^{\mathsf T}B_tx\le V_t(x)\) for every feasible \(x\in X_t\).

notation.meaning: state domain and stage decision domain
linear maps defining the state-linking equation

children.title: Strengthened SDDiP Cuts
children.top_down_role: SDDiP cut families enhanced beyond their baseline certificate form.

knowledge_statements.title: Strengthened SDDiP Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise strengthening of a valid SDDiP lower cut on the admissible integer state set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X_t\) be the admissible state set and let \(\ell(x)=\alpha+\beta^{\mathsf T}x\) be a valid lower cut for \(V_t\). A cut \(\ell^+(x)=\alpha^++(\beta^+)^{\mathsf T}x\) is a strengthening of \(\ell\) on \(X_t\) when \[\ell(x)\le\ell^+(x)\le V_t(x)\qquad\text{for every }x\in X_t.\] Replacing \(\ell\) by \(\ell^+\) in a maximum-of-cuts approximation preserves its lower-bound validity and cannot decrease that approximation anywhere on \(X_t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A strengthened cut remains a valid lower bound and dominates the original cut at every admissible state, so replacing the original can only improve the approximation.
assumptions_latex: \(\ell\) and \(\ell^+\) are finite affine functions on \(X_t\).
The approximation is formed as the pointwise maximum of retained cuts.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Replacing \(\ell\) by \(\ell^+\) preserves validity and pointwise improves or retains the lower approximation on \(X_t\).
review_flags: no supplied locator directly supports SDDiP cut strengthening

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The pointwise strengthening property is mathematically coherent and the content kind fits, but no evidence item or explicit standard-field rationale is supplied for this SDDiP-specific record.

children.title: SDDiP Cut Dominance Regimes
children.top_down_role: Regimes governing relative strength among Lagrangian and strengthened cut families.

knowledge_statements.title: SDDiP Cut Dominance Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise dominance and redundancy criteria for two SDDiP cuts on a declared state domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X_t\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty and let \(\ell_i(x)=\alpha_i+\beta_i^{\mathsf T}x\) for \(i\in\{1,2\}\). Cut \(\ell_1\) weakly dominates \(\ell_2\) on \(X_t\) if and only if \[\inf_{x\in X_t}\bigl[(\alpha_1-\alpha_2)+(\beta_1-\beta_2)^{\mathsf T}x\bigr]\ge0.\] It strictly dominates everywhere when the displayed infimum is positive; it dominates with strict improvement somewhere when it weakly dominates and \(\ell_1(x)>\ell_2(x)\) for at least one \(x\in X_t\). In a maximum-of-cuts approximation that retains \(\ell_1\), deleting \(\ell_2\) does not change the approximation on \(X_t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The first cut weakly dominates the second exactly when their infimum difference over the state set is nonnegative. If the dominating cut remains retained, the dominated cut is redundant in a maximum-of-cuts approximation.
assumptions_latex: \(X_t\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty.
\(\ell_1\) and \(\ell_2\) are finite affine functions and valid lower cuts for the same value function on \(X_t\).
The maximum-of-cuts family retains \(\ell_1\) when \(\ell_2\) is deleted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(\ell_1(x)\ge\ell_2(x)\) for every \(x\in X_t\) and \(\ell_1\) remains retained, deleting \(\ell_2\) leaves the maximum-of-cuts approximation unchanged on \(X_t\).

notation.meaning: state domain on which dominance is tested
intercept and slope of cut i

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: pointwise dominance and redundancy follow directly from maximum-of-functions algebra
