knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Convergence SDDiP Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-state, exact-solve SDDiP regime with exhaustive positive-probability sampling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a finite-horizon, stagewise-independent multistage stochastic integer program with finite feasible state and outcome sets at every stage. Suppose every forward and backward subproblem is solved globally, each generated cut is a valid lower bound and is exact at the sampled state, cuts are retained, and every reachable state-outcome pair is visited with positive probability independently across iterations. Then, with probability one, after finitely many iterations the lower approximation equals the exact cost-to-go function at every reachable state. Thereafter the policy induced by the approximations is optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With finite reachable states, exact subproblem solves, exact valid cuts, cut retention, and recurrent sampling, SDDiP identifies every reachable value and an optimal policy in finite time almost surely.
assumptions_latex: The horizon, feasible state sets, and outcome supports are finite.
All subproblems are solved globally and generated cuts are valid and exact at sampled states.
Every reachable state-outcome pair has positive independent revisit probability.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: With probability one, there exists finite \(K\) such that \(\underline V_t^k(x)=V_t(x)\) for every reachable \(x\), every stage \(t\), and all \(k\ge K\).
review_flags: exact finite-convergence theorem and sampling hypotheses require an SDDiP source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: This is a substantive almost-sure finite-convergence theorem. Its recurrent-sampling, exact-cut, and policy-optimality conclusions require a dedicated SDDiP theorem citation and cannot be validated from standard-field rationale alone.

children.title: Heuristic SDDiP Regimes
children.top_down_role: SDDiP variants relying on heuristic decisions or uncertified computational choices.

knowledge_statements.title: Heuristic SDDiP Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: SDDiP variant allowing uncertified subproblem solutions or cuts, with incumbent reporting only.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given initial approximations \(\underline V_t^0\), iteration \(k\) samples a scenario path, computes forward decisions using any prescribed primal heuristic, and obtains backward candidate functions \(h_t^k\) from approximate or heuristic subproblem information. Update \[\underline V_t^k(x)=\max\{\underline V_t^{k-1}(x),h_t^k(x)\}\] only when a separate validity test certifies \(h_t^k(x)\le V_t(x)\) on the declared state domain; otherwise retain \(h_t^k\) solely for search guidance. Stop by a user-specified budget or empirical stability rule and output the best policy found, without an optimality claim.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Heuristic SDDiP may use uncertified solves for search, but only independently validated cuts enter the lower model; termination reports an incumbent rather than certified optimality.
assumptions_latex: A forward primal heuristic and a finite stopping budget or stability rule are specified.
A separate test distinguishes globally valid lower cuts from search-only functions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is an incumbent policy; a rigorous lower bound exists only from cuts that pass the stated validity test.

notation.meaning: candidate backward function at iteration k

review_flags: locator is indirect and does not establish this SDDiP algorithm

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed safeguards are sensible, but the cited policy-approximation section does not establish this SDDiP algorithm or its distinction between certified cuts and search-only functions.

children.title: Approximate SDDiP Regimes
children.top_down_role: SDDiP variants using controlled approximations in value functions or subproblems.

knowledge_statements.title: Approximate SDDiP Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inexact SDDiP with explicit subproblem tolerances and certified approximate lower cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iteration \(k\), sample a forward path and solve each backward subproblem to a declared tolerance \(\varepsilon_{t,k}\ge0\). From a certified dual or global lower bound construct \(\ell_t^k\) satisfying \(\ell_t^k(x)\le V_t(x)\) on the state domain and \(V_t(x_t^k)-\ell_t^k(x_t^k)\le\varepsilon_{t,k}\) at the sampled state. Set \[\underline V_t^k=\max\{\underline V_t^{k-1},\ell_t^k\}.\] Stop when a prescribed statistical or deterministic gap test, including accumulated approximation errors, is met; otherwise output the current policy and reported tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Approximate SDDiP uses tolerance-controlled subproblem solves and globally valid cuts whose sampled-state error is bounded, while stopping tests must account for accumulated errors.
assumptions_latex: Each backward solve supplies a certified global lower bound.
The sampled-state cut error is bounded by the declared \(\varepsilon_{t,k}\).
The stopping test explicitly incorporates approximation errors.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every \(\underline V_t^k\) remains a lower bound, while its certification accuracy depends on the tolerance schedule and stopping analysis.
review_flags: locator is indirect and does not establish SDDiP error propagation
tolerance-based convergence conditions require a dedicated source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A dedicated inexact-SDDiP source is needed to support the sampled-state error condition, accumulated-error treatment, and valid stopping criteria. The generic approximate-value-iteration citation is insufficient.

children.title: SDDiP Certificate Limitations
children.top_down_role: Boundaries on certificate interpretation under heuristic or approximate computation.

knowledge_statements.title: SDDiP Certificate Limitations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between computational progress indicators and rigorous SDDiP optimality certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U\) be the expected cost of a feasible policy estimate and let \(L\) be the value produced by backward approximations. The reported gap \(U-L\) is an optimality certificate only if \(L\le V^*\le U\) holds with the declared deterministic or statistical confidence. If any retained cut can exceed the true cost-to-go, a backward subproblem is only locally solved without a global bound, or sampling error in \(U\) is ignored, then this bracketing implication is unavailable. Empirical stabilization of decisions or objective estimates alone does not certify global optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An SDDiP gap certifies optimality only when its lower and upper endpoints are valid bounds; local solves, invalid cuts, or ignored sampling error destroy that certificate.
assumptions_latex: The problem is a minimization problem with optimum \(V^*\).
The quantities \(L\) and \(U\) are the reported lower and upper estimates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Without certified bracketing \(L\le V^*\le U\), the numerical difference \(U-L\) is not a global optimality certificate.

notation.meaning: reported feasible-policy estimate or upper bound

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: a certified gap requires valid bracketing bounds

knowledge_statements.title: Loss of Globally Supporting Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete nonconvex value function admitting no globally valid affine lower support at a selected state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=[-1,1]\), define \(V:X\to\mathbb R\) by \(V(x)=-x^2\), and take \(\bar x=0\). There is no affine function \(\ell:X\to\mathbb R\) of the form \(\ell(x)=a+bx\) such that \[\ell(x)\le V(x)\quad\text{for every }x\in X,\qquad \ell(\bar x)=V(\bar x).\] Hence a nonconvex value function need not admit a globally valid affine lower support that is exact at a prescribed trial state.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On the interval from minus one to one, the function minus x squared has no affine global lower bound touching it at zero. Thus exact globally supporting affine cuts can fail for a nonconvex value function.
assumptions_latex: The candidate support is affine and must be valid on all of \(X\).
Exactness is required at \(\bar x=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There is no affine \(\ell\) satisfying \(\ell(x)\le V(x)\) for every \(x\in[-1,1]\) and \(\ell(0)=V(0)\).

notation.meaning: trial state at which exactness is required

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the explicit counterexample is algebraically self-contained
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

knowledge_statements.title: Local Subproblem Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: KKT certificate of first-order stationarity for a smooth constrained nonconvex subproblem and its global-certification boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f,g_1,\ldots,g_m,h_1,\ldots,h_p\) be continuously differentiable near a feasible point \(z^*\in\mathbb R^n\) of \(\min_{z\in\mathbb R^n} f(z)\) subject to \(g_i(z)\le0\) for \(i=1,\ldots,m\) and \(h_j(z)=0\) for \(j=1,\ldots,p\). Multipliers \(\lambda^*\in\mathbb R_+^m\) and \(
u^*\in\mathbb R^p\) provide a KKT first-order stationarity certificate when \[
abla f(z^*)+\sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_i^*
abla g_i(z^*)+\sum_{j=1}^p
u_j^*
abla h_j(z^*)=0,\qquad \lambda_i^*g_i(z^*)=0\quad(i=1,\ldots,m).\] Under a specified constraint qualification, every local minimizer satisfies these conditions. For a nonconvex problem, satisfaction of the conditions alone establishes neither local minimality nor global optimality and does not by itself yield a globally valid decomposition cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Feasibility and KKT multipliers certify first-order stationarity. Under a constraint qualification these conditions are necessary at a local minimizer, but in a nonconvex problem they do not by themselves prove local or global optimality or validate a global decomposition cut.
assumptions_latex: \(f,g_i,h_j\) are continuously differentiable near \(z^*\in\mathbb R^n\).
\(z^*\) is feasible.
A specified constraint qualification is assumed only for the necessity statement at a local minimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed KKT conditions certify first-order stationarity but, without additional sufficient conditions or a global bound, do not certify local or global optimality.

notation.meaning: numbers of inequality and equality constraints

review_flags: specific KKT theorem or section locator required

knowledge_statements.title: Nonconvex Duality Gaps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lagrangian primal-dual relation and positive-gap boundary for nonconvex subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the minimization problem \(p^*=\inf\{f(z):g(z)\le0,\ h(z)=0\}\), define \[q(\lambda,
u)=\inf_z\{f(z)+\lambda^{\mathsf T}g(z)+
u^{\mathsf T}h(z)\},\qquad d^*=\sup_{\lambda\ge0,
u}q(\lambda,
u).\] Weak duality always yields \(d^*\le p^*\). The duality gap is \(p^*-d^*\ge0\); in a nonconvex problem it may be strictly positive. Consequently, a dual solution certifies the lower bound \(d^*\), but it need not recover the primal value or produce a cut exact at the evaluated state.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lagrangian weak duality still gives a lower bound in nonconvex problems, but a positive primal-dual gap can prevent exact value recovery and exact decomposition cuts.
assumptions_latex: The primal feasible set is nonempty and \(p^*\) is finite.
The Lagrangian dual function is not identically negative infinity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d^*\le p^*\), with possible strict inequality when the primal problem is nonconvex.

children.title: Global-Optimization Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Interfaces connecting nonconvex decomposition with global-optimization frameworks.

knowledge_statements.title: Global-Optimization Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certified interface between stagewise decomposition and global nonconvex subproblem solvers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a queried state \(x^k\), pass the complete stage subproblem and state-linking data to a global solver. Require the solver to return a feasible incumbent with value \(U^k\), a rigorous lower bound \(L^k\), and either a globally valid state-dependent underestimator \(\ell^k(x)\le V(x)\) or the information needed to verify it. Insert \(\ell^k\) into the master approximation only after domain and validity checks. Terminate the subproblem when \(U^k-L^k\le\varepsilon_k\); otherwise continue spatial branching. The interface transfers certified bounds, not merely locally optimal primal points.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A global-solver interface exchanges complete subproblems, incumbents, rigorous lower bounds, and verifiable global underestimators; only validated underestimators become decomposition cuts.
assumptions_latex: The global solver supplies rigorous bounds over the declared subproblem domain.
The decomposition layer can verify the domain and validity of transferred underestimators.
A nonnegative tolerance \(\varepsilon_k\) is prescribed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Accepted cuts are globally valid, and \(U^k-L^k\le\varepsilon_k\) certifies an \(\varepsilon_k\)-global subproblem solution.
review_flags: no supplied locator directly supports the decomposition-to-global-solver interface
solver certificate conventions require source confirmation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm describes a plausible certified interface, but no source supports its required solver outputs, underestimator-transfer protocol, or interpretation of the global optimality gap.

children.title: Spatial-Decomposition Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Interfaces connecting decomposition with spatial partitioning frameworks.

knowledge_statements.title: Spatial-Decomposition Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interface between scenario decomposition and spatial lower relaxations for nonconvex recourse.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For scenario probabilities \(p_s>0\), first-stage domain \(X\), and recourse functions \(Q_s:X\to\mathbb R\), suppose spatial node \(r\) has region \(X_r\subseteq X\) and valid estimators \(L_{sr}(x)\le Q_s(x)\) for every \(x\in X_r\). The relaxation
\[\min_{x\in X_r,\theta}\;c^\top x+\sum_s p_s\theta_s\quad\text{subject to}\quad \theta_s\ge L_{sr}(x)\ \text{for all }s\]
is a valid lower-bounding master for the original problem restricted to \(X_r\). Branching may refine \(X_r\), while scenario subproblems generate new region-valid estimators.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A spatial node supplies a region, and scenario subproblems supply recourse underestimators valid there; their master objective is a valid regional lower bound.
assumptions_latex: \(L_{sr}(x)\le Q_s(x)\) for all \(x\in X_r\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{val}(\mathrm{master}_r)\le \min_{x\in X_r}\{c^\top x+\sum_s p_sQ_s(x)\}\).

notation.meaning: first-stage region of spatial node r
regional lower estimator of scenario-s recourse

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: pointwise scenario underestimators produce a valid regional lower-bounding master

children.title: Cross-Framework Certificate Transfer
children.top_down_role: Transfer of bounds and local certificates across decomposition frameworks.

knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Framework Certificate Transfer
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transfer of lower and upper certificates between decomposition and spatial global optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F(x)=c^\top x+\sum_s p_sQ_s(x)\) on \(X\), let \(U=F(\bar x)\) for a globally feasible incumbent \(\bar x\), and let \(\mathcal R\) be the set of open spatial nodes. Suppose each node \(r\in\mathcal R\) has a certified lower bound \(L_r\) obtained from estimators valid throughout its region. Suppose also that every nonopen region is certified infeasible or has a valid lower bound at least \(U\). Define \[L=\min\left\{U,\inf_{r\in\mathcal R}L_r\right\},\] with \(\inf\varnothing=+\infty\). Then \(L\le\inf_{x\in X}F(x)\le U\). Consequently, \(U-L\le\varepsilon\) is a transferable absolute \(\varepsilon\)-global-optimality certificate. Every transferred estimator must retain its certified region of validity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Valid regional lower bounds, valid fathoming certificates, and a feasible incumbent combine into global lower and upper certificates; their gap certifies global accuracy.
assumptions_latex: \(\bar x\in X\) and its scenario recourse decisions are globally feasible.
Every open-node estimator is valid throughout its receiving spatial region.
Every nonopen region is certified infeasible or has a valid lower bound at least \(U\).
The open and nonopen spatial regions cover \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L\le\inf_{x\in X}F(x)\le U\), and \(U-L\le\varepsilon\) implies \(F(\bar x)-\inf_{x\in X}F(x)\le\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: certified lower bound for open spatial node r
global lower certificate combining the incumbent value and open-node bounds
objective value of the globally feasible incumbent

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: valid spatial-node bounds, valid fathoming, and a feasible incumbent yield a global optimality-gap certificate

children.title: Interface Compatibility Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Structural incompatibilities that limit cross-framework integration.

knowledge_statements.title: Interface Compatibility Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Regional validity is the boundary governing transfer of nonconvex spatial cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A cut valid only on a spatial region \(R\) cannot be inserted unconditionally into a master whose domain contains points outside \(R\). Concretely, let \(Q(x)=-x^2\) on \([-1,1]\). The affine function \(\ell(x)=\tfrac12-\tfrac32x\) satisfies \(\ell(x)\le Q(x)\) on \(R=[\tfrac12,1]\), but \(\ell(-1)=2>Q(-1)=-1\). Hence transferring \(\theta\ge\ell(x)\) to the global master can remove feasible epigraph points. Compatibility requires restricting the receiving node to \(R\) or encoding the cut conditionally.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A region-valid nonconvex cut may be invalid elsewhere, so global transfer is safe only when its region is enforced or encoded conditionally.
assumptions_latex: The receiving master contains a point outside the cut's certified validity region.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Regional validity alone does not imply global validity, so unconditional transfer may invalidate the relaxation.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the displayed polynomial example directly establishes the regional-transfer failure
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The polynomial counterexample is correct and the failure-boundary kind fits, but the framework-level transfer rule lacks an inspectable source.

children.title: Cut Selection Policies
children.top_down_role: Policies governing which candidate cuts enter or remain in a cut pool.

knowledge_statements.title: Cut Selection Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Budgeted selection of valid cuts for the next decomposition master solve.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a valid cut pool \(P_k\), reference point \(z^k\), scores \(\sigma_j^k\), and budget \(B\), initialize \(S_k\) with mandatory cuts, including cuts active at the incumbent when required for certification. Add cuts from \(P_k\setminus S_k\) in nonincreasing score order until \(|S_k|=B\) or no positive-score cut remains. Solve the master using \(S_k\), retain all omitted cuts in \(P_k\), and stop only under the decomposition method's independent feasibility and optimality tests. A typical score is normalized violation \(\sigma_j^k=(a_j^\top z^k-b_j)_+/(1+\lVert a_j\rVert)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Select mandatory cuts first, then fill a budget using ranked violations; omitted valid cuts remain available, and stopping uses separate correctness tests.
assumptions_latex: Every pool member represents a valid master inequality.
The budget \(B\) is at least the number of mandatory cuts.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The selected master remains a relaxation, while selection changes strength and cost rather than cut validity.

notation.meaning: cuts selected for the next master

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: budgeted violation-ranked cut selection is a standard cut-pool control rule
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits the leaf, but the particular mandatory-cut, ranking, budgeting, and termination policy is not supported by a cited source.

children.title: Cut Activity Screening
children.top_down_role: Activity-based screening criteria for identifying influential cuts.

knowledge_statements.title: Cut Activity Screening
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tolerance-based test for active, violated, inactive, and undecided master cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Write cut \(j\) as \(a_j^\top z\le b_j\), and define its signed slack at \(z^k\) by \(s_j^k=b_j-a_j^\top z^k\). Choose tolerances satisfying \(0\le\tau_{\mathrm{act}}\le\tau_{\mathrm{viol}}\). Classify the cut as active when \(|s_j^k|\le\tau_{\mathrm{act}}\), violated when \(s_j^k<-\tau_{\mathrm{viol}}\), inactive when \(s_j^k>\tau_{\mathrm{act}}\), and undecided when \(-\tau_{\mathrm{viol}}\le s_j^k<-\tau_{\mathrm{act}}\). Screening may prioritize or temporarily omit cuts, but inactivity at one point does not certify redundancy over the master domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Ordered slack tolerances classify a cut without overlap as active, violated, inactive, or undecided; pointwise inactivity does not establish global redundancy.
assumptions_latex: Cut \(j\) has the form \(a_j^\top z\le b_j\).
\(z^k\) lies in the domain on which the cut is defined.
\(0\le\tau_{\mathrm{act}}\le\tau_{\mathrm{viol}}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The four cases classify every signed slack \(s_j^k\) without overlap, and the classification is pointwise rather than a redundancy certificate.

notation.meaning: signed slack of cut j at the reference point
violation tolerance, no smaller than the activity tolerance

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: ordered signed-slack tolerances give a nonoverlapping pointwise screening classification

children.title: Selection-Screening Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Interactions between selective retention, screening cost, and relaxation quality.

knowledge_statements.title: Selection-Screening Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotonic relaxation strength versus nonmonotonic computational cost under cut screening.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S_1\subseteq S_2\) be two collections of valid cuts added to the same minimization master, and let \(v(S)\) denote its optimal value. Then \(v(S_1)\le v(S_2)\le v^*\), where \(v^*\) is the target problem value. Thus retaining more valid cuts cannot weaken the lower bound. No corresponding monotonicity holds for solution time: a larger set can improve iteration count through stronger bounds but increases master size, whereas aggressive screening reduces each solve yet may require more regeneration and iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: More valid cuts monotonically strengthen a minimization lower bound, but runtime need not improve because master size and iteration count move in opposing directions.
assumptions_latex: Both masters have the same objective and base constraints.
Every cut in \(S_2\) is valid for the target minimization problem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S_1\subseteq S_2\) implies \(v(S_1)\le v(S_2)\le v^*\), but implies no ordering of computational times.

notation.meaning: optimal value of the master using cut set S

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: feasible-set inclusion proves bound monotonicity, while algorithmic runtime has no set-inclusion ordering
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The feasible-set monotonicity statement is correct and the runtime caveat fits the tradeoff leaf, but no inspectable citation is supplied.

children.title: Cut Aggregation
children.top_down_role: Combined cut representations that reduce pool size or master complexity.

knowledge_statements.title: Cut Aggregation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Probability-weighted aggregation of scenario-wise recourse cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose scenario variables satisfy \(\theta_s\ge\alpha_s+\beta_s^\top x\) and \(p_s\ge0\). With aggregate variable \(\theta=\sum_s p_s\theta_s\), summing the inequalities yields the valid aggregate cut
\[\theta\ge\sum_s p_s\alpha_s+\left(\sum_s p_s\beta_s\right)^\top x.\]
More generally, any nonnegative conic combination of valid inequalities is valid. Aggregation reduces the number of master rows, but the single aggregate inequality generally does not recover every scenario-wise restriction and can therefore define a weaker relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Probability-weighted scenario cuts combine into one valid aggregate cut, reducing rows but generally losing the strength of separate scenario restrictions.
assumptions_latex: \(\theta_s\ge\alpha_s+\beta_s^\top x\) is valid for every scenario \(s\).
\(p_s\ge0\) for every \(s\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\theta=\sum_s p_s\theta_s\) satisfies \(\theta\ge\sum_s p_s\alpha_s+(\sum_s p_s\beta_s)^\top x\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: nonnegative weighted summation preserves validity of linear inequalities
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

children.title: Cut Disaggregation
children.top_down_role: Separated cut representations that preserve scenario or component detail.

knowledge_statements.title: Cut Disaggregation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scenario-wise lifting of recourse approximations into separate master inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For separable expected recourse \(Q(x)=\sum_s p_sQ_s(x)\), introduce one variable \(\theta_s\) per scenario and impose every available valid estimator \(\theta_s\ge\ell_{sj}(x)\). The master represents aggregate recourse by \(\theta=\sum_s p_s\theta_s\). This disaggregated system implies each corresponding weighted aggregate cut. Conversely, an aggregate inequality for \(\theta\) alone does not determine valid scenario components and cannot generally be disaggregated without scenario-wise estimators or additional structural information.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Disaggregation gives each scenario its own recourse variable and cuts; it implies weighted aggregate cuts, while aggregate cuts alone generally cannot be reversed.
assumptions_latex: \(Q(x)=\sum_s p_sQ_s(x)\) with \(p_s\ge0\).
Each \(\ell_{sj}(x)\le Q_s(x)\) on the master domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The scenario-wise system implies its nonnegative weighted aggregates, but the converse implication generally fails.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: an extended scenario-wise formulation projects to weighted aggregate inequalities but is not reconstructible from them alone

children.title: Cut Granularity Regimes
children.top_down_role: Problem regimes favoring coarse or fine cut representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Cut Granularity Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Partition-based continuum from single-cut to scenario-wise multicut formulations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal S\) be a finite scenario set and \(\Pi\) a partition of \(\mathcal S\). A \(\Pi\)-granular cut formulation assigns one recourse variable \(\theta_B\) and one family of weighted cuts to each block \(B\in\Pi\). The single-cut regime is \(\Pi=\{\mathcal S\}\); the fully disaggregated multicut regime is \(\Pi=\{\{s\}:s\in\mathcal S\}\); intermediate partitions define clustered regimes. A refinement \(\Pi'\) permits scenario information to be retained at finer resolution, and its complete blockwise formulation implies the corresponding coarser aggregated inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A scenario partition defines cut granularity: one block gives single-cut, singleton blocks give multicut, and intermediate blocks give clustered formulations.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal S\) is finite.
\(\Pi\) is a partition of \(\mathcal S\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Granularity regimes are indexed by scenario partitions, with partition refinement corresponding to finer blockwise recourse representation.

notation.meaning: recourse variable associated with block B

children.title: Cut Deletion Policies
children.top_down_role: Policies for removing cuts from active or archived pools.

knowledge_statements.title: Cut Deletion Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safeguarded removal of inactive cuts from a reusable decomposition pool.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iteration \(k\), assign each cut \(j\) an age \(a_j^k\) since its last activity and a recent maximum violation \(v_j^k\). Given thresholds \(A\) and \(\tau\), retain mandatory certificate cuts and delete only cuts satisfying \(a_j^k>A\) and \(v_j^k\le\tau\). Solve the reduced master, while preserving enough metadata to regenerate deleted cuts from the separation oracle. Before declaring convergence, run separation over all required scenarios and restore every violated valid cut. Deletion preserves relaxation validity but may lower its bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Delete only old, recently unviolated, nonmandatory cuts; retain regeneration data and perform complete separation before accepting convergence.
assumptions_latex: All retained cuts are valid.
A complete separation oracle is available before termination.
Mandatory certificate cuts are protected.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The reduced master remains a valid relaxation, and termination is accepted only when complete separation finds no required violated cut.

notation.meaning: iterations since cut j was last active
recent maximum violation of cut j

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: safeguarded deletion preserves correctness when complete separation precedes termination

children.title: Cut Compression Strategies
children.top_down_role: Strategies for reducing the storage or master-model burden of retained cuts.

knowledge_statements.title: Cut Compression Strategies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity-preserving replacement of cut families by conic combinations or dominating representatives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Represent valid inequalities as \(a_j^\top z\le b_j\). For coefficients \(\lambda_j\ge0\), their conic combination
\[\left(\sum_j\lambda_ja_j\right)^\top z\le\sum_j\lambda_jb_j\]
is valid and may replace several rows as a compressed summary. A cut may also be removed exactly when the remaining system implies it over the master domain. Conic aggregation without such implication is generally lossy: the compressed system contains every point feasible for the original cut family but may contain additional points. Exact compression requires equality of the two feasible regions on the master domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonnegative combinations produce valid compressed cuts, but compression is exact only when retained cuts imply every removed inequality over the master domain.
assumptions_latex: Each inequality \(a_j^\top z\le b_j\) is valid.
Every aggregation coefficient satisfies \(\lambda_j\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Conic compression preserves validity; it preserves the relaxation exactly if and only if the compressed and original cut systems define the same feasible region on the master domain.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: nonnegative conic combinations preserve inequality validity, while feasible-region equality characterizes lossless compression
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
