children.title: Information-Loss Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Loss of relaxation strength or certificate history caused by aggressive pool reduction.

knowledge_statements.title: Information-Loss Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact boundary between harmless pool reduction and weakened master information.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a closed convex base master domain, and let \(C\) and \(C'\) be families of affine inequalities defining nonempty closed convex feasible sets \[F=D\cap\bigcap_{c\in C}\{z:c(z)\le0\},\qquad F'=D\cap\bigcap_{c\in C'}\{z:c(z)\le0\}.\] Reduction is information-lossless exactly when \(F=F'\). If \(F\subsetneq F'\), then some linear minimization objective has a strictly smaller infimum over \(F'\) than over \(F\). For example, minimizing \(x\) on \([0,1]\) subject to the cut \(x\ge1\) has value \(1\); deleting that cut changes the relaxation value to \(0\). Regeneration cannot retroactively justify termination based on the weakened master.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For closed convex linear master systems, pool reduction is lossless exactly when it preserves the feasible region; strict enlargement can be exposed by a linear objective and can weaken the bound.
assumptions_latex: \(D\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is closed and convex.
The original and reduced cut families consist of affine inequalities.
\(F\) and \(F'\) are nonempty, closed, and satisfy \(F\subseteq F'\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F=F'\) characterizes lossless reduction; if \(F\subsetneq F'\), some linear objective has a strictly weaker minimization bound on \(F'\).

notation.meaning: original and reduced master feasible regions

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: equality of feasible regions characterizes losslessness, while strong separation exposes strict enlargement for closed convex systems

children.title: Cut Aging Mechanisms
children.top_down_role: Age-based tracking and prioritization within evolving cut pools.

assumptions_latex: At master iteration \(k\), the active pool contains valid affine cuts \(c_i(x)=\alpha_i+\beta_i^\top x\), indexed by \(i\in I_k\).
Each cut stores its last active iteration \(\ell_i(k)\) and an inactivity threshold \(H\in\mathbb{N}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Cuts inactive for at least \(H\) iterations are retired, while cut validity is unchanged.

notation.meaning: active cut index set at iteration k
last iteration at which cut i was active

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Iteration-count aging for valid affine cuts in a decomposition master problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(i\in I_k\), define the inactivity age by \(a_i(k)=k-\ell_i(k)\), where \(\ell_i(k)\) is the most recent iteration at which cut \(i\) was binding within the activity tolerance or had positive associated multiplier. Given \(H\in\mathbb{N}\), update the pool by \[I_{k+1}=\{i\in I_k:a_i(k)<H\}\cup N_{k+1},\] where \(N_{k+1}\) indexes newly generated valid cuts. Retiring \(i\) removes its inequality from the current master but does not invalidate the inequality; it may be restored later. Cuts designated permanent, including feasibility cuts required to exclude known infeasible trial points, are exempt from this aging rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cut’s age counts iterations since its last material activity; sufficiently old cuts are removed from the active master but remain valid and may be restored.
knowledge_statements.title: Cut Aging Mechanisms

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The iteration-age rule fits the algorithm container, but no evidence supports the activity criterion, permanent-cut exemptions, or convergence-safe deletion policy. A dedicated cut-management source is required.

children.title: Cut-Induced Numerical Instability
children.top_down_role: Numerical deterioration associated with accumulated, scaled, or nearly redundant cuts.

assumptions_latex: The master contains affine cuts \(\theta\geq \alpha_i+\beta_i^\top x\) represented in floating-point arithmetic.
The solver uses feasibility tolerance \(\tau_f>0\) and coefficient scaling measured by a positive factor \(s_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Poorly scaled or nearly dependent cuts can make numerical activity and feasibility decisions unreliable.

notation.meaning: positive scaling factor for cut i

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Floating-point instability caused by scaling and near dependence in an accumulated cut pool.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let cut \(i\) have scaled residual \(r_i(x,\theta)=(\theta-\alpha_i-\beta_i^\top x)/s_i\). If coefficient scales vary widely, or if distinct scaled normals satisfy \(\|\beta_i/s_i-\beta_j/s_j\|\) near machine precision while their right-hand sides differ at the scale of \(\tau_f\), then the active constraint matrix may be ill-conditioned. Consequently, computed slacks, multipliers, and basis choices can change under perturbations comparable to rounding error, and a solver may classify the same cut differently as active, redundant, or violated. Thus exact cut validity alone does not guarantee stable floating-point enforcement; scaling, duplicate detection, and residual validation are required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Valid cuts can still destabilize a master when their coefficients are badly scaled or nearly dependent, making computed slacks, multipliers, and basis choices unreliable.
knowledge_statements.title: Cut-Induced Numerical Instability

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role fits, but the claims about conditioning, machine-precision proximity, and solver classifications require a numerical linear-programming source with a specific locator.

children.title: Aging-Stability Interactions
children.top_down_role: Effects of age-based pool management on numerical conditioning.

assumptions_latex: Every generated cut is valid for the exact recourse epigraph.
The active pool is managed using age and numerical diagnostics.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Retirement is acceptable only when the retained model preserves required progress and numerical reliability.

notation.meaning: full set of cuts generated through iteration k
master lower approximation induced by a cut set

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tradeoff between removing inactive cuts and retaining a stable, informative master approximation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(I_k\subseteq G_k\), deletion weakens the master approximation pointwise because \[m_{I_k}(x)=\max_{i\in I_k}c_i(x)\leq \max_{i\in G_k}c_i(x)=m_{G_k}(x).\] Aging can nevertheless improve numerical stability by removing nearly dependent or poorly scaled rows. A stable aging policy therefore protects cuts needed for incumbent feasibility, certified lower bounds, or prescribed convergence safeguards; removes a cut only after sustained inactivity and acceptable conditioning tests; and restores or regenerates cuts when their violation exceeds a validation tolerance. Without such protection, aggressive aging can erase locally important model information, whereas unrestricted retention can degrade conditioning and master-solve reliability.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cut aging weakens the current approximation but may improve conditioning; a sound policy protects convergence-critical cuts and restores retired cuts when validation detects material violation.
knowledge_statements.title: Aging-Stability Interactions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The pointwise weakening inequality is correct, but the asserted stability benefits and convergence-critical retention, restoration, and conditioning safeguards need a source on dynamic cut deletion.

children.title: Subproblem Basis Reuse
children.top_down_role: Reuse of prior subproblem bases across related decomposition solves.

knowledge_statements.title: Subproblem Basis Reuse
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Simplex-basis reuse for sequential standard-form linear subproblems with a fixed constraint matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(P(p)=\min\{c(p)^\top u:Au=b(p),\ u\geq0\}\), where \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) has row rank \(m\). Let \(J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\), \(|J|=m\), be the previous basis index set and let \(B=A_{:J}\) be nonsingular. When the columns and their identifiers are unchanged, initialize the next simplex solve with \(J\), compute \(u_J=B^{-1}b(p)\), \(y=B^{-\top}c_J(p)\), and the current reduced costs, and then apply the required primal-simplex, dual-simplex, or feasibility-repair phase. Reject the stored basis if a defining column is absent, its identifier cannot be mapped, or \(B\) is singular. Return only the solution and basis verified for the current problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For standard-form linear subproblems with an unchanged matrix, reuse a mapped nonsingular simplex basis, recompute its primal, dual, and reduced-cost data, repair feasibility when necessary, and reject incompatible bases.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) has row rank \(m\), and consecutive subproblems differ only through \(b(p)\) or \(c(p)\).
The stored set \(J\) contains \(m\) mapped column identifiers and \(B=A_{:J}\) is nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The stored basis is an algebraically valid starting basis exactly while its mapped columns remain present and nonsingular; feasibility and optimality must be re-established for the current data.

children.title: Subproblem Warm Starts
children.top_down_role: Initialization of subproblem solves from prior computational states.

knowledge_statements.title: Subproblem Warm Starts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Solver-neutral warm-start interface for a sequence of related scenario subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p_k\in\mathcal{P}\) define the current model \(M(p_k)\), let \(z_{k-1}\in\mathcal{Z}_{k-1}\) be a stored solver state, and let \(\mathcal{C}(z_{k-1},p_k)\) be the interface's compatibility predicate. If \(\mathcal{C}(z_{k-1},p_k)\) holds, map supported components of \(z_{k-1}\) into the current state space \(\mathcal{Z}_k\), recompute all current-model residuals, and pass only validated components to the solver. Otherwise use cold initialization. Apply the ordinary feasibility, optimality, and termination tests for \(M(p_k)\), and return only the solution and certificate verified for the current model. Warm starting changes initialization, not the feasible set or optimality conditions of \(M(p_k)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Map a prior solver state into the current model only when the interface declares it compatible and current residual checks pass; otherwise initialize cold and verify the current solution normally.
assumptions_latex: The parameter space \(\mathcal{P}\), current model \(M(p_k)\), and old and new solver-state spaces \(\mathcal{Z}_{k-1}\) and \(\mathcal{Z}_k\) are specified.
The solver identifies which state components it supports and applies its ordinary current-model termination tests.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A compatible validated state may initialize the current solve, but it does not alter the exact feasible or optimal solution sets of the current model.

children.title: State-Transfer Compatibility
children.top_down_role: Compatibility conditions for transferring solver state across changing subproblems.

assumptions_latex: Old and new subproblem models have explicit variable and constraint identifiers.
A transfer map \(T\) is available for the stored solver state.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: State transfer is compatible exactly when mapped objects retain their structural meaning and pass current-model residual checks.

notation.meaning: stored solver state for the old model
mapping from old to new state coordinates

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural and numerical predicate for transferring solver state between related subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The transfer \(Tz\) is compatible with \(M'\) if and only if: every transferred variable, row, bound, and cone or integrality designation maps to the same mathematical object in \(M'\); every basis or active-set index maps bijectively to a present row or column and preserves the required nonsingularity or independence; sign, scaling, and dual conventions agree; and recomputed primal, dual, and complementarity residuals are finite and within the solver's initialization thresholds. For partial mappings, unmapped components must receive valid default initialization. Failure of any required clause makes the transferred state inadmissible, although transferable compatible components may be retained when the solver explicitly supports partial state reuse.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A solver state is transferable only when identifiers, dimensions, mathematical roles, conventions, and structural requirements match and recomputed residuals satisfy initialization thresholds.
knowledge_statements.title: State-Transfer Compatibility

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition container fits, but the stated if-and-only-if predicate combines solver-dependent requirements and thresholds as though universal. A solver-interface source is needed to determine the exact compatibility clauses.

children.title: Warm-Start Failure Regimes
children.top_down_role: Regimes where transferred solver information becomes ineffective or destabilizing.

assumptions_latex: A stored state is proposed for a changed subproblem.
The solver can compare warm and cold initialization or reject invalid state components.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Warm starting offers no guaranteed improvement and must fall back when transfer is invalid or counterproductive.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural and numerical regimes in which a transferred state is unusable or slower than a cold start.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Warm-start reuse fails structurally when \(z_{k-1}\) references removed rows or columns, violates changed variable types or cone structure, supplies a singular basis, or cannot be mapped to \(M_k\). It fails numerically when mapped residuals are nonfinite or exceed initialization thresholds. Even when admissible, it need not accelerate solution: degeneracy, a large active-set change, severe parameter perturbation, or barrier-state incompatibility may yield \(W(M_k;z_{k-1})\geq W(M_k;\mathrm{cold})\). Therefore no unconditional iteration reduction follows from compatibility alone. The interface must permit rejection, repair, and cold fallback, and should disable reuse after repeated validated performance regressions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Warm starts can be invalid after structural changes or singular mappings and can be slower under degeneracy or large perturbations, so rejection and cold fallback are necessary.
knowledge_statements.title: Warm-Start Failure Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind matches the leaf, but the structural, barrier-state, degeneracy, and performance-regression claims have no cited support.

children.title: Dual-Solution Recovery
children.top_down_role: Recovery of dual optimizer information needed for decomposition certificates.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual-Solution Recovery
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recovery of a mathematically valid Benders optimality-cut certificate for a finite fixed-recourse linear subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), \(W\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times p}\), \(T\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times n}\), \(h\in\mathbb{R}^r\), and \(q\in\mathbb{R}^p\), and define \(Q(x)=\min\{q^\top y:Wy\geq h-Tx,\ y\in\mathbb{R}^p\}\). Its dual feasible set is \(D=\{\pi\in\mathbb{R}^r:W^\top\pi=q,\ \pi\geq0\}\). Convert solver row multipliers to a vector \(\bar\pi\) in these conventions. If \(\bar\pi\in D\), then \(\theta\geq\bar\pi^\top(h-Tx')\) is a valid lower cut for every \(x'\in X\). If, additionally, a primal-feasible \(\bar y\) at the queried point satisfies \(q^\top\bar y=\bar\pi^\top(h-Tx)\), then \(\bar y\) and \(\bar\pi\) certify primal-dual optimality at \(x\). Numerical tolerance checks may screen a candidate, but exact feasibility or an independently certified correction is required before claiming an exact certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After converting solver multipliers, exact dual feasibility gives a globally valid lower cut, and equality with a primal-feasible value certifies optimality at the queried point; tolerance checks alone are not an exact certificate.
assumptions_latex: \(x\in X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), \(y\in\mathbb{R}^p\) is unrestricted, \(W\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times p}\), \(T\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times n}\), \(h\in\mathbb{R}^r\), and \(q\in\mathbb{R}^p\).
The primal subproblem has a finite optimum and strong linear-programming duality applies.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact dual feasibility yields a valid lower cut; a matching primal-feasible value additionally certifies optimality at the queried point.

notation.meaning: primal-feasible subproblem vector used for the value certificate

children.title: Extreme-Ray Recovery
children.top_down_role: Recovery of recession certificates needed for infeasibility cuts.

knowledge_statements.title: Extreme-Ray Recovery
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recovery of an extreme Farkas ray for an infeasible fixed-recourse linear subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), \(W\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times p}\), \(T\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times n}\), and \(h\in\mathbb{R}^r\), and define the recession cone \(C=\{r\in\mathbb{R}^r:r\geq0,\ W^\top r=0\}\). At an infeasible point \(x\in X\), recover a nonzero vector \(\bar r\) that generates an extreme ray of \(C\) and satisfies \(\bar r^\top(h-Tx)>0\). Normalize \(\bar r\), for example by \(\|\bar r\|_1=1\). Then \(\bar r^\top(h-Tx')\leq0\) is a valid feasibility cut for every \(x'\in X\) whose recourse system \(Wy\geq h-Tx'\), \(y\in\mathbb{R}^p\), is feasible, and it excludes the current point \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Recover and normalize an extreme ray of the nonnegative null cone that is positive on the current right-hand side; it certifies infeasibility and gives a feasibility cut excluding the current point.
assumptions_latex: \(x\in X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), \(y\in\mathbb{R}^p\) is unrestricted, \(W\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times p}\), \(T\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times n}\), and \(h\in\mathbb{R}^r\).
The recourse system \(Wy\geq h-Tx\) is infeasible, and an extreme ray of \(C\) with positive pairing against \(h-Tx\) has been recovered in the stated sign convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The validated extreme ray defines a feasibility cut valid for all master points with feasible recourse and violated by the current point.

notation.meaning: nonnegative recession cone used for Farkas certificates

children.title: Recovered-Certificate Validation
children.top_down_role: Validation of solver-reported dual solutions or extreme rays before master use.

knowledge_statements.title: Recovered-Certificate Validation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual screening followed by exact or independently certified validation of recovered dual solutions and Farkas rays.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=\{\pi\in\mathbb{R}^r:W^\top\pi=q,\ \pi\geq0\}\) and \(C=\{r\in\mathbb{R}^r:W^\top r=0,\ r\geq0\}\). Recompute all residuals from unscaled model data. For a recovered dual candidate \(\widehat\pi\), use \(\widehat\pi\geq-\tau_d\), \(\|W^\top\widehat\pi-q\|\leq\tau_d\), and the prescribed gap test only as numerical screening conditions; authorize an exact master cut only after obtaining a vector \(\bar\pi\in D\) by exact verification or an independently certified correction. For a recovered ray candidate \(\widehat r\), normalize and screen it using \(\widehat r\geq-\tau_d\), \(\|W^\top\widehat r\|\leq\tau_d\), and \(\widehat r^\top(h-Tx)>\tau_p\); authorize a feasibility cut only after obtaining \(\bar r\in C\setminus\{0\}\) with \(\bar r^\top(h-Tx)>0\). Set \(V=\mathrm{true}\) exactly when the applicable certified conditions hold; otherwise generate no exact master cut from the candidate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Screen recovered vectors with unscaled residuals, but authorize an exact master cut only after exact verification or an independently certified correction establishes dual feasibility or the Farkas-ray conditions.
assumptions_latex: \(W\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times p}\), \(q\in\mathbb{R}^p\), \(T\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times n}\), \(h\in\mathbb{R}^r\), and \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\) are expressed in unscaled mathematical-model conventions.
The screening tolerances \(\tau_d>0\), \(\tau_p>0\), and any gap tolerance are fixed, and an exact-verification or certified-correction mechanism is identified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Tolerance tests screen numerical candidates; exact or independently certified feasibility and separation conditions determine whether an exact master cut is authorized.

notation.meaning: certificate acceptance predicate for exact cut generation

knowledge_statements.title: Inexact Subproblem Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certified inexact dual oracle for a fixed-recourse linear subproblem used by a decomposition master.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), \(W\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times p}\), \(T\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times n}\), \(h\in\mathbb{R}^r\), and \(q\in\mathbb{R}^p\), and define \(D=\{\pi\in\mathbb{R}^r:W^\top\pi=q,\ \pi\geq0\}\) and \(Q(x)=\max_{\pi\in D}\pi^\top(h-Tx)\). At a query point \(x\in X\), an \(\varepsilon\)-inexact subproblem interface returns \((\widehat\pi,\widehat v,\varepsilon)\in D\times\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{R}_+\) such that \(\widehat v=\widehat\pi^\top(h-Tx)\) and \(0\leq Q(x)-\widehat v\leq\varepsilon\). For every \(x'\in X\), the inequality \(\theta\geq\widehat\pi^\top(h-Tx')\) is a valid lower cut, where \(\theta\in\mathbb{R}\) is the master recourse epigraph variable. Without dual feasibility and a certified error bound, the response is not a certified inexact-cut oracle.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A certified inexact interface returns an exactly dual-feasible affine lower cut and a nonnegative certified bound on its value error at the queried master point.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), \(W\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times p}\), \(T\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times n}\), \(h\in\mathbb{R}^r\), and \(q\in\mathbb{R}^p\) define a fixed-recourse dual problem.
The queried value \(Q(x)\) is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The interface supplies a globally valid affine lower cut and an explicit certified upper bound on its underestimation at the query point.

children.title: Solver-Tolerance Effects
children.top_down_role: Effects of subproblem solver tolerances on returned certificate data.

knowledge_statements.title: Solver-Tolerance Effects
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional conversion of dual residual and optimization tolerances into query-point cut-value error for fixed-recourse linear subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=\{\pi\in\mathbb{R}^r:W^\top\pi=q,\ \pi\geq0\}\) be nonempty, let \(Q(x)=\max_{\pi\in D}\pi^\top(h-Tx)\), and fix a norm \(\|\cdot\|\) on \(\mathbb{R}^r\) with dual norm \(\|\cdot\|_*\) on \(\mathbb{R}^r\). Suppose a returned vector \(\widehat\pi\in\mathbb{R}^r\) admits \(\pi^0\in D\) satisfying \(\|\widehat\pi-\pi^0\|\leq\kappa\tau_d\) and \(0\leq Q(x)-(\pi^0)^\top(h-Tx)\leq\tau_g\). Then its query-value error satisfies \(\big|Q(x)-\widehat\pi^\top(h-Tx)\big|\leq\tau_g+\kappa\tau_d\|h-Tx\|_*\). This bound is conditional on the stated error-bound constant and certified gap. Unless \(\widehat\pi\in D\), its raw affine function is not automatically a globally valid lower cut and must be replaced by a certified feasible correction or a rigorously relaxed cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dual tolerance yields a query-value error bound only when a problem-specific distance bound, a compatible norm pair, and a certified optimization gap are available; an infeasible multiplier does not automatically define a valid global cut.
assumptions_latex: \(W\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times p}\), \(q\in\mathbb{R}^p\), \(T\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times n}\), \(h\in\mathbb{R}^r\), and \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and \(D\) is nonempty.
A norm and its dual norm are fixed, and certified constants \(\kappa\geq0\), \(\tau_d\geq0\), and \(\tau_g\geq0\) satisfy the stated distance and optimization-gap conditions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The absolute query-value error is at most \(\tau_g+\kappa\tau_d\|h-Tx\|_*\); global cut validity still requires exact or certified dual feasibility.

notation.meaning: dual residual tolerance entering the distance bound
certified optimization-gap bound for the feasible comparison vector

children.title: Dual-Recovery Errors
children.top_down_role: Errors introduced while extracting or reconstructing dual certificate information.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual-Recovery Errors
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex scenario subproblems with approximately recovered dual multipliers and reported subproblem values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\varepsilon_s^k\geq0\) be a certified allowance satisfying
\[Q_s(x)\geq \widehat q_s^k+(\widehat g_s^k)^{\mathsf T}(x-x^k)-\varepsilon_s^k\qquad\text{for every }x\in X.\]
Then
\[\delta_s^k=\varepsilon_s^k+Q_s(x^k)-\widehat q_s^k\geq0\]
and \(\widehat g_s^k\in\partial_{\delta_s^k}Q_s(x^k)\). If \(\widehat q_s^k=Q_s(x^k)\), then \(\delta_s^k=\varepsilon_s^k\). The affine cut is globally valid on \(X\) only with the certified subtraction of \(\varepsilon_s^k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A recovered affine cut with error allowance epsilon is valid after subtracting that allowance. Its subgradient error also includes the difference between the true and reported values at the query point.
assumptions_latex: For scenario \(s\), the recourse value \(Q_s:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper and convex on the convex set \(X\).
At \(x^k\in X\), the subproblem interface returns \((\widehat q_s^k,\widehat g_s^k)\) with \(Q_s(x^k)\) finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The recovered vector is a \(\delta_s^k\)-subgradient, where \(\delta_s^k=\varepsilon_s^k+Q_s(x^k)-\widehat q_s^k\), and the reported affine cut underestimates \(Q_s\) after subtracting \(\varepsilon_s^k\).

notation.meaning: recovered value and subgradient pair at iteration k

children.title: Master-Certificate Error Propagation
children.top_down_role: Transmission of subproblem numerical errors into cuts, bounds, and stopping certificates.

assumptions_latex: The problem is a minimization problem with optimal value \(v^*\).
A computed lower certificate \(\widehat L_k\) and feasible-incumbent value \(\widehat U_k\) have certified errors \(\eta_{L,k},\eta_{U,k}\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The true incumbent suboptimality is at most \((\widehat U_k-\widehat L_k)+\eta_{L,k}+\eta_{U,k}\).

notation.meaning: computed master lower and incumbent upper certificates
certified lower- and upper-side error allowances

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive propagation of subproblem and evaluation errors into a minimization certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose the certified inequalities
\[\widehat L_k-\eta_{L,k}\leq v^*\leq f(x_k^{\mathrm{inc}})\leq \widehat U_k+\eta_{U,k}\]
hold. Then
\[0\leq f(x_k^{\mathrm{inc}})-v^*\leq (\widehat U_k-\widehat L_k)+\eta_{L,k}+\eta_{U,k}.\]
Consequently, termination at requested tolerance \(\tau\) is certified whenever the right-hand side is at most \(\tau\), rather than merely when the uncorrected computed gap is at most \(\tau\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Certified lower- and upper-side errors add to the computed master gap; termination is valid only when this corrected gap meets the requested tolerance.
knowledge_statements.title: Master-Certificate Error Propagation

children.title: Stopping-Certificate Integrity
children.top_down_role: Numerical integrity of method-specific stopping certificates without duplicating their statistical or deterministic constructions.

children.title: Bound-Monotonicity Checks
children.top_down_role: Checks for expected directional behavior in evolving decomposition bounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Bound-Monotonicity Checks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: History check for nested accumulated-cut master bounds and best-so-far feasible-incumbent bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The bound-monotonicity diagnostic accepts iteration \(k\) exactly when
\[L_k-L_{k-1}\geq-\delta_k\qquad\text{and}\qquad U_k-U_{k-1}\leq\delta_k.\]
Under a fixed minimization objective and nested retained master constraints, the first inequality checks the expected nondecrease of the master lower bound. When \(U_k\) is the best feasible value observed through iteration \(k\), the second checks its expected nonincrease. A violation larger than \(\delta_k\) is an integrity anomaly rather than evidence of convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With nested retained master constraints, the lower-bound history should not decrease; a best-so-far feasible upper-bound history should not increase. Either change may be tolerated only within the declared numerical allowance.
assumptions_latex: For a minimization problem with a fixed objective, \(L_k\) is obtained from a master problem whose valid constraint set contains the constraint set used to compute \(L_{k-1}\).
The value \(U_k\) is the best certified feasible objective value observed through iteration \(k\).
The implementation uses a diagnostic tolerance \(\delta_k\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The history passes when \(L_k\geq L_{k-1}-\delta_k\) and \(U_k\leq U_{k-1}+\delta_k\).

notation.meaning: nested-master lower-bound and best-incumbent upper-bound histories

children.title: Bound-Consistency Diagnostics
children.top_down_role: Diagnostics comparing bounds across iterations, replications, or certificate sources.

assumptions_latex: The problem is a minimization problem with optimal value \(v^*\).
Reported bounds have certified outward error allowances \(\eta_{L,k},\eta_{U,k}\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Consistency holds when \(L_k-\eta_{L,k}\leq U_k+\eta_{U,k}\); exact certified bounds additionally enclose \(v^*\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Same-iteration ordering and enclosure checks for minimization bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define the relaxed consistency margin by
\[c_k=(U_k+\eta_{U,k})-(L_k-\eta_{L,k}).\]
The reported pair passes the bound-consistency diagnostic exactly when \(c_k\geq0\). If \(L_k\) and \(U_k\) are exact certified bounds, they must satisfy \(L_k\leq v^*\leq U_k\). Hence \(c_k<0\) proves that at least one bound, error allowance, objective convention, or iteration association is invalid.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lower and upper certificates are mutually consistent only when their error-expanded intervals overlap; a negative relaxed gap proves a certificate or bookkeeping defect.
knowledge_statements.title: Bound-Consistency Diagnostics

children.title: Bound-Anomaly Classification
children.top_down_role: Classification of bound reversals, contradictions, and unexplained discontinuities.

assumptions_latex: Bounds \((L_k,U_k)\) and tolerances \((\delta_k,\eta_{L,k},\eta_{U,k})\) are available for a minimization run.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each anomaly is classified by which monotonicity or consistency predicate fails.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Predicate-based taxonomy for bound-history and same-iteration anomalies.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At iteration \(k\), define
\[A_k^L=\{L_k<L_{k-1}-\delta_k\},\qquad A_k^U=\{U_k>U_{k-1}+\delta_k\},\]
\[A_k^C=\{L_k-\eta_{L,k}>U_k+\eta_{U,k}\}.\]
The anomaly class is the subset of \(\{L,U,C\}\) whose predicates hold. Class \(L\) indicates lower-bound regression, class \(U\) incumbent regression, and class \(C\) incompatible certificates; simultaneous predicates form a compound anomaly requiring all implicated interfaces to remain uncertified.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bound anomalies are classified as lower regression, upper regression, certificate crossing, or a compound class when several corresponding predicates fail together.
knowledge_statements.title: Bound-Anomaly Classification

children.title: Residual Diagnostics
children.top_down_role: Diagnostics based on primal, dual, or subproblem residual behavior.

assumptions_latex: Scenario copies \(x_s^k\) and a consensus vector \(z^k\) are produced with probabilities \(p_s>0\), where \(\sum_s p_s=1\).
A penalty parameter \(\rho_k>0\) is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The pair \((r_k,d_k)\) quantifies primal nonanticipativity error and successive consensus motion.

notation.meaning: scenario primal copies and consensus vector

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consensus-form residuals for scenario-copy decomposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a consensus-form scenario decomposition, define
\[r_k=\left(\sum_s p_s\lVert x_s^k-z^k\rVert_2^2\right)^{1/2},\qquad d_k=\rho_k\lVert z^k-z^{k-1}\rVert_2.\]
The primal residual \(r_k\) measures violation of the scenario-consensus equations. The scaled motion residual \(d_k\) detects whether the shared decision remains materially unsettled. Residual termination requires separately declared thresholds for both quantities; one small residual cannot substitute for the other.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weighted scenario disagreement measures primal infeasibility, while scaled consensus motion detects continued iteration movement; both require explicit stopping thresholds.
knowledge_statements.title: Residual Diagnostics

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The primal residual is well defined, but the quantity rho times successive consensus motion is method-specific and is not a generic residual for every scenario-copy decomposition. A source tied to the selected algorithm and its exact residual scaling is required.

children.title: Consensus Diagnostics
children.top_down_role: Diagnostics for agreement across scenarios, copies, or distributed workers.

assumptions_latex: Scenario decisions \(x_s^k\in\mathbb R^n\) have probabilities \(p_s>0\) summing to one.
Consensus is defined by \(z^k=\sum_s p_sx_s^k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Consensus is accepted exactly when both aggregate and worst-scenario deviations meet their declared tolerances.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Aggregate and worst-case checks for scenario nonanticipativity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Set
\[r_k=\left(\sum_s p_s\lVert x_s^k-z^k\rVert_2^2\right)^{1/2},\qquad m_k=\max_s\lVert x_s^k-z^k\rVert_2.\]
For declared tolerances \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{avg}},\varepsilon_{\max}\geq0\), the consensus diagnostic passes exactly when
\[r_k\leq\varepsilon_{\mathrm{avg}}\qquad\text{and}\qquad m_k\leq\varepsilon_{\max}.\]
The second condition prevents a low-probability scenario with a large nonanticipativity violation from being hidden by the probability-weighted aggregate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Consensus passes only when both probability-weighted disagreement and the largest individual scenario deviation are below their respective tolerances.
knowledge_statements.title: Consensus Diagnostics

children.title: Cross-Diagnostic Disagreement
children.top_down_role: Cases where residual evidence conflicts with consensus evidence.

assumptions_latex: A gap diagnostic \(G_k\) and a residual-consensus diagnostic \(R_k\) return Boolean pass values at the same iteration.
Neither diagnostic alone is assumed sufficient for termination.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Cross-diagnostic disagreement occurs exactly when \(G_k\oplus R_k\) is true.

notation.meaning: pass predicate for the corrected optimality-gap test
pass predicate for all required residual and consensus tests

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical disagreement between bound-based and residual-based stopping evidence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define \(G_k\) to mean that the error-corrected optimality gap passes its tolerance, and define \(R_k\) to mean that every required residual and consensus test passes. Cross-diagnostic disagreement is
\[D_k=G_k\oplus R_k=(G_k\wedge\neg R_k)\vee(\neg G_k\wedge R_k).\]
When \(D_k\) holds, the combined stopping certificate fails: gap-only acceptance may hide infeasibility or unsettled consensus, while residual-only acceptance may hide objective suboptimality or invalid bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A disagreement is present when exactly one of the corrected-gap and residual-consensus systems passes; the combined termination certificate must then fail.
knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Diagnostic Disagreement

children.title: Premature Termination
children.top_down_role: Termination events occurring before the required optimization evidence is established.

knowledge_statements.title: Premature Termination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete failure caused by an invalid lower certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider
\[\min\{x:0\leq x\leq1\}.\]
Its optimal value is \(v^*=0\). Let the current feasible incumbent be \(x^{\mathrm{inc}}=1\), so \(\widehat U=1\), and suppose an erroneous master certificate reports \(\widehat L=1\). Then \(\widehat U-\widehat L=0\), so every nonnegative gap tolerance accepts termination, although
\[f(x^{\mathrm{inc}})-v^*=1.\]
Thus a small reported gap does not prevent premature termination unless both bounding roles are independently certified.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimizing x on [0,1] gives a counterexample: an invalid lower bound equal to a poor incumbent creates a zero reported gap despite unit suboptimality.
assumptions_latex: Termination uses only the reported condition \(\widehat U-\widehat L\leq\tau\), without validating the lower certificate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A zero reported gap can coexist with strictly positive incumbent suboptimality.

children.title: Misleading Optimality Gaps
children.top_down_role: Reported gaps that overstate solution quality or certificate strength.

knowledge_statements.title: Misleading Optimality Gaps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive inward errors that make a reported minimization gap optimistic.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The valid gap is \(g=U-L\), whereas the reported gap is
\[\widehat g=\widehat U-\widehat L=(U-e_U)-(L+e_L)=g-(e_L+e_U).\]
Hence \(\widehat g\leq\tau\) implies only
\[g\leq\tau+e_L+e_U.\]
If the inward error sum is not certified, \(\widehat g\) may be arbitrarily smaller than \(g\), may equal zero for a positive valid gap, or may become negative. Such a value is not an optimality certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Unaccounted upward lower-bound error and downward upper-bound error shrink the reported gap by their sum, potentially making it zero or negative.
assumptions_latex: For a minimization problem, the reported quantities satisfy \(\widehat L=L+e_L\) and \(\widehat U=U-e_U\), where \(L\leq v^*\leq U\).
The errors \(e_L,e_U\geq0\) are omitted from the stopping test.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The reported gap can understate the valid gap by \(e_L+e_U\).

children.title: Gap-Induced Termination Risk
children.top_down_role: Pathways through which unreliable gap estimates trigger premature stopping.

knowledge_statements.title: Gap-Induced Termination Risk
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic suboptimality risk from stopping on an uncorrected computed gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Under the certified outward corrections,
\[f(x_k^{\mathrm{inc}})-v^*\leq(\widehat U_k-\widehat L_k)+\eta_{L,k}+\eta_{U,k}.\]
Therefore the uncorrected rule \(\widehat U_k-\widehat L_k\leq\tau\) provides at best the guarantee
\[f(x_k^{\mathrm{inc}})-v^*\leq\tau+\eta_{L,k}+\eta_{U,k}.\]
To guarantee true tolerance \(\tau\), termination must instead require the corrected gap to be at most \(\tau\). If the error allowances are unknown, no finite suboptimality guarantee follows from the reported gap alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stopping on an uncorrected gap inflates the true suboptimality guarantee by both certificate errors; unknown errors leave no finite guarantee.
assumptions_latex: A minimization algorithm stops when \(\widehat U_k-\widehat L_k\leq\tau\).
Certified outward corrections satisfy \(\widehat L_k-\eta_{L,k}\leq v^*\leq f(x_k^{\mathrm{inc}})\leq\widehat U_k+\eta_{U,k}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The stopping rule guarantees only \(f(x_k^{\mathrm{inc}})-v^*\leq\tau+\eta_{L,k}+\eta_{U,k}\).

assumptions_latex: A finite-scenario two-stage convex program has recourse \(Q(x)=\sum_{s=1}^S p_sQ_s(x)\), with \(p_s>0\) and \(\sum_s p_s=1\).
Conditional on a trial point \(x^k\), scenario subproblems are mutually independent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: All scenario oracle calls may execute concurrently, after which their cuts are aggregated into the next master problem.

notation.meaning: master trial point at iteration k
scenario value and subgradient returned by worker s

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Synchronous scenario-parallel L-shaped architecture for finite convex recourse.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Initialize a master model and obtain \(x^0\). At iteration \(k\), broadcast \(x^k\) to workers \(s=1,\ldots,S\). In parallel, worker \(s\) solves its scenario subproblem and returns \(q_s^k=Q_s(x^k)\) and \(g_s^k\in\partial Q_s(x^k)\). Add either the disaggregated cuts
\[\theta_s\geq q_s^k+(g_s^k)^{\mathsf T}(x-x^k)\]
or their probability-weighted aggregate, solve the updated master, and obtain \(x^{k+1}\). Stop only when the declared bound and feasibility certificates pass; output the best certified feasible incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Broadcast each master point, solve independent scenario subproblems concurrently, aggregate their cuts, update the master, and return the best certified incumbent after valid stopping tests.
knowledge_statements.title: Scenario-Parallel Architectures
Stage-Parallel Architectures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Task-graph model for finite-stage scenario decomposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(t\), let \(\mathcal T_t=\{J_v:v\in V_t\}\), where task \(J_v\) solves the local problem at node \(v\). Tasks in \(\mathcal T_t\) may execute concurrently once their required incoming state or multiplier data are available. A stage-parallel architecture is a directed acyclic task graph with an edge \(J_u\to J_v\) whenever the computation at \(v\in V_{t+1}\) consumes output from \(u\in V_t\). Thus every dependency path respects increasing stage index, and the execution time is governed by the longest weighted dependency path, including any communication and synchronization costs on that path.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A stage-parallel architecture executes dependency-ready node problems from the same stage concurrently while preserving interstage dependencies; its runtime is governed by the longest weighted dependency path.
assumptions_latex: A finite scenario tree has stages \(t=0,\ldots,T\), with node sets \(V_t\).
Each node subproblem communicates only through explicitly represented interstage state or multiplier data.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The union \(\mathcal T=\bigcup_{t=0}^{T}\mathcal T_t\), together with the stated dependency edges, is a stage-parallel directed acyclic task graph whose critical-path time is the maximum total weight of a dependency path.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: task-graph representation of stagewise decomposition

assumptions_latex: A finite collection of decomposition tasks has a directed dependency graph \(G=(V,E)\).
Every transmitted task version and dependency version is identifiable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every committed task result is dependency-consistent, although workers need not advance in lockstep.

notation.meaning: Latest committed version of task v

review_flags: exact convergence conditions depend on the decomposition update map
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Versioned asynchronous scheduling, independent of a particular decomposition convergence theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize every task version \(k_v=0\) and place each dependency-satisfied task in a ready queue. Whenever a worker becomes free, it removes any ready task \(v\), reads a versioned snapshot of all predecessor outputs, computes a candidate local update, and returns the result with those dependency versions. The controller commits the candidate only if its prescribed consistency rule accepts that snapshot; it then increments \(k_v\) and releases newly ready successors. Execution stops when the global residual and all required local residuals meet their tolerances; the output is the latest committed collection.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Workers solve ready subproblems without global barriers, while version checks ensure that every accepted result uses an admissible dependency snapshot.
knowledge_statements.title: Asynchronous Decomposition Architectures

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithmic role fits an asynchronous architecture, but the admissible snapshot rule, readiness semantics, residuals, and guarantees are left unspecified. A source tied to a concrete asynchronous decomposition model is needed.

children.title: Decomposition Load Balancing
children.top_down_role: Distribution of scenario, stage, or subproblem workloads across workers.

knowledge_statements.title: Decomposition Load Balancing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Static load balance for heterogeneous decomposition-task costs on identical workers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((A_1,\ldots,A_p)\) be a feasible partition of the tasks among the workers. Define \(L_j=\sum_{i\in A_j}c_i\), \(C=\sum_{i=1}^n c_i\), and \(M=\max_{1\le j\le p}L_j\). When \(C>0\), define \(\rho=M/(C/p)\); the assignment is \(\varepsilon\)-balanced for \(\varepsilon\ge 0\) when \(\rho\le 1+\varepsilon\). When \(C=0\), it is balanced by convention. Dynamic load balancing applies the same criterion to remaining estimated costs at a scheduling epoch, subject to task dependencies and state-migration constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A decomposition assignment is epsilon-balanced when its largest assigned workload is at most (1+epsilon) times the average workload.
assumptions_latex: Tasks \(i=1,\ldots,n\) have estimated processing costs \(c_i\ge 0\).
There are \(p\ge 1\) identical workers.
The sets \(A_1,\ldots,A_p\) form a partition of \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\), and all task dependencies are respected.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For \(C>0\), the imbalance factor satisfies \(\rho\ge 1\), with equality if and only if \(L_j=C/p\) for every \(j=1,\ldots,p\).
review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

children.title: Communication Bottlenecks
children.top_down_role: Network, synchronization, or data-transfer limits on distributed decomposition.

assumptions_latex: Each iteration performs worker computations followed by required communication.
Communication time includes latency, transfer, synchronization, and contention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Communication is the iteration bottleneck exactly when \(T_{\mathrm{comm}}\ge T_{\mathrm{comp}}\), and its runtime share is at least one half.
review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational bottleneck boundary under a non-overlapped iteration model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under a non-overlapped execution model, write the iteration time as \(T=T_{\mathrm{comp}}+T_{\mathrm{comm}}\) and define \(\phi=T_{\mathrm{comm}}/T\). The architecture is communication-dominated when \(T_{\mathrm{comm}}\ge T_{\mathrm{comp}}\), equivalently \(\phi\ge 1/2\). In this regime, reducing all computation times to zero can improve runtime by at most the factor \(T/T_{\mathrm{comm}}\le 2\). Consequently, adding workers without reducing latency, message volume, synchronization, or contention cannot yield unbounded strong scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Communication is the bottleneck when it occupies at least half the critical-path iteration time, limiting gains obtainable solely by accelerating computation.
knowledge_statements.title: Communication Bottlenecks

children.title: Compute-Communication Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Architectural tradeoffs between balanced computation and coordination overhead.

assumptions_latex: An architecture choice \(a\) determines computation, communication, and synchronization costs.
All compared choices satisfy the same numerical accuracy and stopping criterion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An admissible architecture is preferable precisely through its total-time objective, not through computation or communication cost alone.

notation.meaning: Expected solution time under architecture a

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: additive performance model for parallel algorithms
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Expected time-to-solution criterion at fixed accuracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each \(a\in\mathcal A\), let \(N(a)\) be the random number of iterations to termination and let \(C_k(a)\), \(M_k(a)\), and \(S_k(a)\) denote critical-path computation, communication, and synchronization times in iteration \(k\). Define \(T(a)=\mathbb E[\sum_{k=1}^{N(a)}(C_k(a)+M_k(a)+S_k(a))]\). The compute-communication tradeoff is resolved by minimizing \(T(a)\) over accuracy-equivalent choices. Extra local computation is beneficial exactly when its increase is outweighed by the resulting decrease in communication, synchronization, or iteration count.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At fixed solution accuracy, architecture choices should minimize expected total solution time, allowing extra local computation when it sufficiently reduces communication or iterations.
knowledge_statements.title: Compute-Communication Tradeoffs

children.title: Straggler-Dominated Regimes
children.top_down_role: Execution regimes where slow workers determine overall progress.

knowledge_statements.title: Straggler-Dominated Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Synchronous-round criterion based on the maximum task-time order statistic.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X_{(p)}=\max_{1\le j\le p}X_j\) and let the synchronous round time be \(R=X_{(p)}+H\), where \(H\ge 0\) is communication and synchronization time not included in the task times. Fix an operational threshold \(\eta\in(1/2,1)\). The regime is called straggler-dominated when \(\mathbb E[X_{(p)}]/\mathbb E[R]\ge\eta\). The boundary occurs at equality. This definition applies to synchronous rounds; asynchronous or redundant execution requires a different runtime model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a chosen majority threshold, a synchronous regime is straggler-dominated when the expected slowest-task time contributes at least that fraction of expected round time.
assumptions_latex: A synchronous round assigns one task to each of \(p\ge 1\) participating workers.
Task completion times \(X_1,\ldots,X_p\) and overhead \(H\) are nonnegative random variables.
The expectations satisfy \(0<\mathbb E[R]<\infty\), where \(R=\max_{1\le j\le p}X_j+H\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For a prescribed \(\eta\in(1/2,1)\), the round is straggler-dominated exactly when \(\mathbb E[X_{(p)}]/\mathbb E[R]\ge\eta\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: order-statistic model of synchronous stragglers
threshold eta is an operational convention
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

children.title: Random-Stream Management
children.top_down_role: Organization of random streams across sampling tasks, stages, and workers.

assumptions_latex: A deterministic pseudorandom generator supports disjoint indexed substreams.
Logical tasks have stable identifiers independent of worker placement or completion order.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each logical task receives a deterministic nonoverlapping random stream, so rescheduling does not change its generated variates.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Schedule-independent allocation of pseudorandom substreams to logical tasks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose a master key \(K\) and an injective encoding of each logical task identifier \(q\). Initialize task \(q\) at the beginning of substream \(S_q=\operatorname{Split}(K,q)\). Every random request by that task consumes the next unused value of \(S_q\); retries restore the last committed counter, while a deliberate continuation restores the next counter. Substreams must be disjoint over the maximum permitted consumption range. Record \(K\), the generator and splitting versions, \(q\), and the committed counter. Stop stream consumption when the task terminates and output its final counter with its result.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Assign each logical task a deterministic disjoint substream and persist its counter, making random draws independent of scheduling and worker placement.
knowledge_statements.title: Random-Stream Management

children.title: Seed Control
children.top_down_role: Governance of initialization seeds across runs and computational components.

assumptions_latex: The pseudorandom generator is deterministic given its seed and version.
Seeds lie in a finite admissible set \(\mathcal S\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The complete seed key determines every initialized stream, while distinct logical identifiers receive distinct derived seeds whenever the derivation is injective.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic hierarchical seed derivation for parallel stochastic computation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Seed control consists of recording a master seed \(s_0\in\mathcal S\) and deriving every logical stream seed by \(s_q=h(s_0,q)\). The map \(h\) must be deterministic and injective on the identifiers used in a run, or must instead initialize generator substreams proved disjoint over their consumption ranges. Seed derivation may depend on stable scenario, replication, stage, and task identifiers, but not on worker number, wall-clock time, or completion order. Reuse of the same complete key and generator version must reproduce the same initialized state.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Derive every task seed deterministically from a recorded master seed and stable identifiers, avoiding dependence on workers, clocks, or scheduling order.
knowledge_statements.title: Seed Control

children.title: Cross-Run Stream Reproduction
children.top_down_role: Reproduction of stochastic inputs across repeated computational experiments.

assumptions_latex: Two runs use the same generator implementation, numerical inputs, and logical stream identifiers.
Each logical task consumes random values according to the same deterministic request sequence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The two runs produce identical logical random streams, regardless of worker assignment or admissible execution interleaving.

notation.meaning: Value at position k of logical stream q in run r

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: determinism of versioned pseudorandom stream replay
floating-point and nondeterministic solver behavior remain outside this property
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical-stream equality across runs, not full bitwise equality of solver outputs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R\) contain the generator and splitting algorithm versions, master seed, stream identifiers, initial states, and committed counters. Cross-run stream reproduction holds when, for any runs \(r\) and \(r'\) initialized from the same \(R\), \(U^{(r)}_{q,k}=U^{(r')}_{q,k}\) for every logical stream \(q\) and every requested position \(k\). Worker placement and execution order may differ, provided neither changes logical identifiers, request positions, or committed counter transitions. This property alone does not imply identical floating-point optimization outputs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two runs reproduce their random streams when every logical stream position matches under the same recorded generator configuration, despite different schedules.
knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Run Stream Reproduction

children.title: Sample-Path Logging
children.top_down_role: Records of sampled trajectories used during stochastic decomposition.

knowledge_statements.title: Sample-Path Logging
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Replayable provenance certificate for one simulated sample path.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a path identifier \(p\), a sample-path log \(L_p\) records \(x_0\in\mathcal X_0\) and, for each \(t=0,\ldots,T-1\), the random coordinate \((q_t,k_t)\), realized variate \(u_t\in\mathcal U_t\), transition-map version, and resulting state \(x_{t+1}\in\mathcal X_{t+1}\). It is valid when \(u_t=U_{q_t,k_t}\) and \(x_{t+1}=F_t(x_t,u_t)\) at every stage. Together with the recorded generator configuration and transition versions, \(L_p\) is a replay certificate when a verifier can regenerate every \(u_t\), recompute every transition, and check the recorded equalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sample-path log is a replay certificate when it records the versioned random coordinates, states, and deterministic transitions needed to regenerate and check every path step.
assumptions_latex: Each realized sample path is generated by a finite ordered sequence of random requests.
For each \(t\), the recorded version of \(F_t:\mathcal X_t\times\mathcal U_t\to\mathcal X_{t+1}\) is deterministic.
The generator configuration deterministically defines every recorded value \(U_{q,k}\).
Log records are immutable or integrity protected.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A verifier supplied with \(L_p\), the recorded generator configuration, and the recorded transition versions can replay the path and compare every reconstructed variate and state with its logged value.

notation.meaning: Versioned state-transition map at stage t
Value at position k of logical random stream q

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: replay certificate from initial state, random coordinates, and versioned deterministic transitions

children.title: Scenario-Provenance Logging
children.top_down_role: Records of scenario origins, transformations, versions, and computational use.

assumptions_latex: Every scenario and transformation receives a stable identifier.
Provenance records form an immutable directed acyclic graph.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The logged ancestry is a verifiable certificate of how each scenario was generated from recorded roots and transformations.
review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Content-addressed provenance for generated, reduced, or transformed scenarios.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every scenario object \(v\in V_P\), record its identifier, content digest \(d(v)\), parent identifiers, transformation \(g_v\) with parameters and version, random-stream coordinates if used, and creation metadata. An edge \((u,v)\in E_P\) means that \(u\) is an input to \(g_v\). A record is valid when all parent records exist, \(G_P\) is acyclic, recomputation gives the recorded scenario content, and its digest equals \(d(v)\). Root records instead identify immutable source data and verify their digests directly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scenario provenance is certified by an acyclic log of content digests, parents, versioned transformations, parameters, and any random-stream coordinates used.
knowledge_statements.title: Scenario-Provenance Logging

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate role and internal DAG checks are coherent, but no inspectable source supports this particular content-addressed scenario-provenance model or its claimed verification semantics.

children.title: Path-to-Scenario Traceability
children.top_down_role: Traceability links between realized sample paths and their scenario sources.

assumptions_latex: Each scenario is induced by one or more logged sample paths.
Both path and scenario records use stable identifiers and integrity-protected digests.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The relation \(R\) and its supporting records certify which path contributions produced every scenario and permit reverse lookup from either side.
review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bidirectional traceability between replayable paths and derived scenario objects.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Path-to-scenario traceability is a relation \(R\subseteq P\times S\) whose entry \((p,s)\) stores the path digest, scenario digest, mapping or aggregation transformation, parameters, version, and contribution weight when applicable. The trace is complete when every scenario \(s\) names all contributing paths required by its transformation, and every referenced path has a valid sample-path log. It is sound when replaying those paths and applying the recorded transformation reproduces the content digest of \(s\). Indexed projections of \(R\) must support both scenario-to-path and path-to-scenario queries.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A path-to-scenario trace is valid when all contributing paths are logged and their recorded transformation reproduces the scenario digest, with lookup in both directions.
knowledge_statements.title: Path-to-Scenario Traceability

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate role is plausible and the soundness and completeness conditions are intelligible, but an authoritative source is needed for this domain-specific path-to-scenario traceability construction.

children.title: Parallel Reproducibility
children.top_down_role: Repeatability of stochastic decomposition across parallel executions.

assumptions_latex: The scenario data, initial state, stopping rule, software environment, and random seed are fixed.
Let \(\mathcal S\) be the set of admissible parallel schedules for one decomposition run.
Each schedule \(s\in\mathcal S\) produces a recorded output \(Y(s)\) in a specified output space \(\mathcal Y\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Y(s)=Y(t)\) for every \(s,t\in\mathcal S\).

notation.meaning: Set of admissible task schedules and interleavings.
Complete recorded output under schedule s, including iterates and termination status.
Output space with an explicitly chosen equality convention.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: parallel reproducibility is conventionally expressed as invariance of recorded output over admissible schedules under fixed inputs and randomness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses exact equality under a declared output convention; statistical reproducibility is outside this record.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A parallel scenario-decomposition computation is reproducible relative to \(\mathcal S\) when fixing all declared inputs and randomness makes its recorded output independent of the admissible schedule. Formally, for the execution map \(Y:\mathcal S\to\mathcal Y\), reproducibility means \[\forall s,t\in\mathcal S,\qquad Y(s)=Y(t).\] Equality is interpreted according to the declared convention on \(\mathcal Y\): bitwise equality for bitwise reproducibility, or equality of specified mathematical quantities after a documented canonicalization. Merely obtaining objective values within an unspecified tolerance does not satisfy this exact predicate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With inputs and randomness fixed, every admissible parallel schedule must produce the same recorded output under a declared equality convention.
knowledge_statements.title: Parallel Reproducibility

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is mathematically precise, matches the leaf context, distinguishes exact from statistical reproducibility, and uses properly delimited TeX. However, it has no citation supporting the selected schedule-invariance and declared-equality formulation.

children.title: Execution-Ordering Effects
children.top_down_role: Effects of task completion order, message arrival order, or reduction order on results.

assumptions_latex: Floating-point addition is IEEE 754 binary64 round-to-nearest, ties-to-even, denoted by \(\operatorname{fl}\).
No extended-precision intermediate or fused operation changes the stated additions.
A parallel reduction may evaluate the same three summands using either displayed parenthesization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{fl}(\operatorname{fl}(a+b)+c)=1\neq0=\operatorname{fl}(a+\operatorname{fl}(b+c))\).

notation.meaning: Correctly rounded binary64 result of the indicated operation.
Three reduction terms used in the counterexample.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: nonassociativity of finite-precision addition is the standard mechanism by which reduction order affects parallel numerical results
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete binary64 counterexample for floating-point reduction order; compiler reassociation and extended precision are excluded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(a=10^{16}\), \(b=-10^{16}\), and \(c=1\), all represented in binary64 arithmetic. Correct rounding gives \(\operatorname{fl}(a+b)=0\) and \(\operatorname{fl}(b+c)=b\). Consequently, two legal evaluation orders of the same mathematical sum satisfy \[\operatorname{fl}(\operatorname{fl}(a+b)+c)=1,\qquad \operatorname{fl}(a+\operatorname{fl}(b+c))=0.\] Thus a parallel scenario reduction that changes its reduction tree can change a computed aggregate even though its multiset of scenario contributions is unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two legal floating-point reduction orders can return different aggregates from the same scenario contributions because floating-point addition is not associative.
knowledge_statements.title: Execution-Ordering Effects

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The counterexample is locally appropriate and its content kind correctly captures an execution-ordering phenomenon. The assumptions identify the relevant binary64 execution model, but no inspectable source supports the specific numerical example and rounding claims.

children.title: Schedule-Induced Nondeterminism
children.top_down_role: Result variation attributable to nondeterministic parallel schedules.

assumptions_latex: Let \(\mathcal S\) contain all schedules admitted by the implementation and runtime.
The input instance \(d\), initial state \(z_0\), and random stream \(\omega\) are fixed.
The observable output map is \(Y:\mathcal S\times\mathcal D\times\mathcal Z\times\Omega\to\mathcal Y\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists s,t\in\mathcal S\) such that \(Y(s,d,z_0,\omega)\neq Y(t,d,z_0,\omega)\).

notation.meaning: Fixed input, initial state, and random stream.
Observable output generated under the supplied execution data.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: schedule-induced nondeterminism is characterized by unequal observable outputs for two admissible schedules with all nonscheduling inputs fixed
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identifies schedule dependence after conditioning on inputs and randomness; ordinary Monte Carlo variation is excluded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Schedule-induced nondeterminism occurs for fixed \((d,z_0,\omega)\) precisely when the execution map is not constant over admissible schedules: \[\exists s,t\in\mathcal S:\quad Y(s,d,z_0,\omega)\neq Y(t,d,z_0,\omega).\] The inequality may arise from floating-point reduction order, race-dependent updates, inconsistent reads, or schedule-dependent stopping. If outputs differ only because distinct random streams were assigned, the predicate does not isolate schedule-induced nondeterminism unless that assignment itself is a function of the schedule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nondeterminism is schedule-induced when two admissible schedules yield different observable outputs while the data, initial state, and random stream remain fixed.
knowledge_statements.title: Schedule-Induced Nondeterminism

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary formulation matches schedule-induced nondeterminism and correctly holds data, initial state, and randomness fixed. Its variables and quantifiers are explicit, but no cited source supports this execution-map characterization.

children.title: Order-Robust Computation
children.top_down_role: Computational regimes designed to limit sensitivity to execution ordering.

assumptions_latex: Let \(X\) be the set of scenario contributions and \(Y\) the output space.
For each \(n\geq1\), the computation is a map \(F_n:X^n\to Y\).
The symmetric group \(S_n\) acts on inputs by \((x_1,\ldots,x_n)\mapsto(x_{\pi(1)},\ldots,x_{\pi(n)})\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F_n(x_1,\ldots,x_n)=F_n(x_{\pi(1)},\ldots,x_{\pi(n)})\) for every \(n\geq1\), \(x\in X^n\), and \(\pi\in S_n\).

notation.meaning: Computation applied to an ordered list of n scenario contributions.
Group of permutations of n indices.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: order robustness is naturally formalized as permutation invariance of a computation on scenario contributions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact permutation invariance of scenario aggregation; tolerance-based or distributional robustness requires a separate convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The family \((F_n)_{n\geq1}\) is order-robust when every member is invariant under permutation of its scenario inputs. Equivalently, \[\forall n\geq1,\ \forall (x_1,\ldots,x_n)\in X^n,\ \forall\pi\in S_n:\quad F_n(x_1,\ldots,x_n)=F_n(x_{\pi(1)},\ldots,x_{\pi(n)}).\] This condition concerns input order, not arbitrary data races or schedule-dependent stopping. A parallel implementation inherits exact order robustness only when every schedule-dependent combination realizes the same map \(F_n\) under the declared arithmetic and equality conventions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A scenario computation is order-robust when every permutation of the same contributions produces exactly the same output under the declared arithmetic convention.
knowledge_statements.title: Order-Robust Computation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The permutation-invariance condition is precise, internally consistent, and appropriate for the exact order-robust-computation leaf. No cited source supports this exact scope or the stated connection from schedule-dependent combinations to the family of maps.
